title: BitLocker: Users prompted with the BitLocker recovery screen on every startup.
content: BitLocker: Users prompted with the BitLocker recovery screen on every startup. Important: This was authored via https://aka.ms/contentidea. Follow Content Idea (CI) 197034 link for any updates. Author: Aravindhan A Summary/Symptom User's getting BitLocker recovery screen every time they boot up the machine and hence used recovery password to unlock the OS Drive. Details: ====================================== YYYYMMDD HH:MM:SS: manage-bde -status ====================================== BitLocker Drive Encryption: Configuration Tool version 10.0.19041 Copyright (C) 2013 Microsoft Corporation. All rights reserved. Disk volumes that can be protected with BitLocker Drive Encryption: Volume C: [Windows] [OS Volume] Size: 235.48 GB BitLocker Version: 2.0 Conversion Status: Used Space Only Encrypted Percentage Encrypted: 100.0% Encryption Method: XTS-AES 256 Protection Status: Protection On Lock Status: Unlocked Identification Field: Unknown Key Protectors: Numerical Password ====================================== YYYYMMDD HH:MM:SS: manage-bde -protectors c: -get ====================================== BitLocker Drive Encryption: Configuration Tool version 10.0.19041 Copyright (C) 2013 Microsoft Corporation. All rights reserved. Volume C: [Windows] All Key Protectors Numerical Password: ID: {7FE7**78-**************************} We have only the recovery protector and TPM protector was missing. title: Show the critical path of a plan - Microsoft Support
content: Note: The new Microsoft Planner is currently rolling out to customers. If your experience looks different than the steps listed in this article, or you're working from a Government Cloud Communities (GCC), GCC High, or Department of Defense (DoD) environment, refer to the instructions toward the bottom of this page. ​​​​​​​Learn more about the new Planner in Frequently asked questions about Planner. Every task is important, but only some of them are critical. The critical path is a chain of linked tasks that directly affects the plan finish date. If any task on the critical path is late, the whole plan is late. The critical path is a series of tasks (or sometimes only a single task) that controls the calculated start or finish date of the plan. The tasks that make up the critical path are typically interrelated by task dependencies. There are likely to be many such networks of tasks throughout your plan. When the last task in the critical path is complete, the plan is also complete. Learn more about critical path analysis. In Microsoft Planner, you can view the critical path by using a filter. In your plan, select Timeline Select Filters. ​​​​​​​​​​​​​​ Turn on the toggle Show Critical Path. When Show Critical Path is on, you'll see the critical path for your plan highlighted red in the timeline. ​​​​​​​

title: KB5034229: Compatibility update for installing and recovering Windows Server, version 23H2: January 9, 2024
content: KB5034229: Compatibility update for installing and recovering Windows Server, version 23H2: January 9, 2024 Summary This update makes improvements to the Windows recovery features for Windows Server, version 23H2. How to get this update Install this update Release Channel Available Next Step Windows Update and Microsoft Update Yes This update is available through Windows Update. It will be downloaded and installed automatically. Microsoft Update Catalog Yes To get the standalone package for this update, go to the Microsoft Update Catalog website. To download updates from the Update Catalog, see Steps to download updates from the Windows Update Catalog. Windows Server Update Services (WSUS) and Microsoft Endpoint Configuration Manager Yes This update will be installed as part of the associated Windows monthly security update. Additionally, this update will automatically sync with WSUS if you configure Products and Classifications as follows: Product: Windows 11​​​​​​​ Classification: Security Updates Prerequisites There are no prerequisites to apply this update. Restart information You do not have to restart your device after you apply this update. Removal information This update cannot be removed once it is applied to a Windows image. Update replacement information This update does not replace any previously released update. Verify the installation of this update After installing this update, the WinRE version installed on the device should be 10.0.25398.640​​​​​​​. ​​​​​ Methods to verify the WinRE version installed​​​​​​​​​​​​​​ GetWinReVersion.ps1WinREAgent eventDISM command To get the version of WinRE installed, run the following PowerShell script "GetWinReVersion.ps1" with Administrator credentials. After you run the script, you should receive the installed WinRE version as in the following example: GetWinReVersion.ps1 PowerShell script ################################################################################################ # # Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation. # Licensed under the MIT License. # # THE SOFTWARE IS PROVIDED *AS IS*, WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND, EXPRESS OR # IMPLIED, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO THE WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, # FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE AND NONINFRINGEMENT. IN NO EVENT SHALL THE # AUTHORS OR COPYRIGHT HOLDERS BE LIABLE FOR ANY CLAIM, DAMAGES OR OTHER # LIABILITY, WHETHER IN AN ACTION OF CONTRACT, TORT OR OTHERWISE, ARISING FROM, # OUT OF OR IN CONNECTION WITH THE SOFTWARE OR THE USE OR OTHER DEALINGS IN THE # SOFTWARE. # ################################################################################################ # Function to get WinRE path function GetWinREPath { $WinRELocation = (reagentc /info | Select-String "Windows RE location") if ($WinRELocation) { return $WinRELocation.ToString().Split(':')[-1].Trim() } else { Write-Host "Failed to find WinRE path" -ForegroundColor Red exit 1 } } # Creates and needs to be return the mount directory function GetMountDir { # systemdirve\mnt $MountDir = "$env:SystemDrive\mnt" if (-not (Test-Path $MountDir)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $MountDir -Force | Out-Null } return $MountDir } # Function to get WinRE version function GetWinREVersion { $mountedPath = GetMountDir $filePath = "$mountedPath\Windows\System32\winpeshl.exe" $WinREVersion = (Get-Item $filePath).VersionInfo.FileVersionRaw.Revision return [int]$WinREVersion } # Main Execution $WinREPath = GetWinREPath # Make dir C:\mnt if not exists $TempDir = GetMountDir # Get the read write permission for this directory if (-not (Test-Path $TempDir)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $TempDir -Force | Out-Null } # Mount WinRE image dism /Mount-Image /ImageFile:"$WinREPath\winre.wim" /Index:1 /MountDir:"$TempDir" $WinREVersion = GetWinREVersion Write-Host "WinRE Version: $WinREVersion" -ForegroundColor Cyan dism /Unmount-Image /MountDir:"$TempDir" /Discard Remove-Item -Path $TempDir -Force -Recurse WinREAgent logs events related to the Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE), primarily recording details about the creation, modification, and usage of the recovery image. In this case, we are looking for Event ID: 4501 Servicing succeeded events. If you are unsuccessful in locating WinREAgent servicing events because of space limitations that might occur in your environment, we suggest you use the DISM command. Open the Windows Search bar. To do this, right-click Start and then click Search. In the Search bar, type Event Viewer and then click Event Viewer. Expand Windows Logs and then click System. In the right-side navigation pane, under Actions, click Find. In the Find what: box, type WinREAgent and then click Find Next. Click Cancel to close the Find dialog box. The WinREAgent servicing event should be shown in the bottom middle pane and you should see a message similar to the followng on the General tab: Servicing succeeded. The Windows Recovery Environment version is now: 10.0.22621.4742 The WinRE version in this example is 10.0.22621.4742. ​​​​​​​To view the Event Properties pane for the WinREAgent servicing event, right-click the WinREAgent entry in the System pane (top middle pane) and then click Event Properties. ​​​​​​​ Open an elevated Windows command prompt. To do this, press the Windows key, type cmd, right-click Command Prompt, and then click Run as Administrator. At the command prompt, type reagentc /info and then press Enter. Note the path of the Windows RE location. For this example, the location is \\?\GLOBALROOT\device\harddisk0\partition5\Recovery\WindowsRE. This path may vary based on your Windows installation. At the command prompt, use the DISM command to retrieve the Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE) information. For this example, enter the following command and then press Enter: Dism /Get-ImageInfo /ImageFile:\\?\GLOBALROOT\device\harddisk0\partition5\Recovery\WindowsRE\winre.wim /index:1 Note The default name for the WinRE image file is winre.wim. In your environment, the name of the WinRE image file might be different. Also, the Index number of the default winre.wim file is 1. In your environment, the Index number might be different. The WinRE image file information is returned as illustrated in the following example: The WinRE version in this example is 10.0.22621.4742. In the right-side navigation pane, under Actions, click Find. In the Find what: box, type WinREAgent and then click Find Next. Click Cancel to close the Find dialog box. The WinREAgent servicing event should be shown in the bottom middle pane and you should see a message similar to the followng on the General tab: Servicing succeeded. The Windows Recovery Environment version is now: 10.0.22621.4742 The WinRE version in this example is 10.0.22621.4742. ​​​​​​​To view the Event Properties pane for the WinREAgent servicing event, right-click the WinREAgent entry in the System pane (top middle pane) and then click Event Properties. ​​​​​​​ Open an elevated Windows command prompt. To do this, press the Windows key, type cmd, right-click Command Prompt, and then click Run as Administrator. At the command prompt, type reagentc /info and then press Enter. Note the path of the Windows RE location. For this example, the location is \\?\GLOBALROOT\device\harddisk0\partition5\Recovery\WindowsRE. This path may vary based on your Windows installation. At the command prompt, use the DISM command to retrieve the Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE) information. For this example, enter the following command and then press Enter: Dism /Get-ImageInfo /ImageFile:\\?\GLOBALROOT\device\harddisk0\partition5\Recovery\WindowsRE\winre.wim /index:1 Note The default name for the WinRE image file is winre.wim. In your environment, the name of the WinRE image file might be different. Also, the Index number of the default winre.wim file is 1. In your environment, the Index number might be different. content: Applies To.NET Release Date:November 21, 2024 Version: .NET Framework 3.5 and 4.8 The November 21, 2024 update for Windows 10 Version 22H2 includes security and cumulative reliability improvements in .NET Framework 3.5 and 4.8. We recommend that you apply this update as part of your regular maintenance routines. Before you install this update, see the Prerequisites and Restart requirement sections. description: Whenever your access is challenged, Teams will show you a sign-in banner and request that you Sign in to re-authenticate and regain access.
title: Restore your access to Microsoft Teams - Microsoft Support
content: Whenever your access to Teams is challenged, you may see a sign-in banner requesting that you Sign in to re-authenticate and regain access. ​​​​​​​ If Teams asks you to sign in again, you won't be able to chat, call or join meetings until you do. Follow the steps below to restore access. Fix the problem Select the Sign in banner or button. In the window that opens, enter your sign-in info and complete any prompts, such as multi-factor authentication (MFA). If you don't see the sign in button, check the notification area on the taskbar (near the clock). Look for the Teams icon with a badge - for example, a dot or exclamation mark. Select the Teams icon to open the sign-in window. If the sign-in window still doesn't open, quit and reopen Teams. In the notification area, select the Teams icon, and then select Quit. Open teams again. After you sign in, the banner should disappear, and you should be able to use Teams normally. If you see the banner again, repeat the steps above or contact your IT administrator for assistance. Help prevent the issue Connect to the network your organization requires before you open Teams. For example, if your organization requires a VPN, connect to the VPN first. Try to avoid switching between different networks while Teams is open. For example, if you are using a laptop, don't disconnect from your office Wi-Fi and connect to a public Wi-Fi without signing out of Teams first. Keep Teams up to date. In Teams, select your profile picture, then select Check for updates (if available). Why this happens Teams may ask you to sign in again for security reasons. For example: Your organization requires a specific network (for example, a VPN), and you are not connected. Your organization detects a sign-in risk and asks you to verify your identity (for example, with your phone). A password breach has occurred, and your organization requires you to change your password right away. Your device does not meet your organization’s requirements, so you must verify your identity before you can continue. Related topics: I can't reconnect to Teams

title: Cannot set role priority for SQL role SQL "Failed to execute control code '54526046'
content: Cannot set role priority for SQL role SQL "Failed to execute control code '54526046' Important: This was authored via https://aka.ms/contentidea. Follow Content Idea (CI) 198058 link for any updates. Author: Badal Pundir Summary/Symptom While trying to set role priority for SQL role in failover cluster manager you are getting error. "Failed to execute control code '54526046' Cause (Misconfiguration of witness disk.) It was that one of the core resources (Witness Disk) is part of the SQL Role, whereas it should be part of Core Group. Article resolution 1, Check if witness resource is aligned in the Core Group or not. 2, If not, you may use "Move-ClusterResource -Name resource1 -Group "group name" ". It will allow you to move the Witness resource to cluster core group. 3, Afterwards we should be able to change the priority of the SQL role.

title: Dynamic list filtering - Microsoft Support
content: Applies ToSharePoint in Microsoft 365 With dynamic filtering, you can filter one list based on a selection made in another list. In the following example, the Marketing Documents library is filtered by a selection in the Project Information list. The "Marketing" value in the Project Team column is selected, so only documents owned by the Marketing team are displayed in the Marketing Documents library. To do this: On your page, select Edit and add a List web part or a Document library web part then select the list or library with the values you want to filter by. Add another List web part or a Document library web part and select the list or library that contains the information you want to filter. Select the list or library web part you want to filter and select Edit properties in the upper-left of the web part. Under Dynamic filtering, slide the toggle to the On position. Select the column you want to filter in the field Column in [your list name] to filter. Under List or library containing filter value, select the list or library you added to your page in Step 1. Under Column containing the filter value's properties, select the column that has the values you want to filter by. Select Apply. Using the example image at the beginning of section, the Dynamic filtering options for the Marketing Documents library would look like the following: When you're done, click Save and close at the top of the page, or if you're ready for your audience to see the page, select Republish at the top right of the page.

title: Windows Server 2016: Bugcheck 0x9F due to CPU busy trimming the working set of RStudio process rsession-utf8.exe
content: Windows Server 2016: Bugcheck 0x9F due to CPU busy trimming the working set of RStudio process rsession-utf8.exe Important: This was authored via https://aka.ms/contentidea. Follow Content Idea (CI) 197545 link for any updates. Author: Khalid Sabri Summary/Symptom Reported on Windows Server 2016 Reported symptoms System crashes with bugcheck DRIVER_POWER_STATE_FAILURE, hexadecimal value 9F. But the issue can be manifested in other ways such as high CPU, system hang or slowness or other bugcheck codes Cause The memory dump shows the system is locked up with many threads from various processes waiting for long time on various types of locks. Following the wait chains lead to the thread running on CPU#0, which has been running for long time at high priority trimming the working set for an instance of the process rsession-utf8.exe. A process working set is the process memory pages that are resident in the physical memory. This rsession-utf8.exe process instance has massive memory usage of 30GB+ of physical memory when it had run for a total time of only ~3hrs. Furthermore, there are multiple instances of the rsession-utf8.exe with high memory usage, one of them alone using ~110GB of memory. rsession-utf8.exe is launched by rstudio.exe, which is part of RStudio Desktop, an integrated development environment (IDE) with a set of tools built to help develop apps using the R and Python languages. RStudio is owned by Posit Software. The system lockup caused one of the power requests (to power on COM2 serial port) to block hence triggering the power manager kernel component watchdog timeout mechanism (10min) to crash the system with bugcheck DRIVER_POWER_STATE_FAILURE (9F). This is just a symptom of the system lockup for long period of time. Article resolution Follow up with the vendor for RStudio to investigate the high memory usage. title: Windows: App: Phone Link and Mobile Device UI is unavailable (greyed-out) due to policy on ALL Windows OS versions
content: Windows: App: Phone Link and Mobile Device UI is unavailable (greyed-out) due to policy on ALL Windows OS versions Important: This was authored via https://aka.ms/contentidea. Follow Content Idea (CI) 197160 link for any updates. Author: Jonah Atkins Summary/Symptom Abstract No Phone Linked policies are being configured. Settings -> Bluetooth & devices -> Mobile Devices is greyed-out. The Phone Linked/Mobile Device UI is showing " Some of these settings are managed by your organization." Cause There are other policies that also cause the UI to be greyed out, here are two uncommon ones that have been causing customers issues. Since Phone Link app uses Microsoft accounts for signing in, certain policies that affect Microsoft accounts can cause the UI to grey out. #Computer Configuration > Windows Settings > Security Settings > Local Polices > Security Options "Accounts: Block Microsoft Accounts" RegKey: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System Dword: NoConnectedUser Value: (any value other than 0) #Computer Configuration -> Administrative Templates -> Windows Components -> Cloud Content "Turn off Microsoft consumer experiences." HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\CloudContent Dword: DisableWindowsConsumerFeatures Value: 1 Note: Other policies that affect the ability to install app updates can also have impact on the UI being greyed-out. Article resolution Remove the policies/regkeys , perform a 'gpupdate /force' and the UI should no longer show it's controlled by policy after re-opening More information Here is a script you can run to check different locations in the registry where that UI would be affected. # Define the registry keys and values to check$regKeys = @( @{ Path = "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System"; Name = "NoConnectedUser"; PolicyPath = "#Computer Configuration > Windows Settings > Security Settings > Local Polices > Security Options `nAccounts: Block Microsoft Accounts the value was set to Users can't add or log on with Microsoft Accounts" }, @{ Path = "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\System"; Name = "EnableMmx"; PolicyPath = "#Configuration > Administrative Templates > System > Group Policy Phone-PC linking on this device (disabled)" }, @{ Path = "HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\CloudContent"; Name = "DisableWindowsConsumerFeatures"; PolicyPath = "#Computer Configuration -> Administrative Templates -> Windows Components -> Cloud Content `nTurn off Microsoft consumer experiences." }, @{ Path = "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\WindowsStore"; Name = "RemoveWindowsStore"; PolicyPath = "#Computer Configuration -> Administrative Templates -> Windows Components -> Store `nTurn off the store application" }, @{ Path = "HKCU:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\WindowsStore"; Name = "RemoveWindowsStore"; PolicyPath = "#User Configuration -> Administrative Templates -> Windows Components -> Store `nTurn off the store application" })# Initialize an array to hold output lines$outputLines = @()# Check each registry key and valueforeach ($regKey in $regKeys) { $keyExists = Test-Path -Path $regKey.Path $valueExists = Get-ItemProperty -Path $regKey.Path -Name $regKey.Name -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue if ($keyExists -and $valueExists) { # Add the found key and its policy path to output lines $outputLines += "**$($regKey.Path)** Dword: $($regKey.Name)" $outputLines += "$($regKey.PolicyPath)" $outputLines += "" # Add an empty line for spacing }}# Write output lines to a text file in C:\$outputFilePath = "C:\RegistryCheckResults.txt"$outputLines | Out-File -FilePath $outputFilePathWrite-Output "`nResults written to: C:\RegistryCheckResults.txt" Notes: Support Topics: Windows\Windows 10, Windows\Windows 11 First published: Nov 13, 2024 Keywords: Phone Linked, Policy, Mobile Devices, winx

title: July 9, 2024—KB5040438 (OS Build 25398.1009)
content: <div> July 9, 2024—KB5040438 (OS Build 25398.1009) For information about Windows update terminology, see the article about the types of Windows updates and the monthly quality update types. For an overview of Windows Server, version 23H2, see its update history page. Improvements This security update includes quality improvements. Below is a summary of the key issues that this update addresses when you install this KB. If there are new features, it lists them as well. The bold text within the brackets indicates the item or area of the change we are documenting. [Absent apps and features] Some apps and features are absent after you upgrade to Windows 11. [BCryptSignHash API (known issue)] Because of this issue, the API returns “STATUS_INVALID_PARAMETER.” This occurs when callers use NULL padding input parameters for RSA signatures. This issue is more likely to occur when Customer-Managed Key (CMK) are in use, like on an Azure Synapse dedicated SQL pool. [Input Method Editor (IME)] The candidate list fails to show or shows in the wrong position. [Windows Presentation Foundation (WPF)] A malformed Human Interface Device (HID) descriptor causes WPF to stop responding. [Handwriting panels and touch keyboards] They do not appear when you use the tablet pen. [HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\DWM ForceDisableModeChangeAnimation (REG_DWORD)] This is a new registry key. When you set its value to 1 (or a non-zero number), it turns off the display mode change animation. If the value is 0 or the key does not exist, the animation is set to on. [Remote Desktop MultiPoint Server] A race condition causes the service to stop responding. [Windows Local Administrator Password Solution (LAPS)] Its Post Authentication Actions (PAA) do not occur at the end of the grace period. Instead, they occur at restart. [Remote Authentication Dial-In User Service (RADIUS) protocol] This issue is related to MD5 collisions. For more information, see KB5040268. [BitLocker] This update adds PCR 4 to PCR 7 and 11 for the default Secure Boot validation profile. See CVE-2024-38058 for more information. This update changes how IT administrators should set up remote paths for file shortcut icons (.LNK files). The set up now requires that you configure the policy “Allow the use of remote paths in file shortcut icons”. If you don’t configure this policy, icons on the Start menu, Windows desktop and taskbar will fail to render after you install this update or subsequent updates. For more information about security vulnerabilities, please refer to the Security Update Guide and the July 2024 Security Updates. Windows Server, version 23H2 servicing stack update (KB5040560) - 25398.1000 This update makes quality improvements to the servicing stack, which is the component that installs Windows updates. Servicing stack updates (SSU) ensure that you have a robust and reliable servicing stack so that your devices can receive and install Microsoft updates. Known issues in this update Symptom Workaround After installing the July 9, 2024, Windows security update, you might see a BitLocker recovery screen upon starting up your device. This screen does not commonly appear after a Windows update. You are more likely to face this issue if you have the Device Encryption option enabled in Settings under Privacy & Security > Device encryption. Because of this issue, you might be prompted to enter the recovery key from your Microsoft account to unlock your drive This issue is addressed in KB5041573. How to get this update Before you install this update Microsoft now combines the latest servicing stack update (SSU) for your operating system with the latest cumulative update (LCU). For general information about SSUs, see Servicing stack updates and Servicing Stack Updates (SSU): Frequently Asked Questions. Install this update To install this update, use one of the following Windows and Microsoft release channels. Windows UpdateBusinessCatalogServer Update Services Available Next Step Yes None. This update will be downloaded and installed automatically from Windows Update and Microsoft Update. Available Next Step Yes None. This update will be downloaded and installed automatically from Windows Update for Business in accordance with configured policies. Available Next Step Yes To get the standalone package for this update, go to the Microsoft Update Catalog website. Available Next Step Yes This update will automatically sync with Windows Server Update Services (WSUS) if you configure Products and Classifications as follows: Product: Microsoft Server operating system-21H2 Classification: Security Updates If you want to remove the LCU To remove the LCU after installing the combined SSU and LCU package, use the DISM/Remove-Package command line option with the LCU package name as the argument. You can find the package name by using this command: DISM /online /get-packages. Running Windows Update Standalone Installer (wusa.exe) with the /uninstall switch on the combined package will not work because the combined package contains the SSU. You cannot remove the SSU from the system after installation. File Information For a list of the files that are provided in this update, download the file information for cumulative update 5040438. For a list of the files that are provided in the servicing stack update, download the file information for the SSU (KB5040560) - version 25398.1000. title: Procedure: Unsupported devices for hosting Windows Server 2022
content: Procedure: Unsupported devices for hosting Windows Server 2022 Important: This was authored via https://aka.ms/Rubik. Follow Rubik 429 link for any updates. Author: v-yinghuang@microsoft.com This article provides a list of devices that are not supported for hosting Windows Server 2022 as of February 2023. It aims to help you determine if your device is eligible for firmware updates or if it can host Windows Server 2022. The following devices are not supported for hosting Windows Server 2022 and are not eligible for firmware updates: Dell PowerEdge R630 Dell PowerEdge R930 Server Dell PowerEdge T430 HP EliteDesk 800 G2 Mini HPE DL20 Gen9 HPE DL580 Gen9 HPE ProLiant XL420 Gen9 Intel NUC NUC6i7KYK (desktop client system) Lenovo M93p Tiny Other legacy devices Ensure that your hardware is compatible with the requirements of Windows Server 2022 before attempting installation. If your device is listed above, consider upgrading to a supported model to ensure compatibility and receive necessary firmware updates. Have feedback about this article? – Provide feedback in the survey link at the bottom of this article. If you want to make a change to this article, be sure to access aka.ms/contentidea, and then create an AECT item here and follow the change instructions. Notes: First published: Dec 16, 2024 Keywords: ktest1, ktest2, ktest3 Tags: 429 Support Topics: Windows Servers\Windows Server 2022\Windows Server 2022 Standard (Preview)

title: Error while creating a Remote Perfmon dataset
content: Error while creating a Remote Perfmon dataset Important: This was authored via https://aka.ms/contentidea. Follow Content Idea (CI) 198353 link for any updates. Author: Abdul Qadir Khambati Summary/Symptom When a user tries to create a Remote Perfmon data set they get the following error: "Remote Perfmon gives the following error: ""when attempting to create the data collector set the following system error occurred, A specified logon session does not exist, it may already have been terminated". Cause The following Security policy is enabled on the system: “Network access: Do not allow storage of passwords and credentials for network authentication” Article resolution Disable the following security policy: “Network access: Do not allow storage of passwords and credentials for network authentication”

title: Windows: Pop-up message "Unknown Hard Error" after logon due to corrupt user profile
content: Windows: Pop-up message "Unknown Hard Error" after logon due to corrupt user profile Important: This was authored via https://aka.ms/contentidea. Follow Content Idea (CI) 198618 link for any updates. Author: Manish Singh Summary/Symptom UNKNOWN HARD ERROR pop up after logging in. We click on OK and nothing happens. cx is completely unable to do anything on the machine. Cause User Profile corruption Article resolution Modified below registry and it stopped the UNKNOWN HARD ERROR pop up. 1. Run Registry Editor. 2. From the HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE subtree, go to the following key: \SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Windows Value: ErrorMode Type: REG_DWORD Default: 0 3. Change it to 2. 4. Reboot the machine. Additionally, found that local admin was working fine. Recreated the user profile and it resolved the issue. Note: First published: Jan 06, 2025

title: Windows: Host Activity Manager (HAM) overview
content: Windows: Host Activity Manager (HAM) overview Important: This was authored via https://aka.ms/contentidea. Follow Content Idea (CI) 195772 link for any updates. Author: Jason Epperly Summary/Symptom Host Activity Manager (HAM) is the component responsible for tracking packaged applications ‘activities’ that they need to perform and ensuring that any other required applications are in the resumed state when attempts are made to perform these activities. Resources 5.1 Example of previous cases 1. Prerequisites Return to top 2. Scenario/Problem statement Starting June 19, 2023, use this table https://aka.ms/MCIBIEIneligibleReasons to help partners understand the reason text that appears to them for each ineligible engagement they see in the Associate Engagement step of adding/claiming customers. The reasons are ranked. If multiple ineligible reasons apply, partner will only see the reason text with the highest rank. Both Partner location ID and customer ID appear to be eligible for desired engagement per the relevant BI reports linked in https://aka.ms/MCIBIEPowerBIReportsLibrary but partner cannot create new claim for customer. OR Both Partner location ID and customer ID appear to be eligible in MCI Eligibility Report for desired engagement. Partner has already created claim but when customer tries to use emailed link to give consent, they get below error message in browser window: Once customer gives consent to one partner on an engagement, any other partners will not be able to get consent for that same engagement from that customer unless the consented claim is cancelled, expired, or rejected unless the engagement allows customers to receive multiple deliveries. You can confirm whether an engagement allows the same customer to be associated to more than 1 active/approved claim by checking the "Max claims allowed per customer" column in https://aka.ms/MCIEngagementsIDMasterList. In this example shown in screenshot, AIM Assessment - Fixed Fee only allows 1 active/approved claim per customer ID, whereas AMM PL for ISV SAP RISE (L) has no limit on how many active/approved claims are allowed per customer. If the "Max claims allowed per customer" limit shown in https://aka.ms/MCIEngagementsIDMasterList has been hit, do not share details of claims from one partner to another - only advise that the customer already gave consent and that we cannot divulge specifics per Microsoft's confidentiality agreement with each partner and customer. Return to top 3. Investigation Search in Partner Center (microsoft.com) and WorkshopClaimsAndPayments - Power BI report for customer ID and engagement name to look for active or completed claims that would prevent new claims from being made for that customer ID + engagement. An engagement claim is considered Active or Completed if it is in any of the following states: Draft/Customer Consent Received Submitted Under Review Partner Action Required Approved Disputed Rejected (if rejection occurred less than 30 days ago) If you cannot find matching engagement using same engagement name, use Engagement ID to name mapping table here https://aka.ms/MCIEngagementsIDMasterList to determine whether customer already has an active or complete claim for matching engagement under a different name. If you cannot find any active or completed engagement that would prevent new claims from being made for this engagement + customer ID, return to #39691274 and proceed through the remaining steps in that scenario. If customer ID already has an active or completed engagement and the "Max claims allowed per customer" limit shown in https://aka.ms/MCIEngagementsIDMasterList has been hit, respond as follows:Response for partner/requester: In addition to the qualifications specified for each individual MCI engagement, customers who were already nominated for an active or completed [ENGAGEMENT NAME] engagement will be ineligible to receive that engagement again in MCI. Customer ID [ID] is not currently eligible to [claim / to give consent] to a claim for [ENGAGEMENT NAME] because they already have given consent on an active or completed claim for this engagement with another partner. This customer will not be eligible to [be claimed / give consent] for this engagement to any other partner unless the current active claim is expired, rejected, or cancelled. Return to top 4. Resolution Return to top 5. title: Errors:1783 ('The Stub Received Bad Data') and 0x8007042c, When Launching Services and Firewall Console in Windows Servers
content: Errors:1783 ('The Stub Received Bad Data') and 0x8007042c, When Launching Services and Firewall Console in Windows Servers Important: This was authored via https://aka.ms/contentidea. Follow Content Idea (CI) 196935 link for any updates. Author: Saisrinivas Chikoti Summary/Symptom The customer followed these steps, based on the external article, to enable multiple remote desktop sessions per user: Terminal Services installation guide (tricentis.com) In the Registry Editor go to HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\System\CurrentControlSet\Control\TerminalServer. On selecting the TerminalServices Registry, you can see the fSingleSessionPerUser registry key on the right panel. If the key is not available, then create a new key by right clicking Terminal Services and selecting New > DWORD. Double click the fSingleSessionPerUser key. Change the value from "1" to "0". The value "1" means single session for each user and "0" means multiple sessions for each user. The system is a Windows Server 2016 with the Application role, hosted on VMware. After rebooting following the changes above, issues arose with the services console, MMC, firewall console, and RDP connections, Etc. The errors displayed include: "Error 1783: The Stub received bad data" and "Windows Defender Firewall can't change some of your settings. Error code 0x8007042c. Additionally, access to the machine is limited to the VMware console with a local admin account, and attempting to launch the MMC triggers the same error: "The Stub received bad data." It shows the below errors --> While launching the services console The Error code of firewall console pointing to 0x42c 1068 ERROR_SERVICE_DEPENDENCY_FAIL ( winerror.h ) Cause The error message “Error 1783: The stub received bad data” typically occurs when there is an issue with the Services Management Console (Services.msc) on Windows Server. This error can happen when the number of services installed exceeds the size limit of the Services.msc buffer, which is limited to 256 kb of data. It was documented in public as well: Error 1783 when you open Services.msc - Windows Server | Microsoft Learn which is by design. It was confirmed that there is no registry bloat present. The customer is using a third-party application called "Tricentis NeoLoad", which can remotely initiate multiple Windows sessions as needed on each Windows Server utilized as a Load Generator. Each Windows session automatically starts a Load Generator process, which is then added to the list of available Load Generators for the zone. Additionally, each Load Generator creates a registry key under the path "HKLM\CurrentControlSet\Services\PAExec-12212-***********" on each Windows instance using a service account, leading to service bloat as described in the referenced article above. Article resolution suggested the customer remove the registry keys (PAExec*) under the path "HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services" after backing up the existing registry hives. The customer consulted the vendor, who confirmed that it was safe to delete these keys. The customer used the custom script below to delete the keys after backing up the existing hives. Following a reboot, the machine functioned as expected. It was recommended that the customer consult the vendor for further investigation. ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++ $registryPath = "HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services" $pattern = "PAExec*" # Get all registry keys matching the pattern and delete them Get-ChildItem -Path $registryPath | Where-Object { $_.PSChildName -like $pattern } | ForEach-Object { Remove-Item -Path $_.PSPath -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue } ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++ Reference images show multiple services present on the customer’s machine, with over 1,000 registry keys. Note: Please note that this action was not recommended by Microsoft, it was carried out as a last resort after obtaining customer consent and ensuring a backup was taken as best effort More information Error 1783 when you open Services.msc - Windows Server | Microsoft Learn Notes: Support Topics: Windows Servers\Windows Server 2016\Windows Server 2016, all editions (Preview)\System Performance (Preview) First published: Oct 28, 2024 Keywords: 1783, Services bloat, 0x8007042c, The Stub Received Bad Data

title: Windows 11: Some Apps missing icon in search results, but retain icons in Start Menu after upgrade
content: Windows 11: Some Apps missing icon in search results, but retain icons in Start Menu after upgrade Important: This was authored via https://aka.ms/contentidea. Follow Content Idea (CI) 197019 link for any updates. Author: Mansi Sharma Summary/Symptom Icons of applications like Edge and other apps like Chrome browser tool lose its image in Search results, but retain it Start Menu and taskbar. Icons are clickable No profile management in use. Issue observed only with User accounts and not with admin accounts so far. Issue happened after in-place upgrade from Windows 10 to Windows 11 The issue was only temporary, and would appear after first logon post reboot, and then would disappear eventually only to come back after few reboots. Article resolution Please start by making below policy as default on the test machine (after removing it from the OU for the domain policy): Bypass Traverse Checking: Expected entries: Default Members : Administrators , Backup Operators, Everyone , Local Service, Network Service, Users impacted device: Administrators, Local Service, Network Service, Users Please add- Backup Operators, Everyone to Bypass Traverse Checking entry under: Policy :Computer Configuration\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignments\ Gpupdate /force Try to repro the issue by uninstalling and installing back Microsoft.MicrosoftEdge.Stable_124.0.2478.51_neutral__8wekyb3d8bbwe If this works, then this will be fix. If it wont, please proceed with next step: In the same path, below policy is also not set as default: Logon as a Batch Job: Expected entries: Default Members : Administrators , Backup Operators, Performance Log Users impacted device only as Administrators Please add- Backup Operators, Performance Log Users Gpupdate /force Try to repro the issue by uninstalling and installing back Microsoft.MicrosoftEdge.Stable_124.0.2478.51_neutral__8wekyb3d8bbwe If this works, then this will be fix. If it wont, please proceed with next step: In the same path, please disable this and remove all users from the list: Notes: Support Topics: Windows\Windows 11\Windows 11 Home and Pro, version 24H2\Windows Desktop and Shell Experience\Windows Search First published: Oct 30, 2024 Keywords: winx, upgrade, ipu, badupgrade,

title: VBS: Microsoft Windows Secure Kernel Mode and Update Stack Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability (CVE-2024-21302) still being reported as vulnerable
content: VBS: Microsoft Windows Secure Kernel Mode and Update Stack Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability (CVE-2024-21302) still being reported as vulnerable Important: This was authored via https://aka.ms/contentidea. Follow Content Idea (CI) 196240 link for any updates. Author: Paul Haustein Summary/Symptom Qualys vulnerability report showed that the servers were requiring remediation from CVE-2024-21302 Understanding the New Windows Secure Kernel Mode Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability (CVE-2024-21302) | Qualys Security Blog Attempts to apply the remediation plan from KB5042562 had failed because the mountvol process would not mount the EFI volume. KB5042562: Guidance for blocking rollback of Virtualization-based Security (VBS) related security updates - Microsoft Support Cause The customer has enabled VBS Security on the servers that have the BIOS Mode of Legacy. The enablement of the VBS Security settings are only applicable to servers with the BIOS Type of UEFI. Enable memory integrity | Microsoft Learn Article resolution Removed the VBS Security policy from the servers by setting the policy to Not Configured or Disabled Enable memory integrity | Microsoft Learn Notes: Support Topics: Windows Servers\Windows Server 2016\Windows Server 2016\Microsoft Common Vulnerabilities and Exposure (Retired)\Microsoft Common Vulnerabilities and Exposure Questions (Retired), Windows Servers\Windows Server 2019\Windows Server 2019\Microsoft Common Vulnerabilities and Exposure (Retired)\Microsoft Common Vulnerabilities and Exposure Questions (Retired) First published: Nov 01, 2024 Keywords: Legacy BIOS, VBS, CVE-2024-21302

title: November 12, 2024—KB5046665 (OS Build 10240.20826) - EXPIRED - Microsoft Support
content: Applies ToWindows 10 EXPIRATION NOTICE IMPORTANT As of January 27, 2026, this update is no longer available from the Microsoft Update Catalog or other release channels. We recommend that you update your devices to the latest version of Windows. 12/8/20 For information about Windows update terminology, see the article about the types of Windows updates and the monthly quality update types. For an overview of Windows 10, version 1507, see its update history page. Important: Windows updates do not install Microsoft Store application updates. If you are an enterprise user, see Microsoft Store apps - Configuration Manager. If you are a consumer user, see Get updates for apps and games in Microsoft Store. Highlights This update addresses security issues for your Windows operating system. Improvements This security update includes quality improvements. Below is a summary of the key issues that this update addresses when you install this KB. If there are new features, it lists them as well. The bold text within the brackets indicates the item or area of the change we are documenting. [vmswitch] Fixed: A vmswitch triggers a stop error. This occurs when you use Load Balancing and Failover (LBFO) teaming with two virtual switches on a virtual machine (VM). In this case, one virtual switch uses single root Input/Output virtualization (SR-IOV). ​​​​​​​ If you installed earlier updates, only the new updates contained in this package will be downloaded and installed on your device. For more information about security vulnerabilities, please refer to the new Security Update Guide website and the November 2024 Security Updates. Known issues in this update Microsoft is not currently aware of any issues with this update.​​​​​​​ How to get this update EXPIRATION NOTICE IMPORTANT As of January 27, 2026, this update is no longer available from the Microsoft Update Catalog or other release channels. We recommend that you update your devices to the latest version of Windows.

title: ADDS: PKI: Certificate Revocation Fails for LDAP locations for Standalone or Clustered CAs After Renewing CA with New Key
content: ADDS: PKI: Certificate Revocation Fails for LDAP locations for Standalone or Clustered CAs After Renewing CA with New Key Important: This was authored via https://aka.ms/contentidea. Follow Content Idea (CI) 195706 link for any updates. Author: Chris Cartwright (CSS DS) Summary/Symptom Abstract Customers may experience revocation failures on Standalone or Clustered CAs after renewing with a new private key. This should only apply to LDAP locations. HTTP locations are either updated manually or automatically and should not run into this problem. Symptoms PKIView displays the error "Unable to download" Revocation failures in environment for new certificates post CA renewal. Running certutil -verify -urlfetch against a cert (If publish was done incorrectly) fails with "Wrong Issuer" Cause When a CA is enrolled with a new private key, the index value increases. Enterprise, non-clustered CAs take care of this automatically. Standalone (Non domain joined) and Clustered CAs do not. Standalone CAs that aren't domain joined won't be able to update LDAP locations. Clustered CAs won't be able to update LDAP locations because the renewal isn't done from the cluster resource. It is done from an individual node. This means that certutil -dspublish must be used. However, documentation on how to leverage certutil is suboptimal, to say the least. There is a barely noted option for DSCDPCN, that mentions "DSCDPCN is the DS CDP object CN based on the sanitized CA short name and key index." This is not even covered on pkisolutions.com or sysadmins.lv, where we usually go to get better quality documentation. Article resolution Modify the certutil command to include the index. This index will be found in C:\Windows\System32\CertSrv\CertEnroll. It will be the number in parenthesis at the end of the filename. Format: certutil [options] -dspublish CRLfile [DSCDPContainer [DSCDPCN]] Example for Offline Root Contoso-Root-CA running on computer ContOffRoot: certutil -f -dspublish C:\Windows\System32\CertSrv\CertEnroll\Contoso-Root-CA(2).crl RootCA ContOffRoot(2) Example for clustered enterprise clustered subordinate CA Adatum-Issuing-CA running on cluster resource AdaSubCA: certutil -f -dspublish C:\Windows\System32\CertSrv\CertEnroll\Adatum-Issuing-CA(1).crl SubCA AdaSubCA(1) More information Author chcart@microsoft.com Notes: Support Topics: Windows Servers\Windows title: September 10, 2024—KB5043125 (Monthly Rollup)
content: September 10, 2024—KB5043125 (Monthly Rollup) Important The installation of this Extended Security Update (ESU) might fail when you try to install it on an Azure Arc-enabled device that is running Windows Server 2012. For a successful installation, please make sure all Subset of endpoints for ESU only are met as described in Connected Machine agent network requirements. End of support information Windows Server 2012 reached the end of support (EOS) on October 10, 2023. Extended Security Updates (ESUs) are available for purchase and will continue for three years, renewable on an annual basis, until the final date on October 13, 2026. For more information, see Windows Server End of Support: Key Dates. For information about the procedure to continue receiving security updates, see Procedure to continue receiving security updates after extended support has ended on October 10, 2023. For more information about the ESU program, see Learn about the ESU program. We recommend that you upgrade to a later version of Windows Server. For more information, see Overview of Windows Server upgrades. Windows Embedded 8 Standard reached the end of support (EOS) on July 11, 2023. Therefore, technical assistance and software updates are no longer provided. Change log Change date Change description October 8, 2024 Added the fix for the Remote Procedure Call over HTTP known issue. September 20, 2024 Added the resolution for the Windows/Linux start up known issue. Summary Learn more about this cumulative security update, including improvements, any known issues, and how to get the update. Note Verify that you have installed the required updates listed in the How to get this update section before installing this update. For information about the various types of Windows updates, such as critical, security, driver, service packs, and so on, please see the following Description of the standard terminology that is used to describe Microsoft software updates. To view other notes and messages, see the Windows Server 2012 update history home page. Improvements This cumulative security update contains improvements that are part of update KB5041851 (released August 13, 2024). The following is a summary of the key issues that this update addresses. The bold text within the brackets indicates the item or area of the change we are documenting. [User Account Control (UAC)] When the Windows Installer repairs an application, the UAC does not prompt for your credentials. After you install this update, it will prompt for them. Because of this, you might have to update your automation scripts. Additionally, you should add the Shield icon to indicate that your automation scripts require full administrator access. To turn off the UAC prompt, set the HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Installer\DisableLUAInRepair registry value to 1. For more information, see: Application Resiliency: Unlock the Hidden Features of Windows Installer Machine Policies - Win32 apps [Remote Desktop Services (RDS)] Fixes an issue in which RDS would stop responding. [Dual boot of Windows and Linux (known issue)] Linux might fail to start up after installing the August 2024 Windows update. The error message is, “Verifying shim SBAT data failed: Security Policy Violation. Something has gone seriously wrong: SBAT self-check failed: Security Policy Violation.” See the full guidance in CVE-2022-2601 and CVE-2023-40547. For more information about the resolved security vulnerabilities, please refer to the Deployments | Security Update Guide and the September 2024 Security Updates. Known issues in this update Symptom Next Step After installing the Windows update released on or after July 9, 2024, Windows Servers might affect Remote Desktop Connectivity across an organization. This issue might occur if legacy protocol (Remote Procedure Call over HTTP) is used in Remote Desktop Gateway. Resulting from this, remote desktop connections might be interrupted. This issue might occur intermittently, such as repeating every 30 minutes. At this interval, logon sessions are lost and users will need to reconnect to the server. IT administrators can track this as a termination of the TSGateway service which becomes unresponsive with exception code 0xc0000005. This issue is fixed in update KB5044342. For the current status of any past known issue, see the Windows Server 2012 Known Issues page. How to get this update Before installing this update We strongly recommend that you install the latest servicing stack update (SSU) for your operating system before installing the latest Rollup. SSUs improve the reliability of the update process to mitigate potential issues while installing the Rollup and applying Microsoft security fixes. For general information about SSUs, see Servicing stack updates and Servicing Stack Updates (SSU): Frequently Asked Questions. If you use Windows Update, the latest SSU (KB5044412) will be offered to you automatically. To get the standalone package for the latest SSU, search for it in the Microsoft Update Catalog. Language packs If you install a language pack after you install this update, you must reinstall this update. Therefore, we recommend that you install any language packs that you need before you install this update. For more information, see Learn about adding a language pack to Windows. title: Windows: DPS: Diagnostic Policy Service fails to start with error 4201
content: Windows: DPS: Diagnostic Policy Service fails to start with error 4201 Important: This was authored via https://aka.ms/contentidea. Follow Content Idea (CI) 198828 link for any updates. Author: Samuel Weng Summary/Symptom The Diagnostic Policy Service (DPS) service fails to start. Cause The cause of this issue is related to event trace session DiagLog. Stopping the event trace session DiagLog triggers these errors when starting the DPS service. Article resolution Check if ETW session DiagLog is running on your machine using tools like Perfmon. After starting the DiagLog ETW session, try starting the DPS service. title: ADDS: PKI: Unable to install CA certificate 0x8007000d ERROR_INVALID_DATA and reinstallation of ADCS role failed with 0x800700b7 ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS
content: ADDS: PKI: Unable to install CA certificate 0x8007000d ERROR_INVALID_DATA and reinstallation of ADCS role failed with 0x800700b7 ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS Important: This was authored via https://aka.ms/contentidea. Follow Content Idea (CI) 198839 link for any updates. Author: Fernando Gude Summary/Symptom Abstract A customer is upgrading their existing two-tier PKI infrastructure to the latest OS. The Root Offline CA was restored using a backup, and two issuing CAs were installed from scratch using enterprise admin account. There is no HSM (Hardware Security Module) involved in the environment. The first issuing CA is healthy and successfully issuing certificates. This article discusses the 0x8007000d ERROR_INVALID_DATA error encountered on the second issuing CA during the installation of a certificate generated from the Root CA, as well as the 0x800700b7 ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS error that occurred after attempting to uninstall and reinstall the ADCS role on the issuing CA. Symptoms When running the command Certutil -f -v -installcert "XXXXXXXXX-SUBCA-20240319.cer", the following error message appears: “An error was detected while configuring Active Directory Certificate Services. The Active Directory Certificate Services Setup Wizard will need to be run to complete the configuration. The new Certification Authority certificate cannot be installed because the CA Version extension is incorrect. The most recently generated request file should be used to obtain the new certificate: C:\Temp\XXXXXXXXX-SUBCA-20240319(1).csr. The data is invalid. 0x8007000d (WIN32: 13 ERROR_INVALID_DATA)”. The system event log shows that the Service Control Manager starts and immediately terminates the certsvc service with error “Installation suspended, incomplete.” The following entries are recorded: Information 3/26/2024 3:29:15 PM Service Control Manager 7036 The Active Directory Certificate Services service entered the running state.Information 3/26/2024 3:29:15 PM Service Control Manager 7036 The Active Directory Certificate Services service entered the stopped state.Error 3/26/2024 3:29:15 PM Service Control Manager 7023 The Active Directory Certificate Services service terminated with the following error: Installation suspended, incomplete. The application event log shows Event ID 27: Active Directory Certificate Services did not start: Hierarchical setup is incomplete. Use the request file in %1.req to obtain a certificate for this certification authority and use the Certification Authority snap-in to install the new certificate and complete the installation. The request file was not found and attempting to renew the certificate with `certutil -renewCert` did not generate a new request file. This led to the decision to uninstall and reinstall the ADCS role on the second issuing CA using PowerShell (code below). However, the setup encountered a CertificationAuthoritySetupException due to the pre-existence of the private key. $params = @{ CACommonName = "Contoso Issuing CA2" CAType = "EnterpriseSubordinateCA" CryptoProviderName = "RSA#Microsoft Software Key Storage Provider" HashAlgorithmName = "SHA256" DatabaseDirectory = "C:\CertDB" LogDirectory = "C:\CertLog" OutputCertRequestFile = "C:\newsetup.csr" } Install-AdcsCertificationAuthority @params The setup continued to fail even when using the parameters below to overwrite the key and existing CA: Install-AdcsCertificationAuthority -OverwriteExistingKey -OverwriteExistingCAInDS @params -Force Exception : Microsoft.CertificateServices.Deployment.Common.CA.CertificationAuthoritySetupException: Setup needs to overwrite existing database files in the "C:\CertDB" folder. It is recommended that you shutdown the applications that are using files in this folder. System.Runtime.InteropServices.COMException: CCertSrvSetup::SetDatabaseInformation: Cannot create a file when that file already exists. 0x800700b7 (WIN32/HTTP: 183 ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS) Procmon reveals `NAME COLLISION` and the Certificate Services Setup log (%SystemRoot%\certocm.log) shows `ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS`, both for the C:\CertLog folder. Renaming C:\CertDB to C:\CertDB_old or deleting its content did not resolve the issue. The -Force switch also made no difference. Cause N/A Article resolution The problem was mitigated by the use of `-OverwriteExistingDatabase` switch, which proved successful in overwriting the previous ADCS configuration and completing the setup without further issues. Install-AdcsCertificationAuthority -OverwriteExistingKey -OverwriteExistingCAInDS -OverwriteExistingDatabase @params Notes: Support Topics: Windows Servers\Windows Server 2016\Windows Server 2016, all editions (Preview)\Certificates and Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) (Preview)\Active Directory Certificate Services (ADCS) (Preview) SR Number: 2403260030003053 First published: Jan 13, 2025 Keywords: pki, 0x8007000d, ERROR_INVALID_DATA, 0x800700b7, ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS, OverwriteExistingDatabase, fegude

title: ConfigMgr: CLD: Unable to create a Cloud Management Gateway -CloudMgr.log has The Resource not found (404)

content: ConfigMgr: CLD: Unable to create a Cloud Management Gateway -CloudMgr.log has The Resource not found (404) Important: This was authored via https://aka.ms/contentidea. Follow Content Idea (CI) 198936 link for any updates. Author: Archana Sathaye Summary/Symptom Issue: Unable to create a Cloud Management Gateway Cause Cause: CloudMgr.log has below error: ERROR: TaskManager: Task [AnalyticsCollectionTask: Service SCCMGateway] has failed. Exception Azure.RequestFailedException, The Resource 'Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/LabCMG1' under resource group 'ResourceGroupName' was not found. For more details please go to https://aka.ms/ARMResourceNotFoundFix~~Status: 404 (Not Found)~~ErrorCode: ResourceNotFound~~~~Content:~~{"error":{"code":"ResourceNotFound","message":"The Resource 'Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/LabCMG1' under resource group 'ResourceGroupName' was not found. For more details please go to https://aka.ms/ARMResourceNotFoundFix"}}~~~~Headers:~~Pragma: no-cache~~x-ms-failure-cause: REDACTED~~x-ms-request-id: some-GUID-~~x-ms-correlation-request-id: REDACTED~~x-ms-routing-request-id: REDACTED~~Strict-Transport-Security: REDACTED~~X-Content-Type-Options: REDACTED~~X-Cache: REDACTED~~X-MSEdge-Ref: REDACTED~~Content-Length: 242~~Cache-Control: no-cache~~Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8~~Date: Fri, 06 Dec 2024 21:42:12 GMT~~Expires: -1~~.~~ To investigate 404 and the reason why it does not exist, may have been logged in earlier. Got the cloudmgr_lo.log to look further. And found below error. ERROR: Exception occured for service LabCMG1: System.AggregateException: One or more errors occurred. ---> Azure.RequestFailedException: At least one resource deployment operation failed. Please list deployment operations for details. Please see https://aka.ms/arm-deployment-operations for usage details.~~Status: 200 (OK)~~ErrorCode: DeploymentFailed~~~~Content:~~{"status":"Failed","error":{"code":"DeploymentFailed","target":"/subscriptions/GUID/resourceGroups/Azure-Resource-Group-Name/providers/Microsoft.Resources/deployments/CreateKeyVault-GUID","message":"At least one resource deployment operation failed. Please list deployment operations for details. Please see https://aka.ms/arm-deployment-operations for usage details.","details":[{"code":"VaultAlreadyExists","message":"The vault name 'LabCMG1' is already in use.Vault names are globally unique, so it is possible that the name is already taken. If you are sure that the vault name was not taken, then it is possible that a vault with the same name was recently deleted but not purged after being placed in a recoverable state. If the vault is in a recoverable state, then the vault will need to be purged before reusing the name. For more information about VaultAlreadyExists, soft delete and purging a vault follow this link https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?linkid=2147740."}]}}~~~~Headers:~~Pragma: no-cache~~x-ms-ratelimit-remaining-subscription-reads: REDACTED~~x-ms- It says: The vault name 'Labvault1' is already in use. Vault names are globally unique Article resolution Resolution: Delete and recreate CMG with a unique name. Cx confirmed that after creating unique name for the cloud management gateway and the issue is resolved. More information Attached the below articles for your reference: - Configuration Manager troubleshooting | Microsoft Learn CMG server authentication certificate - Configuration Manager | Microsoft Learn Notes: Support Topics: Management Tools\Configuration Manager, Management Tools\Configuration Manager\Microsoft Configuration Manager (current branch)\Cloud Services\Cloud Management Gateway (CMG) First published: Jan 16, 2025 Keywords: asathaye, The Resource not found, T 404 Not Found, The vault name is already in use

title: ConfigMgr: CORE: Management Point unable to execute queries against database (CMPDBConnection::ExecuteSQL(): ICommandText::Execute() failed with 0x80040E09)

Follow Content Idea (CI) 197927 link for any updates. Author: Shivam Chhimwal Summary/Symptom There was only one proxy management point (located on Secondary Site Server) in customer`s environment with which the client machines were failing to communicate and was getting the error 0x8000000a We found that the client machine was getting 401 2 (This HTTP status code indicates a problem in the authentication configuration settings on the server.) on the MP IIS logs We were getting error in MP_Framework.log which records the activities of the core management point and client framework components: ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++ MPDB ERROR - CONNECTION PARAMETERS SQL Server Name : XXXXXXX\XXXXXX SQL Database Name : CM_XXX Integrated Auth : True MPDB ERROR - EXTENDED INFORMATION MPDB Method : ExecuteSP() MPDB Method HRESULT : 0x80040E09 Error Description : The EXECUTE permission was denied on the object 'sp_GetPublicKeyForSMSID', database 'CM_XXX', schema 'dbo'. OLEDB IID : {0C733A63-2A1C-11CE-ADE5-00AA0044773D} ProgID : Microsoft SQL Server Native Client 11.0 MPDB ERROR - INFORMATION FROM DRIVER SQL Server Name : XXXXXXXXXXXX Stored Procedure : sp_GetPublicKeyForSMSID Native Error no. : 229 Error State : 5 Class (Severity) : 14 Line number in SP : 1 MpFramework 2/14/2023 2:15:06 PM 10280 (0x2828) ======================================= MpFramework 2/14/2023 2:15:06 PM 10280 (0x2828) CMpDatabase::GetClientPublicKeyEx(ClientID='GUID:9B2FBFB3-A2EB-4446-AE45-B79029F3CD09') failed (0x87d00242). MpFramework 2/14/2023 2:15:06 PM 10280 (0x2828) Stored procedure failed Source: Microsoft Endpoint Configuration Manager ----- ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++ Similar entries were present in MP_location.log: ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++ CMPDBConnection::ExecuteSQL(): ICommandText::Execute() failed with 0x80040E09 MP_LocationManager 2/14/2023 2:11:09 PM 12960 (0x32A0) ======================================= MP_LocationManager 2/14/2023 2:11:09 PM 12960 (0x32A0) MPDB ERROR - CONNECTION PARAMETERS SQL Server Name : XXX SQL Database Name : CM_XXX Integrated Auth : True MPDB ERROR - EXTENDED INFORMATION MPDB Method : ExecuteSP() MPDB Method HRESULT : 0x80040E09 Error Description : The EXECUTE permission was denied on the object 'MP_GetPortalCertificates', database 'CM_XXX', schema 'dbo'. OLEDB IID : {0C733A63-2A1C-11CE-ADE5-00AA0044773D} ProgID : Microsoft SQL Server Native Client 11.0 MPDB ERROR - INFORMATION FROM DRIVER SQL Server Name : XXX Stored Procedure : MP_GetPortalCertificates Native Error no. : 229 Error State : 5 Class (Severity) : 14 Line number in SP : 1 MP_LocationManager 2/14/2023 2:11:09 PM 12960 (0x32A0) ======================================= MP_LocationManager 2/14/2023 2:11:09 PM 12960 (0x32A0) CHandleLocationRequest::CreateReply failed with error (80040e09). MP_LocationManager 2/14/2023 2:11:09 PM 12960 (0x32A0) MP LM: Message discarded MP_LocationManager 2/14/2023 2:11:09 PM 12960 (0x32A0) ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++ Cause Later customer informed that they have removed the MP from the domain and then re-joined it. We informed the customer that this is not supported and should not be performed. ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++ It's not supported to change the following configurations for a computer that hosts a site system role: Domain membership, including if you remove a site system from the domain, and then rejoin the same domain. Domain name Computer name Supporting article: Support for Active Directory domains - Configuration Manager | Microsoft Learn ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++ Article resolution We removed the computer account for the secondary site server (Proxy Management Point for which we are getting the error) from the Primary Site Server database: Then we readded it using the queries: CREATE LOGIN [XXXXXXXX\XXXXXXX$] FROM WINDOWS WITH DEFAULT_DATABASE=[master], DEFAULT_LANGUAGE=[us_english] GO CREATE USER [XXXXXXXX\XXXXXXX1$] FOR LOGIN [XXXXXXXX\XXXXXXX$] WITH DEFAULT_SCHEMA=[dbo] GO Issue was remediated post performing the above-mentioned operation.

title: WMI namespace equivalent to "root\SecurityCenter2" on Windows Server 2019 and later.
content: WMI namespace equivalent to "root\SecurityCenter2" on Windows Server 2019 and later. Important: This was authored via https://aka.ms/contentidea. Follow Content Idea (CI) 197790 link for any updates. Author: Ahmed Omar Summary/Symptom Issue/Inquiry: The existence of a WMI namespace equivalent to "root\SecurityCenter2" on Windows Server 2019 and later, specifically to retrieve the "productState" property. Cause Article resolution Unfortunately, there is no WMI class equivalent to "root\SecurityCenter2" for this purpose. The class was undocumented for a reason in older versions. The above script uses the WscGetSecurityProviderHealth function to get the aggregate health state of the security provider categories. For more information, you can refer to WscGetSecurityProviderHealth function (wscapi.h) - Win32 apps | Microsoft Learn More information It may not work on a Windows Server as it is only supported on client systems. The below script uses the WscGetSecurityProviderHealth function to get the aggregate health state of the security provider categories. Please try the following PowerShell script: $CSharpCode = @" using System; using System.Runtime.InteropServices; public class SecurityProviderHealth { public enum WSC_SECURITY_PROVIDER_HEALTH { WSC_SECURITY_PROVIDER_HEALTH_GOOD, WSC_SECURITY_PROVIDER_HEALTH_NOTMONITORED, WSC_SECURITY_PROVIDER_HEALTH_POOR, WSC_SECURITY_PROVIDER_HEALTH_SNOOZE } [DllImport("wscapi.dll")] public static extern int WscGetSecurityProviderHealth(int providers, out WSC_SECURITY_PROVIDER_HEALTH health); public static string PrintStatus(WSC_SECURITY_PROVIDER_HEALTH status) { switch (status) { case WSC_SECURITY_PROVIDER_HEALTH.WSC_SECURITY_PROVIDER_HEALTH_GOOD: Console.ForegroundColor = ConsoleColor.Green; return "GOOD"; case WSC_SECURITY_PROVIDER_HEALTH.WSC_SECURITY_PROVIDER_HEALTH_NOTMONITORED: Console.ResetColor(); return "NOTMONITORED"; case WSC_SECURITY_PROVIDER_HEALTH.WSC_SECURITY_PROVIDER_HEALTH_POOR: Console.ResetColor(); return "POOR"; case WSC_SECURITY_PROVIDER_HEALTH.WSC_SECURITY_PROVIDER_HEALTH_SNOOZE: Console.ResetColor(); return "SNOOZE"; default: Console.ResetColor(); return "Status Error"; } } public static void GetHealth() { WSC_SECURITY_PROVIDER_HEALTH health; if (WscGetSecurityProviderHealth(0x1, out health) == 0) Console.WriteLine("FIREWALL: " + PrintStatus(health)); if (WscGetSecurityProviderHealth(0x2, out health) == 0) Console.WriteLine("AUTOUPDATE: " + PrintStatus(health)); if (WscGetSecurityProviderHealth(0x4, out health) == 0) Console.WriteLine("ANTIVIRUS: " + PrintStatus(health)); if (WscGetSecurityProviderHealth(0x8, out health) == 0) Console.WriteLine("ANTISPYWARE: " + PrintStatus(health)); if (WscGetSecurityProviderHealth(0x10, out health) == 0) Console.WriteLine("INTERNET SETTINGS: " + PrintStatus(health)); if (WscGetSecurityProviderHealth(0x20, out health) == 0) Console.WriteLine("UAC: " + PrintStatus(health)); if (WscGetSecurityProviderHealth(0x40, out health) == 0) Console.WriteLine("SERVICE: " + PrintStatus(health)); if (WscGetSecurityProviderHealth(0x7FFFFFFF, out health) == 0) Console.WriteLine("ALL: " + PrintStatus(health)); Console.ResetColor(); } public static void Main() { GetHealth(); } } "@ Add-Type -TypeDefinition $CSharpCode [SecurityProviderHealth]::GetHealth() For more information, you can refer to WscGetSecurityProviderHealth function (wscapi.h) - Win32 apps | Microsoft Learn
