title: Procedure: VISOps: Using the One Stop Onboarding Template to provision new users to multiple tools
content: Procedure: VISOps: Using the One Stop Onboarding Template to provision new users to multiple tools Have feedback about this article? – Please provide feedback in the survey link at the bottom of this article. Your feedback matters to us and helps improve article content and support experience for you and our customers. Share your suggestions by providing commentary in the survey box provided. The more you tell us the more we can help. This survey isn’t anonymous. If you leave a comment, you may be contacted by a member of the Process & Program Excellence team​​​​​​​ for more information. Who should use this article? Role: Delivery Partner Admins Organization: All Location: Delivery Partner Sites What is this article about? This article provides instructions for using the One Stop Onboarding Template to provision new users to multiple tools and applications with one ticket submission to VISOps. This helps streamline the onboarding process as multiple templates don’t need to be filled out and submitted as separate tickets. Table of contents 1. Overview 2. Requirements 3. Filling out the template 3.1 Start here: 1. User Info tab 3.2 Completing the other tabs in the template 3.3 Completing the 9. Profiler Tools tab 4. Submit a ticket to VISOps 1. Overview The article details the process of filling out the One Stop Onboarding Template which replaces the need to fill out various other templates and allows the Delivery Partner Admin to just file one ticket for users to be provisioned to several tools or applications by VISOps. The Delivery Partner Admin must fill out a One Stop Onboarding Template with specific details about the users and their provisioning needed to various tools. The template must be attached to the SNOW ticket. Return to top 2. Requirements To minimize delays in processing your request, ensure the following requirements are met. A completed One Stop Onboarding Template (excel file). Submission of a ticket to the VISOps team in SNOW. Return to top 3. Filling out the template The Delivery Partner Admins must download a copy of One Stop Onboarding Template, then fill out the first tab, 1. User Info. The information entered on this tab will carry over to all the other tabs within the template. Important: Delivery Partner Admins can only enter values into the cells which are green and white in color. The blue cells are locked from editing. The template is built to provision up to 10 users. If the request is for greater than 10 users, the Delivery Partner Admins will need to submit a separate request to VISOps with a separate template filled in. The template tabs are numbered and it’s best for the Delivery Partner Admin to fill out each tab sequentially, starting with the first tab: 1. User Info. Return to top 3.1 Start here: 1. User Info tab The Delivery Partner Admins will fill out all columns on this tab. The information entered here will carry over to the other tabs in the file. This tab contains specific information about each user to be provisioned such as their name, background screen ID number, email address, line of business, and others. Return to top 3.2 Completing the other tabs in the template Starting with the second tab, 2. V- Account, the admin will enter the required information into the green and white cells. All blue cells are locked for editing. Key user information is populated into the blue cells on each tab. This is pulled from the first tab, 1. User Info. If there is a mistake on any information in a locked blue cell, the Delivery Partner Admin may correct it by returning to this first tab and making the correction there. The first editable column in every tab asks if the tool or application for that tab is needed or not. Delivery Partner Admins will need to select either Needed or Not Needed from the dropdown menu. This is important because these values are being used to build a working checklist on a hidden tab for VISOps to use to quickly complete the request. If Not Needed was selected, no other columns need to be filled out on that tab. The Delivery Partner Admin can then move on to the next tab. The last editable column is an optional free form Comments column where the Delivery Partner Admin may add any additional context or explanations that they feel VISOps may need to know when completing the request. Return to top 3.3 Completing the 9. Profiler Tools tab On the tab, 9. Profiler Tools, the admin will enter values for all the many Profiler tools and other applications which VISOps also provisions. Like the other tabs, the first editable column asks if Profiler tool access is Needed or Not Needed. The Delivery Partner Admin will answer this question. For users where this access is Needed there are three columns: One column for tools needing access with the users V- Corp account alias. One column for tools needing access with the users MID account alias. One column for tools needing access with the users Delivery Partner specific company email alias. In each column, the Delivery Partner admin will choose the tools or applications needed from a dropdown menu. When more than one tool is needed for the same type of account, the Delivery Partner Admin will continue to select as many tools as needed from the dropdown menu. The template will add each tool selected to the cell in a string. If a tool was selected from the dropdown menu by mistake, the Delivery Partner Admin would need to delete the values entered into that cell and reselect them all again from the dropdown menu. Return to top 4. Submit a ticket to VISOps Once the One Stop Onboarding Template is completed, submit a VISOps SNOW (aka.ms/visops) ticket. Ensure you attach the completed template to the ticket. Return to top Change history Item ID Change Description Date AECT Content Tracking Item 198284 Created new article. 12/17/2024

title: Accessibility in Viva Learning - Microsoft Support
content: Viva Learning is committed to creating an inclusive experience for all users who use the app to discover, share, and recommend learning content. Read this article to learn about the current accessibility features you can use to have the best learning experience for you. These features include: 1. Screen reader support 2. Keyboard only navigation 3. Text size adjustments 4. Optimized color contrast for all elements on screen 5. Multiple color themes: light mode, dark mode and high contrast mode 6. Subtitles for video and audio content 7. Multi-language support You can utilize screen readers and magnifiers to access Viva Learning, helping you navigate and use the platform effectively. Viva Learning is available on both the Web and Teams. Here's how to activate and use accessibility features on each. Enabling accessibility features on your browser To activate the feature Do this Narrator on Windows Press the Windows logo key + Ctrl + Enter on your keyboard. In earlier versions of Windows, you may need to press the Windows logo key + Enter. On the sign-in screen, select the Ease of access button in the lower-right corner, and turn on the toggle under Narrator. Go to Settings > Ease of Access > Narrator, and then turn on the toggle under Use Narrator. Voice over on Mac Go to System Preferences from the Apple menu. Select Accessibility. In the left sidebar, choose VoiceOver. Check the box to Enable VoiceOver or press Command + F5 to toggle VoiceOver on or off. Adjust text size You can change the text size in your browser to view Viva Learning. Microsoft Edge: Open the browser and select the ellipsis (three dots) in the top right corner of the home page. Go to Settings > Appearance. Find the Fonts section. Choose your preferred font size from the dropdown. Learn more about increasing default text size. Change the color theme Select Settings (the gear icon at the top right corner of the screen). A side panel opens, displaying the available theme options and an option to enable dark mode. Additionally, you can adjust color themes in the browser you use to view Viva Learning. Microsoft Edge: Open the Microsoft Edge browser. Select the ellipsis (three dots) in the top right corner of the home page. Go to Settings. From the Settings page, go to Appearance. Choose your preferred theme from the Theme and Overall appearance section. Turn on or turn off subtitles Select a course with video content. Toggle subtitles on or off by selecting the CC icon in the video player control bar. Change language Select the ellipsis (three dots) in the top right corner of the home page. Select Settings from the dropdown menu. In the Language tab, choose your preferred language and select Save & Refresh. Enabling accessibility features on the Teams application To activate the feature Do this Narrator on Windows Press the Windows logo key + Ctrl + Enter on your keyboard. In earlier versions of Windows, you may need to press the Windows logo key + Enter. On the sign-in screen, select the Ease of access button in the lower-right corner, and turn on the toggle under Narrator. Go to Settings > Ease of Access > Narrator, and then turn on the toggle under Use Narrator. Voice over on Mac Go to System Preferences from the Apple menu. Select Accessibility. In the left sidebar, choose VoiceOver. Check the box to Enable VoiceOver or press Command + F5 to toggle VoiceOver on or off. Adjust text size Select the ellipsis (three dots) next to your avatar in the top right corner. Select Zoom from the panel Adjust zoom with + or – icons. Change the color theme Select the ellipsis (three dots) next to your avatar in the top right corner. Select Settings. Go to Appearance and accessibility from the left menu. Under the Theme section, you can choose a theme according to your preferences Turn on or turn off subtitles Select a course with video content. Toggle subtitles on or off by selecting the CC icon in the video player control bar. Change language Select the ellipsis (three dots) in the top right corner of the home page. Select Settings from the dropdown menu. In the Language tab, choose your preferred language and select Save & Refresh.

title: ADDS: W32time: Windows Time sync request from client fails due to WaitTimeout with error code “0x800705B4”
content: ADDS: W32time: Windows Time sync request from client fails due to WaitTimeout with error code “0x800705B4” Important: This was authored via https://aka.ms/contentidea. Follow Content Idea (CI) 198559 link for any updates. Author: Md Habib Nawaz Summary/Symptom In certain scenarios, a time synchronization request from a client to a domain controller can fail, returning a "WaitTimeout" error. This issue is often identified through the failure of the Strip Chart command, which returns the error code "0x800705B4". Below is an example of the output when attempting to sync time with the command w32tm /stripchart /computer:Cont-DC.contoso.com /samples:5 /dataonly: Tracking Cont-DC.contoso.com [DC:123]. Collecting 5 samples. The current time is 12/16/2024 1:17:10 PM. 13:17:10, error: 0x800705B4 13:17:13, error: 0x800705B4 13:17:16, error: 0x800705B4 13:17:19, error: 0x800705B4 13:17:22, error: 0x800705B4 Cause The primary cause of this issue is the disabling of the Windows Time NTP Server provider on the domain controller via the system registry. This configuration prevents proper time synchronization with the client. Article resolution To resolve this issue, follow these steps: Backup the Registry: Before making any changes to the registry, it's crucial to back up the current settings. Navigate to HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\W32Time\ and create a backup. Enable the NTP Server Provider: Option 1: Set the "Enabled" (DWORD) value to 1 in the following registry key: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\W32Time\TimeProviders\NtpServer Option 2: Alternatively, you can delete the registry key HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\W32Time\TimeProviders\NtpServer after ensuring a backup is available. title: Customize your calendar in Microsoft Teams - Microsoft Support
content: Customize your calendar view in Microsoft Teams for a tailored approach to managing your schedule. In this article Change your calendar view Save a calendar view Apply calendar filters Delete a calendar view View different time scales Change your calendar view Your Teams calendar will display your work week schedule by default, but you can choose to view your schedule for the entire week or specific days only. Select your current view at the top of your calendar to choose a different view. Apply calendar filters At the top of your calendar or in More options , select Filter . Deselect specific types of events to remove them from view. View different time scales Change your time scale in the new calendar to adjust the amount of space for meeting details. To change your calendar’s time scale: Select your calendar view (e.g., Work week, Week, etc.). Select Time scale. Choose the time scale you want to view your calendar in. When you choose a time scale, the change will be applied immediately. Tips: Increase the time scale to see more of your schedule at once, but with fewer details. Decrease the time scale to see your schedule close-up, with more details. Save a calendar view When you’ve set the specific filters, calendar groups, and other presets you want to see in your calendar, save the view to return to it later. To save a calendar view: Select your calendar view. From the dropdown menu, select Saved views > Save current view. Name the view and select Save. To apply a saved view: Select your calendar view. From the dropdown menu, select Saved views . Select the view you want to apply. Delete a calendar view To delete a saved calendar view: Select your calendar view. From the dropdown menu, select Saved views . Next to the view you want to delete, select > Delete . Related topics Get started with the new calendar in Microsoft Teams View multiple calendars in Microsoft Teams

title: Windows 11:NET: Wi-Fi fails to connect automatically after GP update when fMinimizeConnections and fBlockNonDomain transition from 3,1 to 0,0 respectively
content: Windows 11:NET: Wi-Fi fails to connect automatically after GP update when fMinimizeConnections and fBlockNonDomain transition from 3,1 to 0,0 respectively Important: This was authored via https://aka.ms/contentidea. Follow Content Idea (CI) 198835 link for any updates. Author: Bharath Kumar M Summary/Symptom The customer is implementing a security baseline called CIS Baseline Security GPO, which has WCM configuration to disables simultaneous network connections and blocks any new network connections when a domain authenticated connection is already present. This security baseline policy sets the WCM settings fMinimizeConnections to 3 and fBlockNonDomain to 1. This Group Policy is applied to all Windows 11 devices in the environment. However, the customer wants to create an exception to allow multiple network connections for a specific set of devices. They created another Group Policy with WCM settings fMinimizeConnections set to 0 and fBlockNonDomain set to 0. Baseline Security GPO is also enabling “Process even if the Group Policy objects have not changed” setting. The issue arises when the first Group Policy is processed, causing the Wi-Fi interface to disconnect as expected. However, when the second Group Policy is processed, the Wi-Fi should automatically reconnect, but it does not do so. Repro Steps: Customer has setup two GPOs in the following way in an OU containing Windows 11 machines.The 1st GPO having lowest precedence is setting the below to all Windows 11 machines, Apply the settings as specified in CIS Baseline Security GPO which also contains the below WCM settings. fMinimizeConnections to 3 to block Wi-Fi Connection when connected to Ethernet. fBlockNonDomain to 1 to prevent connections to both a domain-based network and a non-domain-based network at the same time. The 2nd GPO having higher precedence is setting the below to few Windows 11 machines through GPO machine account security filtering to exempt them from above strict WCM policy, fMinimizeConnections set to 0 fBlockNonDomain to 0. Let’s say we have a client in the exemption category (WCM settings of Winning GPO - 2nd GPO) and with the above GPO configuration in place, perform a gpupdate with Ethernet and Wi-Fi connected to CORP network. Both connections are needed to reproduce the issue. Wi-Fi gets disconnected and it does not connect automatically. Even when Ethernet is unplugged later, Wi-Fi does not auto-connect. Expected Behaviour: Wi-Fi should reconnect automatically. Cause This issue is identified as bug in Windows 11 ( 21H2 /22H2 /23H2 /24H2) Operating system Bug 55459382: Win11: Wi-Fi fails to connect automatically after GP update when fMinimizeConnections and fBlockNonDomain transition from 3,1 to... - Boards Article resolution Verified workarounds: 1. Once disconnected, disable and re-enable the Wi-Fi adapter, to let Wi-Fi connect automatically. 2. Set “Process even if the Group Policy objects have not changed” to disabled. 3. Organize the GPOs linked in the Windows 11 OU such that, GPO 1 – “Applies baseline security settings (except WCM settings) to all computers” GPO 2 – “Applies the fMinimizeConnections=3, fBlockNonDomain=1 to all computers with exempted computers in the Deny List” GPO 3 – “Applies the fMinimizeConnections=0, fBlockNonDomain=0 only to the exempted computers” 4. The other possibility is to restart the WCM service after the group policies have been applied. This will then auto-reconnect the Wi-Fi. But during the application of the GPOs the Wi-Fi gets disconnected and would only be re-connected after restarting the WCM when Group Policy is completed. More information +++++++++++ MS INTERNAL Do not share with customer +++++++++++++++ WCMSvc gets the notification as GPO changes are applied, and we will review the 2 stages below, 1. fMinimizeConnections to 3 and fBlockNonDomain to 1 2. fMinimizeConnections to 0 and fBlockNonDomain to 0 (After GP Registry extension processing is completed – Settings of 2nd GPO - Winning)For 1st set of notification,1. fMinimizeConnections=3 and fBlockNonDomain=1 values are read, with Wi-Fi connected still.2. EvaluateDomainDomainPolicyAction () identifies no conflict between Ethernet and Wi-Fi as both are domain-authenticated.3. TokenManager::Evaluate calls to ApplyStrictMinimizePolicyFilter() which clears all tokens for Wi-Fi interface as Ethernet is already connected (fMinimizeConnections=3).4. WCM is later notified of Wi-Fi disconnection through the event “wcm_notification_cde_disconnected” and EvaluateDomainDomainPolicyAction() is called as result of network status change.5. EvaluateDomainDomainPolicyAction() disables AutoConnect token for Wi-Fi and marks the action as “DisconnectAndDenyAutoConnect” as fBlockNonDomain=1.The reason is that as we have a domain-authenticated Ethernet, Wi-Fi is disconnected currently, hence Wi-Fi auto-connect to be blocked.For 2nd set of notification, 1. fMinimizeConnections=0 and fBlockNonDomain=0 values are read again. 2. EvaluateDomainDomainPolicyAction() is called, does not reset the Action set on the list of interfaces and returns early. 3. TokenManager::Evaluate() -> ApplyDomainPolicyFilter() -> GetDomainPolicyActionForInterface () returns the stale value “DisconnectAndDenyAutoConnect” that was calculated when the settings were fMinimizeConnections=3 and fBlockNonDomain=1.4. Wi-Fi interface does not have the auto-connect token after the last GP change notification and needs to be connected manually.Detailed Analysis:Ethernet GUID – {e70fbf0f-0589-4599-b3d0-2004a22aa980}Wi-Fi GUID – {e37d2a65-7e67-4b24-9eff-479611d13435}For 1st set of notification,1. fMinimizeConnections=3 and fBlockNonDomain=1 values are read, with Wi-Fi connected still.11556 [0] 0A80.1048::11/15/24-18:31:48.3755083 [wcmserver] configmanager_cpp708 ConfigManager::InternalGetCdePolicies() - ConfigManager::InternalGetCdePolicies - using the Group Policy fMinimizeConnections value (3)11580 [1]0A80.1048::11/15/24-18:31:48.3900956 [Operational ] A Group Policy change was processed11585 [5] 0A80.1074::11/15/24-18:31:48.3906645 [wcmserver] configmanager_cpp854 ConfigManager::InternalGetWcmGroupOrLocalPolicy() - ConfigManager::InternalGetWcmGroupOrLocalPolicy - using the Group Policy fBlockNonDomain value (1)2. title: Windows Server: RDS connection fails with error "Your credentials did not work"
content: Windows Server: RDS connection fails with error "Your credentials did not work" Important: This was authored via https://aka.ms/contentidea. Follow Content Idea (CI) 198860 link for any updates. Author: Leon Cheng Summary/Symptom RDP to destination, then popup below error message and RDP failed. Your credentials did not work. Background: 1.workgroup environment. 2.local user for RDP. Test user: **DSH Source IP: ***.4 Destination: ***.5 Cause Source system was set the lmcompatibilitylevel as 2, destination system was set the lmcompatibilitylevel as 5, NTLM version is not matched. Article resolution We can follow below link to make NTLM version on source and destination are matched. Path: HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\lmcompatibilitylevel Setting Description Registry security level Send LM & NTLM responses Client devices use LM and NTLM authentication, and they never use NTLMv2 session security. Domain controllers accept LM, NTLM, and NTLMv2 authentication. 0 Send LM & NTLM – use NTLMv2 session security if negotiated Client devices use LM and NTLM authentication, and they use NTLMv2 session security if the server supports it. Domain controllers accept LM, NTLM, and NTLMv2 authentication. 1 Send NTLM response only Client devices use NTLMv1 authentication, and they use NTLMv2 session security if the server supports it. Domain controllers accept LM, NTLM, and NTLMv2 authentication. 2 Send NTLMv2 response only Client devices use NTLMv2 authentication, and they use NTLMv2 session security if the server supports it. Domain controllers accept LM, NTLM, and NTLMv2 authentication. 3 Send NTLMv2 response only. Refuse LM Client devices use NTLMv2 authentication, and they use NTLMv2 session security if the server supports it. Domain controllers refuse to accept LM authentication, and they'll accept only NTLM and NTLMv2 authentication. 4 Send NTLMv2 response only. Refuse LM & NTLM Client devices use NTLMv2 authentication, and they use NTLMv2 session security if the server supports it. Domain controllers refuse to accept LM and NTLM authentication, and they'll accept only NTLMv2 authentication. 5 More information TS: ----- 1.Checked the connection between source and destination----------ping and test-connection IP 3389 are working. 2.recreate a new user on destination and try to RDP----------same issue 3.Try other sources RDP to destination-------Other sources RDP to destination are working, only this client have this issue. 4.Collect the logs with below TSS commands Client: .\TSS.ps1 -Start -Scenario ADS_Auth -UEX_RDScli Server: .\TSS.ps1 -Start -Scenario ADS_Auth -UEX_RDSsrv Analysis result:--------------------- Nonworking scenario: RDSH network trace Source ETL: [1] 3404.35CC::01/13/25-17:34:06.3635271 [RdpWinSecFilter] SecurityFilter_cpp324 CSecurityFilter::DoHandshake() - [89f41665]HandshakeWorker (hr=0x8009030c) [1] 3404.35CC::01/13/25-17:34:06.3635279 [RdpWinSecFilter] SecurityFilter_cpp368 CSecurityFilter::DoHandshake() - [89f41665]DoHandshake: Disconnecting due to SSPI error! hr = 0x8009030c [1] 3404.35CC::01/13/25-17:34:06.3635297 [XPlatSslFilter] SslFilter_cpp2882 CTscSslFilter::ContinueHandshake() - [89f41665]_spSecFilter->DoHandshake failed! title: How to download and Install language packs while you are using Windows Server Update Services (WSUS) as the update source
content: How to download and Install language packs while you are using Windows Server Update Services (WSUS) as the update source Important: This was authored via https://aka.ms/contentidea. Follow Content Idea (CI) 198350 link for any updates. Author: Selim Abdallah Summary/Symptom As the WSUS does not offer to download the language pack files , The Windows instance cannot obtain the corresponding updates from the WSUS server. As a result, installation issues occur because the installation files of language packs do not exist on the instance. symptoms: the check box of the install language back does not appear when you try to add language from settings Cause WSUS does not offer to download the language pack files Article resolution Workaround: Method 1 - first work around is to run the below script before you add language to temporary disable the link to use WSUS for a moment of the installation and restore it back again after installing Open PowerShell as an admin and run the below commands Set-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate\AU' -Name UseWUServer -Value 0 Restart-Service -Name wuauserv Then go to setting and add language you will see the check box appear After that you need to run the script again to restore the changes to value 1 for the WSUS setting Set-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate\AU' -Name UseWUServer -Value 1 Restart-Service -Name wuauserv ------------------------------------------------------- -- Method 2 Downland the language pack ISO of Windows 2019 and install the required language pack as below Download language pack offline iso from your volume license On the Microsoft Volume License Site or the Microsoft Visual Studio Subscription website, search for language pack and you will find all language packs for all supported operating systems. Extract or mount the ISO on a server share to be shared with all servers Use LPKsetup.exe to install the language pack , Run the language pack setup “LPKsetup.exe” then select and install the language you need from the iso files Then install the language pack from the language setting in the Windows setting – region and language – add language

title: ConfigMgr: Communication failing with ERROR_WINHTTP_INVALID_SERVER_RESPONSE
content: ConfigMgr: Communication failing with ERROR_WINHTTP_INVALID_SERVER_RESPONSE Important: This was authored via https://aka.ms/contentidea. Follow Content Idea (CI) 197967 link for any updates. Author: Yukti Arora Summary/Symptom One complete subnet after client upgrade not able to communicate with MP and few clients in same subnet where client upgrade failed were able to communicate. Successfully queued event on HTTP/HTTPS failure for server 'ABC.XYZ.COM'. CcmMessaging Post to http://ABC.XYZ.COM/ccm_system/request failed with 0x87d00231. CcmMessaging Failed in WinHttpReceiveResponse API, ErrorCode = 0x2f78 CcmMessaging [CCMHTTP] ERROR: URL=http://ABC.XYZ.COM/ccm_system_windowsauth/request, Port=80, Options=1504, Code=12152, Text=ERROR_WINHTTP_INVALID_SERVER_RESPONSE Cause Specifically check and ask for all the proxy in between source and destination. Article resolution Check in IIS logs with client logs in case of any hit (as client needs to connect to the windows_auth endpoint first, first hit will fail with 401 but subsequent request goes through since the client get the kerb token) If no hits are found in IIS, then: Collect netmon trace from source and destination while browsing URL http://ABC.XYZ.COM/ccm_system/request and http://ABC.XYZ.COM/ccm_system_windowsauth/request failed in system context. Filter with IP address with source and destination in respective netmon to check if you are able to find hit or misses. If you are not able to find respective IP’s in netmon, then try to download cab file using link http://WUServerFQDN:port/Selfupdate/wuident.cab and check in IIS, if you are able to find respective IP addresses in the log file. If any proxy issue will be there, client will be re-directed to proxy address and that will be present in IIS log file during that time stamp. From there you can be assured that this is a proxy configuration issue and not something with SCCM. Notes: Support Topics: Management Tools\Configuration Manager\Microsoft Configuration Manager (current branch)\Client Installation, Registration and Assignment\Client Registration First published: Jan 06, 2025

title: KB5046911: Safe OS Dynamic Update for Windows 10, version 1607 and Windows Server 2016: November 12, 2024 - Microsoft Support
content: Applies ToWin 10 Ent LTSB 2016 Win 10 IoT Ent LTSB 2016 Windows Server 2016 Support for Windows 10 will end in October 2025 After October 14, 2025, Microsoft will no longer provide free software updates from Windows Update, technical assistance, or security fixes for Windows 10. Your PC will still work, but we recommend moving to Windows 11. Learn more Summary This update makes improvements to the Windows recovery environment in Windows 10, version 1607 and Windows Server 2016. How to get this update Install this update To install this update, use one of the following release channels. Windows UpdateUpdate CatalogServer Update Services Available Next step Yes This update is available through Windows Update. It will be downloaded and installed automatically. Available Next step Yes To get the standalone package for this update, go to the Microsoft Update Catalog website. To download updates from the Update Catalog, see Steps to download updates from the Windows Update Catalog. Available Next step No See the other release channels. Prerequisites There are no prerequisites to apply this update. Restart information You do not have to restart your device after you apply this update. Removal information This update cannot be removed once it is applied to a Windows image. Update replacement information This update replaces the previously released update KB5044613. Verify the installation of this update After installing this update, the WinRE version installed on the device should be 10.0.14393.7513. Methods to verify the WinRE version installed​​​​​​​​​​​​​​ GetWinReVersion.ps1WinREAgent eventDISM command To get the version of WinRE installed, run the following PowerShell script "GetWinReVersion.ps1" with Administrator credentials. After you run the script, you should receive the installed WinRE version as in the following example: GetWinReVersion.ps1 PowerShell script ################################################################################################ # # Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation. # Licensed under the MIT License. # # THE SOFTWARE IS PROVIDED *AS IS*, WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND, EXPRESS OR # IMPLIED, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO THE WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, # FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE AND NONINFRINGEMENT. IN NO EVENT SHALL THE # AUTHORS OR COPYRIGHT HOLDERS BE LIABLE FOR ANY CLAIM, DAMAGES OR OTHER # LIABILITY, WHETHER IN AN ACTION OF CONTRACT, TORT OR OTHERWISE, ARISING FROM, # OUT OF OR IN CONNECTION WITH THE SOFTWARE OR THE USE OR OTHER DEALINGS IN THE # SOFTWARE. # ################################################################################################ # Function to get WinRE path function GetWinREPath { $WinRELocation = (reagentc /info | Select-String "Windows RE location") if ($WinRELocation) { return $WinRELocation.ToString().Split(':')[-1].Trim() } else { Write-Host "Failed to find WinRE path" -ForegroundColor Red exit 1 } } # Creates and needs to be return the mount directory function GetMountDir { # systemdirve\mnt $MountDir = "$env:SystemDrive\mnt" if (-not (Test-Path $MountDir)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $MountDir -Force | Out-Null } return $MountDir } # Function to get WinRE version function GetWinREVersion { $mountedPath = GetMountDir $filePath = "$mountedPath\Windows\System32\winpeshl.exe" $WinREVersion = (Get-Item $filePath).VersionInfo.FileVersionRaw.Revision return [int]$WinREVersion } # Main Execution $WinREPath = GetWinREPath # Make dir C:\mnt if not exists $TempDir = GetMountDir # Get the read write permission for this directory if (-not (Test-Path $TempDir)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $TempDir -Force | Out-Null } # Mount WinRE image dism /Mount-Image /ImageFile:"$WinREPath\winre.wim" /Index:1 /MountDir:"$TempDir" $WinREVersion = GetWinREVersion Write-Host "WinRE Version: $WinREVersion" -ForegroundColor Cyan dism /Unmount-Image /MountDir:"$TempDir" /Discard Remove-Item -Path $TempDir -Force -Recurse WinREAgent logs events related to the Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE), primarily recording details about the creation, modification, and usage of the recovery image. In this case, we are looking for Event ID: 4501 Servicing succeeded events. If you are unsuccessful in locating WinREAgent servicing events because of space limitations that might occur in your environment, we suggest you use the DISM command. Open the Windows Search bar. To do this, right-click Start and then click Search. In the Search bar, type Event Viewer and then click Event Viewer. Expand Windows Logs and then click System. In the right-side navigation pane, under Actions, click Find. In the Find what: box, type WinREAgent and then click Find Next. Click Cancel to close the Find dialog box. The WinREAgent servicing event should be shown in the bottom middle pane and you should see a message similar to the followng on the General tab: Servicing succeeded. The Windows Recovery Environment version is now: 10.0.22621.4742 The WinRE version in this example is 10.0.22621.4742. ​​​​​​​To view the Event Properties pane for the WinREAgent servicing event, right-click the WinREAgent entry in the System pane (top middle pane) and then click Event Properties. ​​​​​​​ Open an elevated Windows command prompt. To do this, press the Windows key, type cmd, right-click Command Prompt, and then click Run as Administrator. At the command prompt, type reagentc /info and then press Enter. Note the path of the Windows RE location. For this example, the location is \\?\GLOBALROOT\device\harddisk0\partition5\Recovery\WindowsRE. This path may vary based on your Windows installation. At the command prompt, use the DISM command to retrieve the Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE) information. For this example, enter the following command and then press Enter: Dism /Get-ImageInfo /ImageFile:\\?\GLOBALROOT\device\harddisk0\partition5\Recovery\WindowsRE\winre.wim /index:1 Note The default name for the WinRE image file is winre.wim. In your environment, the name of the WinRE image file might be different. Also, the Index number of the default winre.wim file is 1. In your environment, the Index number might be different. The WinRE image file information is returned as illustrated in the following example: The WinRE version in this example is 10.0.22621.4742. title: November 12, 2024—KB5046682 (Monthly Rollup) - Microsoft Support
content: Applies ToWindows Server 2012 R2 ESU Important The installation of this Extended Security Update (ESU) might fail when you try to install it on an Azure Arc-enabled device that is running Windows Server 2012 R2. For a successful installation, please make sure all Subset of endpoints for ESU only are met as described in Connected Machine agent network requirements. End of support information Windows 8.1 reached the end of support (EOS) on January 10, 2023, at which point technical assistance and software updates are no longer provided. If you have devices running Windows 8.1, we recommend upgrading them to a more current, in-service, and supported Windows release. If devices do not meet the technical requirements to run a more current release of Windows, we recommend that you replace the device with one that supports Windows 11. Microsoft will not be offering an Extended Security Update (ESU) program for Windows 8.1. Continuing to use Windows 8.1 after January 10, 2023 may increase an organization’s exposure to security risks or impact its ability to meet compliance obligations. For more information, see Windows 8.1 support will end on January 10, 2023. We recommend upgrading to a later version of Windows. For more information, see Upgrade to a later version of Windows. Windows Server 2012 R2 reached the end of support (EOS) on October 10, 2023. Extended Security Updates (ESUs) are available for purchase and will continue for three years, renewable on an annual basis, until the final date on October 13, 2026. For more information, see Windows Server End of Support: Key Dates. For information about the procedure to continue receiving security updates, see KB5031043. We recommend upgrading to a later version of Windows Server. For more information, see Overview of Windows Server upgrades. Windows Embedded 8.1 Industry Enterprise and Windows Embedded 8.1 Industry Pro reached the end of support (EOS) on July 11, 2023. Therefore, technical assistance and software updates are no longer provided. Summary Learn more about this cumulative security update, including improvements, any known issues, and how to get the update. Note For information about the various types of Windows updates, such as critical, security, driver, service packs, and so on, see Description of the standard terminology that is used to describe Microsoft software updates. To view other notes and messages, see the Windows 8.1 and Windows Server 2012 R2 update history home page. Improvements This cumulative security update includes improvements that are part of update KB5044343 (released October 8, 2024). The following is a summary of the key issues that this update addresses. The bold text within the brackets indicates the item or area of the change we are documenting. [Virtual Machine] Fixed: A virtual switch might trigger consistent crashes and you receive a stop error on a blue screen. This issue might occur when load balancing and failover (LBFO) teaming with two virtual switches in a virtual machine (VM) are used. In this case, one virtual switch contains a single root I/O virtualization (SR-IOV) interface. For more information about the resolved security vulnerabilities, please refer to the Deployments | Security Update Guide and the November 2024 Security Updates. Known issues in this update We are currently not aware of any issues with this update. For the most up-to-date information about known issues for Windows Server 2012 R2, please go to the Windows release health dashboard. How to get this update Before installing this update We strongly recommend that you install the latest servicing stack update (SSU) for your operating system before you install the latest Monthly Rollup. SSUs improve the reliability of the update process to mitigate potential issues while installing the Monthly Rollup and applying Microsoft security fixes. For general information about SSUs, see Servicing stack updates and Servicing Stack Updates (SSU): Frequently Asked Questions. If you use Windows Update, the latest SSU (KB5044411) will be offered to you automatically. To get the standalone package for the latest SSU, search for it in the Microsoft Update Catalog. Language packs If you install a language pack after you install this update, you must reinstall this update. Therefore, we recommend that you install any language packs that you need before you install this update. For more information, see Learn about adding a language pack to Windows. Install this update To install this update, use one of the following release channels. Windows UpdateUpdate CatalogServer Update Services Available Next step Yes This update will be downloaded and installed automatically from Windows Update. Available Next step Yes To get the standalone package for this update, go to the Microsoft Update Catalog website. To download updates from the Update Catalog, see Steps to download updates from the Windows Update Catalog. Available Next step Yes This update will automatically sync with Windows Server Update Services (WSUS) if you configure Products and Classifications as follows: Product: Windows Server 2012 R2 Classification: Security Updates File information For a list of the files that are provided in this update, download the file information for update KB5046682.

title: October 8, 2024 Security update (KB5044281)
content: <div> October 8, 2024 Security update (KB5044281) For information about Windows update terminology, see the article about the types of Windows updates and the monthly quality update types. For an overview of Azure Stack HCI, version 22H2, see its update history page. Improvements This security update includes quality improvements. Below is a summary of the key issues that this update addresses when you install this KB. If there are new features, it lists them as well. The bold text within the brackets indicates the item or area of the change we are documenting. [Software Defined Networking (SDN)] New! The SDN API now performs better for large-scale deployments. Watch for load balancer connectivity issues after you install this update. If you have any, move the SDNAPI microservice to another node. An SDN admin can move the service. To do that, use the Move-ServiceFabricPrimaryReplica PowerShell cmdlet. [MSIX applications] Fixed: When you install them from an HTTPS URI, they fail to open. This issue occurs when the download of the app is not complete. This damages the package. [Task Manager] Fixed: It stops responding when you select the “Performance” tab. [Direct Composition batched presentations] Fixed: A brief flash of triangles or boxes show on the screen. This issue affects browsers, like Microsoft Edge, and other apps. [Input Method Editor (IME)] Fixed: When a combo box has input focus, a memory leak might occur when you close that window. [AppLocker] Fixed: The rule collection enforcement mode is not overwritten when rules merge with a collection that has no rules. This occurs when the enforcement mode is set to “Not Configured.” [Remote Desktop Gateway Service] Fixed: The service stops responding. This occurs when a service uses remote procedure calls (RPC) over HTTP. Because of this, the clients that are using the service disconnect. For more information about security vulnerabilities, please refer to the Security Update Guide and the October 2024 Security Updates. To return to the Azure Stack HCI documentation site Azure Stack HCI, version 22H2 servicing stack update (KB5044414)- 20349.2750 This update makes quality improvements to the servicing stack, which is the component that installs Windows updates. Servicing stack updates (SSU) ensure that you have a robust and reliable servicing stack so that your devices can receive and install Microsoft updates. Known issues in this update Microsoft is not currently aware of any issues with this update. How to get this update Before you install this update Microsoft now combines the latest servicing stack update (SSU) for your operating system with the latest cumulative update (LCU). For general information about SSUs, see Servicing stack updates and Servicing Stack Updates (SSU): Frequently Asked Questions. To install the LCU on your Azure Stack HCI cluster, see Update Azure Stack HCI clusters. Install this update To install this update, use one of the following Windows and Microsoft release channels. Windows UpdateBusinessCatalogServer Update Services Available Next Step Yes None. This update will be downloaded and installed automatically from Windows Update and Microsoft Update. Available Next Step Yes None. This update will be downloaded and installed automatically from Windows Update for Business in accordance with configured policies. Available Next Step Yes To get the standalone package for this update, go to the Microsoft Update Catalog website. Available Next Step Yes This update will automatically sync with Windows Server Update Services (WSUS) if you configure Products and Classifications as follows: Product: Azure Stack HCI Classification: Security Updates If you want to remove the LCU To remove the LCU after installing the combined SSU and LCU package, use the DISM/Remove-Package command line option with the LCU package name as the argument. You can find the package name by using this command: DISM /online /get-packages. Running Windows Update Standalone Installer (wusa.exe) with the /uninstall switch on the combined package will not work because the combined package contains the SSU. You cannot remove the SSU from the system after installation. File Information For a list of the files that are provided in this update, download the file information for cumulative update 5044281. For a list of the files that are provided in the servicing stack update, download the file information for the SSU (KB5044414) - version 20349.2750. title: May 14, 2024—KB5037800 (Monthly Rollup)
content: May 14, 2024—KB5037800 (Monthly Rollup) End of support information Windows Server 2008 SP2 Extended Security Updates (ESU) third and final year ended on January 10, 2023. Additionally, Extended Security Updates on Azure only support ended on January 9, 2024. For more information, see Extended Security Updates for Windows Server overview. We recommend that you upgrade to a later version of Windows Server. For more information, see Overview of Windows Server upgrades. Summary Learn more about this cumulative security update, including improvements, any known issues, and how to get the update. NOTE As of July 2020, optional non-security releases for this operating system are no longer offered. Operating systems in extended support have only cumulative monthly security updates. Verify that you have installed the required updates in the How to get this update section before installing this update. For information about the various types of Windows updates, such as critical, security, driver, service packs, and so on, see Description of the standard terminology that is used to describe Microsoft software updates. To view other notes and messages for Windows Server 2008 SP2, see Windows Server 2008 SP2 update history. Improvements This cumulative security update contains improvements that are part of update KB5036932 (released April 9, 2024). This update includes the following improvements: Croatia currency is changed from Krona to Euro. Resolves the following known issues after installing the update released April 9, 2024 (KB5036932): A Domain Controller might experience an unexpectedly high NTLM authentication load. Your VPN connection might fail. For more information about the resolved security vulnerabilities, please refer to the Deployments | Security Update Guide and the May 2024 Security Updates. Known issues in this update Symptom Next step After installing this update and restarting your device, you might receive the error, “Failure to configure Windows updates. Reverting Changes. Do not turn off your computer”, and the update might show as Failed in Update History. This is expected in the following circumstances: If you are installing this update on a device that is running an edition that is not supported for ESU. For a complete list of which editions are supported, see KB4497181. If you do not have an ESU MAK add-on key installed and activated. If you have an ESU key and have encountered this issue, please verify you have applied all prerequisites and that your key is activated. For information on activation, see the Obtaining Extended Security Updates for eligible Windows devices blog post. For information on the prerequisites, see the "How to get this update" section of this article. How to get this update Before installing this update We strongly recommend that you install the latest servicing stack update (SSU) for your operating system before you install the latest Monthly Rollup. SSUs improve the reliability of the update process to mitigate potential issues while installing the Monthly Rollup and applying Microsoft security fixes. For general information about SSUs, see Servicing stack updates and Servicing Stack Updates (SSU): Frequently Asked Questions. If you use Windows Update, the latest SSU (KB5034867) will be offered to you automatically. To get the standalone package for the latest SSU, search for it in the Microsoft Update Catalog. Language packs If you install a language pack after you install this update, you must reinstall this update. Therefore, we recommend that you install any language packs that you need before you install this update. For more information, see Learn about adding a language pack to Windows. Install this update To install this update, use one of the following release channels. Windows UpdateUpdate CatalogServer Update Services Available Next Step Yes This update will be downloaded and installed automatically from Windows Update if you are an ESU customer. Available Next Step Yes To get the standalone package for this update, go to the Microsoft Update Catalog website. To download updates from the Update Catalog, see Steps to download updates from the Windows Update Catalog. Available Next Step Yes This update will automatically sync with WSUS if you configure Products and Classifications as follows: Product: Windows Server 2008 Service Pack 2 Classification: Security Updates For more information, see Configure classifications and products to synchronize. title: November 12, 2024—KB5046615 (OS Build 17763.6532)
content: November 12, 2024—KB5046615 (OS Build 17763.6532) 11/17/20 For information about Windows update terminology, see the article about the types of Windows updates and the monthly quality update types. For an overview of Windows 10, version 1809, see its update history page. Important: Windows updates do not install Microsoft Store application updates. If you are an enterprise user, see Microsoft Store apps - Configuration Manager. If you are a consumer user, see Get updates for apps and games in Microsoft Store. Highlights This update addresses security issues for your Windows operating system. Improvements This security update includes improvements. Below is a summary of the key issues that this update addresses when you install this KB. If there are new features, it lists them as well. The bold text within the brackets indicates the item or area of the change we are documenting. [vmswitch] Fixed: A vmswitch triggers a stop error. This occurs when you use Load Balancing and Failover (LBFO) teaming with two virtual switches on a virtual machine (VM). In this case, one virtual switch uses single root Input/Output virtualization (SR-IOV). [Windows Kernel Vulnerable Driver Blocklist file (DriverSiPolicy.p7b)] Fixed: This update adds to the list of drivers that are at risk for Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver (BYOVD) attacks. If you installed earlier updates, only the new updates contained in this package will be downloaded and installed on your device. For more information about security vulnerabilities, please refer to the new Security Update Guide website and the November 2024 Security Updates. Windows 10 servicing stack update (KB5043126) - 17763.6289 This update makes quality improvements to the servicing stack, which is the component that installs Windows updates. Servicing stack updates (SSU) ensure that you have a robust and reliable servicing stack so that your devices can receive and install Microsoft updates. Known issues in this update Symptom Workaround Following the installation of the October 2024 security update, some customers report that the OpenSSH (Open Secure Shell) service fails to start, preventing SSH connections. The service fails with no detailed logging, and manual intervention is required to run the sshd.exe process. This issue is affecting both enterprise, IOT, and education customers, with a limited number of devices impacted. Microsoft is investigating whether consumer customers using Home or Pro editions of Windows are affected. This issue is addressed in KB5053596. How to get this update Before you install this update Microsoft now combines the latest servicing stack update (SSU) for your operating system with the latest cumulative update (LCU). SSUs improve the reliability of the update process to mitigate potential issues while installing the LCU. For general information about SSUs, see Servicing stack updates and Servicing Stack Updates (SSU): Frequently Asked Questions. Prerequisite: You must install the August 10, 2021 SSU (KB5005112) before installing the LCU. Install this update To install this update, use one of the following Windows and Microsoft release channels. Windows UpdateBusinessCatalogServer Update Services Available Next Step Yes None. This update will be downloaded and installed automatically from Windows Update and Microsoft Update. Available Next Step Yes None. This update will be downloaded and installed automatically from Windows Update for Business in accordance with configured policies. Available Next Step Yes To get the standalone package for this update, go to the Microsoft Update Catalog website. Available Next Step Yes This update will automatically sync with Windows Server Update Services (WSUS) if you configure Products and Classifications as follows: Product: Windows 10 Classification: Security Updates If you want to remove the LCU To remove the LCU after installing the combined SSU and LCU package, use the DISM/Remove-Package command line option with the LCU package name as the argument. You can find the package name by using this command: DISM /online /get-packages. Running Windows Update Standalone Installer (wusa.exe) with the /uninstall switch on the combined package will not work because the combined package contains the SSU. You cannot remove the SSU from the system after installation. File information For a list of the files that are provided in this update, download the file information for cumulative update 5046615. For a list of the files that are provided in the servicing stack update, download the file information for the SSU (KB5043126) - version 17763.6289. title: September 10, 2024—KB5043087 (Security-only update)
content: September 10, 2024—KB5043087 (Security-only update) End of support information Windows Server 2008 SP2 Extended Security Updates (ESU) third and final year ended on January 10, 2023. Additionally, Extended Security Updates on Azure only support ended on January 9, 2024. For more information, see Extended Security Updates for Windows Server overview. We recommend that you upgrade to a later version of Windows Server. For more information, see Overview of Windows Server upgrades. Summary Learn more about this security-only update, including improvements, any known issues, and how to get the update. Note As of July 2020, optional non-security releases for this operating system are no longer offered. Operating systems in extended support have only cumulative monthly security updates. Verify that you have installed the required updates in the How to get this update section before installing this update. For information about the various types of Windows updates, such as critical, security, driver, service packs, and so on, see Description of the standard terminology that is used to describe Microsoft software updates. To view other notes and messages for Windows Server 2008 SP2, see Windows Server 2008 SP2 update history. Improvements The following is a summary of the key issues that this update addresses. The bold text within the brackets indicates the item or area of the change we are documenting. [User Account Control (UAC)] When the Windows Installer repairs an application, the UAC does not prompt for your credentials. After you install this update, it will prompt for them. Because of this, you might have to update your automation scripts. Additionally, you should add the Shield icon to indicate that your automation scripts require full administrator access. To turn off the UAC prompt, set the HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Installer\DisableLUAInRepair registry value to 1. For more information, see: Application Resiliency: Unlock the Hidden Features of Windows Installer Machine Policies - Win32 apps [Remote Desktop Services (RDS)] Fixes an issue in which RDS would stop responding. For more information about the resolved security vulnerabilities, please refer to the Deployments | Security Update Guide and the September 2024 Security Updates. Known issues in this update Symptom Next step After installing this update and restarting your device, you might receive the error, “Failure to configure Windows updates. Reverting Changes. Do not turn off your computer”, and the update might show as Failed in Update History. This is expected in the following circumstances: If you are installing this update on a device that is running an edition that is not supported for ESU. For a complete list of which editions are supported, see KB4497181. If you do not have an ESU MAK add-on key installed and activated. If you have an ESU key and have encountered this issue, please verify you have applied all prerequisites and that your key is activated. For information on activation, see the Obtaining Extended Security Updates for eligible Windows devices blog post. For information on the prerequisites, see the How to get this update section of this article. For the current status of any past known issue, see the Windows Server 2008 SP2 Known Issues page. How to get this update Before installing this update We strongly recommend that you install the latest servicing stack update (SSU) for your operating system before you install the latest Monthly Rollup. SSUs improve the reliability of the update process to mitigate potential issues while installing the Monthly Rollup and applying Microsoft security fixes. For general information about SSUs, see Servicing stack updates and Servicing Stack Updates (SSU): Frequently Asked Questions. If you use Windows Update, the latest SSU (KB5039341) will be offered to you automatically. To get the standalone package for the latest SSU, search for it in the Microsoft Update Catalog. Language packs If you install a language pack after you install this update, you must reinstall this update. Therefore, we recommend that you install any language packs that you need before you install this update. For more information, see Learn about adding a language pack to Windows. Install this update To install this update, use one of the following release channels. Windows UpdateUpdate CatalogServer Update Services Available Next step No This update is not available from Windows Update. See the Update Catalog or Server Update Services release channel. Available Next step Yes To get the standalone package for this update, go to the Microsoft Update Catalog website. To download updates from the Update Catalog, see Steps to download updates from the Windows Update Catalog. Available Next step Yes This update will automatically sync if you configure Products and Classifications as follows: Product: Windows Server 2008 Service Pack 2 Classification: Security Updates For more information about configuring in WSUS, see Windows Server Update Services (WSUS). For more information about configuring in Configuration Manager, see Synchronize software updates. Reminder If you are using Security-only updates, you will also need to install all previous Security-only updates and the latest cumulative update for Internet Explorer (KB5043049). File information For a list of the files that are provided in this update, download the file information for update KB5043087.

title: Event ID 2017 is frequently logged on the server
content: Event ID 2017 is frequently logged on the server Important: This was authored via https://aka.ms/contentidea. Follow Content Idea (CI) 197633 link for any updates. Author: Sudha N Summary/Symptom Issue: Event ID 2017 is frequently logged on the server Log Name: Application Source: Microsoft-Windows-PerfOS Date: Event ID: 2017 Task Category: None Level: Warning Keywords: User: SYSTEM Computer: Description: Unable to collect NUMA physical memory utilization data. The first four bytes (DWORD) of the Data section contains the status code. This event is not causing any performance issues on the server at this point But it is logged multiple time every day Cause The event is logged indicating issue with the performance counters. The counters might be damaged or out of sync, hence flagging the event. Article resolution Rebuild the performance counters: From elevated command prompt run the below command: Lodctr /r

title: ConfigMgr: SRV: exporting the reports in excel fail with the error "rrRendering Error"
content: ConfigMgr: SRV: exporting the reports in excel fail with the error "rrRendering Error" Microsoft Configuration Manager (current branch) More...Less Important: This was authored via https://aka.ms/contentidea. Follow Content Idea (CI) 197513 link for any updates. Author: Nikhil Chandra Borkar Summary/Symptom When the customer is exporting reports from SSRS web portal in excel format, they were getting the following error message: Cause The permissions on the execution account (make sure to grab it from reporting configuration manager) were missing on a registry key which will cause the exporting failure. Article resolution 1/ we grabbed a procmon of the system when executing the export of the report. 2/ we observed that we were getting access denied on the following registry key - Computer\HKEY_USERS\S-1-5-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx\Software\Microsoft\ Avalon.Graphics 3/ we gave the execution account read permission to the reg key exclusively which resolved the issue. More information https://stackoverflow.com/questions/45864808/ssrs-reports-exporting-to-excel-gives-rrrenderingerror-error-the-type-initial Reporting Services Registry Access Denied When Exporting - Business wIntelligence Notes: Support Topics: Management Tools\Configuration Manager First published: Nov 22, 2024 Keywords: rrRendering error, SSRS, nborkar, reporting, excel

title: ConfigMgr: SRV: SQL ODBC driver was failing to install with error - "Error 2503 Called RunScript when not marked in progress" and "Error 2502 Called InstallFinalize when no install in progress."
keywords: odbc,2503,2502,msi,nborkar,"Called RunScript when not marked in progress","Called InstallFinalize when no install in progress."
content: ConfigMgr: SRV: SQL ODBC driver was failing to install with error - "Error 2503 Called RunScript when not marked in progress" and "Error 2502 Called InstallFinalize when no install in progress." Important: This was authored via https://aka.ms/contentidea. Follow Content Idea (CI) 197515 link for any updates. Author: Nikhil Chandra Borkar Summary/Symptom CX was trying to upgrade their SCCM infrastructure to latest version but the pre-req check failed with ODBC driver install failure. we tried to install the ODBC driver manually but it failled with following errors- "Error 2503 Called RunScript when not marked in progress" "Error 2502 Called InstallFinalize when no install in progress." Cause MSI installation was failing manually on the sever. no particular reason but access denied on temp folder. Article resolution 1/ We cleaned up the c:\windows\temp folder and made sure the file count in it is less than 64k files. 2/ we tried the following commands to check if there was a system level corruption- sfc /scannow DISM.exe /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth /Source:C:\RepairSource\Windows /LimitAccess 3/ We gave the user running the install full access to temp folder - Go to Local Disc (C:) and open the Windows folder. Find the Temp folder and right-click on it. Go to Properties >>> Security tab >>> Advanced. Click on your Windows user and change the permission to Full control. Click Apply. If you receive warning messages, click Yes and continue. 4/ Rebooted the server and the issue still persists. 5/ We tried to use command prompt to install the ODBC driver msi package (make sure to run the command prompt as system context, we used psexec here) Msiexec.exe /I “mssqlodbc.msi” /l*v “c:\temp\odbcinstall.log” 6/ This time, it went through, and the config manger upgrade was also successful. More information https://www.boxaid.com/blog/how-to-fix-2502-2503-errors/ https://advyon.com/solved-2502-2503-error-when-installing-from-a-msi-file/ Notes: Support Topics: Management Tools\Configuration Manager First published: Nov 22, 2024 Keywords: odbc, 2503, 2502, msi, nborkar, "Called RunScript when not marked in progress", "Called InstallFinalize when no install in progress."

title: wsl.exe fails to launch with the error "Access is denied"
content: wsl.exe fails to launch with the error "Access is denied" Important: This was authored via https://aka.ms/contentidea. Follow Content Idea (CI) 197726 link for any updates. Author: Chanakya Manepalli Summary/Symptom WSL.exe throws an error "ACCESS IS DENIED" when tried to launch. Customer has also shared the following error message: EventID=1092 domain/username ran C:\Windows\System32\wsl.exe, which attempted to access the process LxssManagerProxyStub.dll, violating the rule "Executing Windows Subsystem for Linux", and was blocked. For information about how to respond to this event, see KB85494. Cause We observed that WSL.exe attempted to load LxssManagerProxyStub.dll and encountered an ACCESS DENIED error. It appears that the McAfee process initiated a scan and subsequently blocked the file from being loaded. During our research, we found a discussion on a third-party forum where a similar issue was resolved by disabling a McAfee-defined Access Protection rule. Additionally, the KB85494 document shared by the customer is a McAfee article that briefly discusses a process being blocked from accessing a specific file. NLS messaging syntax: " <domain>\<user> ran <process name>, which attempted to access <path>\<filename>. The <malware type> named <malware name> was detected and access to the file was denied." Article resolution McAfee End Point has a McAfee-defined Access Protection rule that blocks WSL execution. Once this rule was disabled, WSL started working without issue. More information References: linux - Trying to get WSL working on a Windows Server 2019 VM. Getting 'Access denied' error - Super User Complete list of event IDs for Endpoint Security wsl.exe fails with "Access is denied" · Issue #4920 · microsoft/WSL Test attack surface reduction rules - Microsoft Defender for Endpoint | Microsoft Learn

content: Applies ToMicrosoft Teams Microsoft Teams for Education Earn Reading 3-day, 5-day, and 7-day streaks to unlock valuable rewards in Reading Coach. This feature aims to motivate students to engage in consistent reading habits. Additionally, readers can monitor their progress over different time frames—weekly, 30-days, and all-time—through an intuitive dashboard designed for learners of all ages. This user-friendly interface not only tracks their reading achievements but also encourages them to set and achieve new reading goals, thereby fostering a lifelong love for reading. My Progress Achievements and History, once on the Reading Coach homepage, are now under the My Progress tab. Selecting this tab will load the following page: When you click on the My Progress tab, you will see a new page that shows how well you are doing with your reading. Choosing any one of the boxes for reading time, readings completed, average accuracy, and correct words per minute will produce a graph showing your progress. My achievements shows the badges you’ve earned over the selected time period. And my stories displays stories you’ve completed throughout a select period. It helps you get better at reading, learn new words, and feel good about your reading skills. When you read using Reading Coach, you can earn badges. If you read for three, five, or seven days in a seven day period, you get special badges called Reading Streak badges. title: December 10, 2024—KB5048661 (OS Build 17763.6659) - Microsoft Support
content: Applies ToWin 10 Ent LTSC 2019 Win 10 IoT Ent LTSC 2019 Windows 10 IoT Core LTSC Windows Server 2019 11/17/20 For information about Windows update terminology, see the article about the types of Windows updates and the monthly quality update types. For an overview of Windows 10, version 1809, see its update history page. Important: Windows updates do not install Microsoft Store application updates. If you are an enterprise user, see Microsoft Store apps - Configuration Manager. If you are a consumer user, see Get updates for apps and games in Microsoft Store. Highlights This update addresses security issues for your Windows operating system. Improvements This security update includes improvements. Below is a summary of the key issues that this update addresses when you install this KB. If there are new features, it lists them as well. The bold text within the brackets indicates the item or area of the change we are documenting. [Motherboard replacement] Fixed: Windows does not activate after you replace a motherboard. ​​​​​​​ If you installed earlier updates, only the new updates contained in this package will be downloaded and installed on your device. For more information about security vulnerabilities, please refer to the new Security Update Guide website and the December 2024 Security Updates. Windows 10 servicing stack update (KB5043126) - 17763.6289 This update makes quality improvements to the servicing stack, which is the component that installs Windows updates. Servicing stack updates (SSU) ensure that you have a robust and reliable servicing stack so that your devices can receive and install Microsoft updates. Known issues in this update Symptom Workaround Following the installation of the October 2024 security update, some customers report that the OpenSSH (Open Secure Shell) service fails to start, preventing SSH connections. The service fails with no detailed logging, and manual intervention is required to run the sshd.exe process. This issue is affecting both enterprise, IOT, and education customers, with a limited number of devices impacted. Microsoft is investigating whether consumer customers using Home or Pro editions of Windows are affected. Customers can temporarily resolve the issue by updating permissions (ACLs) on the affected directories. Follow these steps: Open PowerShell as an Administrator. Update the permissions for C:\ProgramData\ssh and C:\ProgramData\ssh\logs to allow full control for SYSTEM and the Administrators group, while allowing read access for Authenticated Users. You can restrict read access to specific users or groups by modifying the permissions string if needed. Use the following commands to update the permissions: $directoryPath = "C:\ProgramData\ssh" $acl = Get-Acl -Path $directoryPath $sddlString = "O:BAD:PAI(A;OICI;FA;;;SY)(A;OICI;FA;;;BA)(A;OICI;0x1200a9;;;AU)" $securityDescriptor = New-Object System.Security.AccessControl.RawSecurityDescriptor $sddlString $acl.SetSecurityDescriptorSddlForm($securityDescriptor.GetSddlForm("All")) Set-Acl -Path $directoryPath -AclObject $acl Repeat the above steps for C:\ProgramData\ssh\logs. Microsoft is actively investigating the issue and will provide a resolution in an upcoming Windows update. Further communications will be provided when a resolution or additional workarounds are available. How to get this update Before you install this update Microsoft now combines the latest servicing stack update (SSU) for your operating system with the latest cumulative update (LCU). SSUs improve the reliability of the update process to mitigate potential issues while installing the LCU. For general information about SSUs, see Servicing stack updates and Servicing Stack Updates (SSU): Frequently Asked Questions. Prerequisite: You must install the August 10, 2021 SSU (KB5005112) before installing the LCU. Install this update To install this update, use one of the following Windows and Microsoft release channels. Windows UpdateBusinessCatalogServer Update Services Available Next Step Yes None. This update will be downloaded and installed automatically from Windows Update and Microsoft Update. Available Next Step Yes None. This update will be downloaded and installed automatically from Windows Update for Business in accordance with configured policies. Available Next Step Yes To get the standalone package for this update, go to the Microsoft Update Catalog website. Available Next Step Yes This update will automatically sync with Windows Server Update Services (WSUS) if you configure Products and Classifications as follows: Product: Windows 10 Classification: Security Updates If you want to remove the LCU To remove the LCU after installing the combined SSU and LCU package, use the DISM/Remove-Package command line option with the LCU package name as the argument. You can find the package name by using this command: DISM /online /get-packages. Running Windows Update Standalone Installer (wusa.exe) with the /uninstall switch on the combined package will not work because the combined package contains the SSU. You cannot remove the SSU from the system after installation. File information For a list of the files that are provided in this update, download the file information for cumulative update 5048661. For a list of the files that are provided in the servicing stack update, download the file information for the SSU (KB5043126) - version 17763.6289.
