title: Procedure: VISOps: Microsoft Teams card for Modern Identity (MID) Account Password Distribution
content: Procedure: VISOps: Microsoft Teams card for Modern Identity (MID) Account Password Distribution Have feedback about this article? – Please provide feedback in the survey link at the bottom of this article. Your feedback matters to us and helps improve article content and support experience for you and our customers. Share your suggestions by providing commentary in the survey box provided. The more you tell us the more we can help. This survey isn’t anonymous. If you leave a comment, you may be contacted by a member of the Process & Program Excellence team​​​​​​​ for more information. Who should use this article? Role: Delivery Partner Admin and FTEs Organization: All Location: All What is this article about? A Modern Identity (MID) account is a type of Microsoft account separate from a corpnet account; used for support related tools. This article provides details about receiving a Modern Identity (MID) account password via a Microsoft Teams card. Table of contents 1. Overview 2. Microsoft Teams card 3. Users are ready to receive their password 4. MID account no longer needed 1. Overview The article provides details regarding the VISOps team sending a Microsoft Teams card to inform users that their new Microsoft Identity (MID) account and password are ready, or for a MID account password reset. Receiving a password for a MID account requires a voice call between the user and the VISOps team. The Teams card offers users the option to connect with the VISOps team via a voice call. Using a Microsoft Teams card, sent to the user’s corpnet account, the users can select Yes or No to receive the password for their MID account. Important: Receiving a password for a MID account must occur via a voice chat with the VISOps team. Return to top 2. Microsoft Teams card Once the VISOps team creates the MID account or the user submits the password reset request, the VISOps will send a Microsoft Teams card to the end user via their Teams chat associated with their corpnet account (@microsoft.com). The sender is Workflows as shown below: Figure one: Workflows – Sent a card Return to top 3. Users are ready to receive their password The user selects Yes in the Teams card message, when ready and available for their password. The Teams card will go into a group Teams chat for all VISOps team members. A VISOps team member will then initiate a Teams chat with the user and call the user at a time that is convenient for them. If the user is on a call, near the end of their shift, or on an off day when the Teams card arrives, they simply leave the card in the chat and select Yes at another time when they are available. The card will not expire for at least 30 days. Figure two: VISOps is ready to share the password Notes: If the user selects Yes on the Teams card but they do not receive a response from the VISOps team, or it occurs at a time when they are no longer able to take the call then a new Teams card will be sent within a day. If there is no response from the VISOps team within a day the Delivery Partner Admin or FTE should open a new VISOps SNOW ticket. The VISOps team sends out the Teams cards in waves to better load balance the volume for VISOps. Return to top 4. MID account no longer needed If the user no longer requires assistance from the VISOps team they can select No to decline any further action on their MID account for the current request. The VISOps will note that the user has declined MID account assistance. The VISOps team will make no further contact on the request. Should the user need their MID account password reset at a future date, the Delivery Partner Admin or FTE will open a new VISOps SNOW ticket and start this process again to receive a new Teams card at that time. Return to top Notes: First published: Apr 08, 2025 Keywords: UpdatedByRubik Tags: Rubik Article Id: 5574 Change history Item Change Description Date AECT CONTENT TRACKING ITEM 202410 Fixed formatting issues. 5/8/2025 AECT Content Tracking Item 198315 Created new article. 12/16/2024

title: ADDS: GPHELP: Understanding Group Policy Object versionNumber Limits
keywords: #Group Policy Object (GPO) #GPO version number limit #GPO max value 65535 #GPO changes detection #GPO version reset #GPO versionNumber attribute #adsiedit GPO version #Sysvol GPO version #GPMC GPO version #gpsvclog GPO processing #Group Policy changes #GP
content: ADDS: GPHELP: Understanding Group Policy Object versionNumber Limits Important: This was authored via https://aka.ms/contentidea. Follow Content Idea (CI) 198572 link for any updates. Author: Vivek Agarwal Summary When the Group Policy Object (GPO) version number for a computer reaches its maximum value of 65535 (Decimal), any further changes made by the admin to the GPO will still be detected by the client machines. Lab Environment: Client Machine: Client3.contoso.com Domain Controller (DC): ContTokDCD.contoso.com GPO Name: MSTEST-GPO5 More information Steps to Reproduce: Create a GPO: Create a GPO named MSTEST-GPO5 and configure one computer group policy setting in it. It will show computer version 1 (AD) and 1 (Sysvol). Example GPO GUID: {AE143147-B206-469D-A074-0B908A12FCDC} Set Maximum Version Number: In adsiedit, edit the GPO GUID {AE143147-B206-469D-A074-0B908A12FCDC} and set the versionNumber attribute value to 2147483647. In the Sysvol folder for the GPO {AE143147-B206-469D-A074-0B908A12FCDC}, set the gpt.iniversionNumber value to 2147483647. Link the GPO appropriately where the computer objects reside. It will show computer version 65535 (AD) and 65535 (Sysvol) in GPMC. GPSVC(1890.f24) 05:17:51:870 ProcessGPOs(Machine): Processing extension Registry GPSVC(1890.f24) 05:17:51:870 ReadStatus: Read Extension's Previous status successfully. GPSVC(1890.f24) 05:17:51:870 ReadGPOList:++ GPSVC(1890.f24) 05:17:51:871 ReadGPOList: Read Key:0 GPSVC(1890.f24) 05:17:51:872 ReadGPOList: Read Key:1 GPSVC(1890.f24) 05:17:51:872 ReadGPOList:-- (Result:TRUE) GPSVC(1890.f24) 05:17:51:872 CheckGPOs: ReadGPOList count = 2 GPSVC(1890.f24) 05:17:51:872 CompareGPOLists: Different version numbers found ------- GPSVC(1890.f24) 05:17:51:873 ParseRegistryFile: Entering with \\contoso.com\SysVol\contoso.com\Policies\{AE143147-B206-469D-A074-0B908A12FCDC}\Machine\registry.pol. GPSVC(1890.f24) 05:17:51:889 SetRegistryValue: RedirectionGuardPolicy => 1 [OK] GPSVC(1890.f24) 05:17:51:889 SetRegistryValue: DisableWebPrinting => 0 [OK] GPSVC(1890.f24) 05:17:51:889 ParseRegistryFile: Leaving. Observations: When the GPO Version Number Reaches 65535: There is no problem from the security filter check; the access check passes. The gpsvclog from the client shows the following: GPSVC(1890.f24) 05:13:54:068 ProcessGPO(Machine): ============================== GPSVC(1890.f24) 05:13:54:068 ProcessGPO(Machine): Searching <cn={AE143147-B206-469D-A074-0B908A12FCDC},cn=policies,cn=system,DC=contoso,DC=com> GPSVC(1890.f24) 05:13:54:068 ProcessGPO(Machine): Machine has access to this GPO. GPSVC(1890.f24) 05:13:54:068 ProcessGPO(Machine): Found common name of: <{AE143147-B206-469D-A074-0B908A12FCDC}> GPSVC(1890.f24) 05:13:54:068 ProcessGPO(Machine): GPO passes the filter check. GPSVC(1890.f24) 05:13:54:068 ProcessGPO(Machine): Found functionality version of: 2 GPSVC(1890.f24) 05:13:54:068 ProcessGPO(Machine): Found file system path of: \\contoso.com\SysVol\contoso.com\Policies\{AE143147-B206-469D-A074-0B908A12FCDC} GPSVC(1890.f24) 05:13:54:084 ProcessGPO(Machine): Found display name of: <MSTEST-GPO5> GPSVC(1890.f24) 05:13:54:084 ProcessGPO(Machine): Found machine version of: GPC is 65535, GPT is 65535 GPSVC(1890.f24) 05:13:54:084 ProcessGPO(Machine): Found flags of: 0 GPSVC(1890.f24) 05:13:54:084 ProcessGPO(Machine): Found extensions: [{35378EAC-683F-11D2-A89A-00C04FBBCFA2}{D02B1F72-3407-48AE-BA88-E8213C6761F1}] GPSVC(1890.f24) 05:13:54:084 ProcessGPO(Machine): ============================== When Configuring One More Setting in GPO: The counter value resets and starts from 1. The GPMC shows the GPO AD and Sysvol versions as 1. The gpsvclog from the client shows the following: GPSVC(1890.f24) 05:17:51:636 ProcessGPO(Machine): ============================== GPSVC(1890.f24) 05:17:51:636 ProcessGPO(Machine): Searching <cn={AE143147-B206-469D-A074-0B908A12FCDC},cn=policies,cn=system,DC=contoso,DC=com> GPSVC(1890.f24) 05:17:51:636 ProcessGPO(Machine): Machine has access to this GPO. GPSVC(1890.f24) 05:17:51:636 ProcessGPO(Machine): Found functionality version of: 2 GPSVC(1890.f24) 05:17:51:636 ProcessGPO(Machine): Found file system path of: \\contoso.com\SysVol\contoso.com\Policies\{AE143147-B206-469D-A074-0B908A12FCDC} GPSVC(1890.f24) 05:17:51:651 ProcessGPO(Machine): Found display name of: <MSTEST-GPO5> GPSVC(1890.f24) 05:17:51:651 ProcessGPO(Machine): Found machine version of: GPC is 1, GPT is 1 GPSVC(1890.f24) 05:17:51:651 ProcessGPO(Machine): Found flags of: 0 GPSVC(1890.f24) 05:17:51:651 ProcessGPO(Machine): Found extensions: [{35378EAC-683F-11D2-A89A-00C04FBBCFA2}{D02B1F72-3407-48AE-BA88-E8213C6761F1}] GPSVC(1890.f24) 05:17:51:651 ProcessGPO(Machine): ============================== ------- GPSVC(1890.f24) 05:17:51:870 ProcessGPOs(Machine): Processing extension Registry GPSVC(1890.f24) 05:17:51:870 ReadStatus: Read Extension's Previous status successfully. GPSVC(1890.f24) 05:17:51:870 ReadGPOList:++ GPSVC(1890.f24) 05:17:51:871 ReadGPOList: Read Key:0 GPSVC(1890.f24) 05:17:51:872 ReadGPOList: Read Key:1 GPSVC(1890.f24) 05:17:51:872 ReadGPOList:-- (Result:TRUE) GPSVC(1890.f24) 05:17:51:872 CheckGPOs: ReadGPOList count = 2 GPSVC(1890.f24) 05:17:51:872 CompareGPOLists: Different version numbers found ------- GPSVC(1890.f24) 05:17:51:873 ParseRegistryFile: Entering with \\contoso.com\SysVol\contoso.com\Policies\{AE143147-B206-469D-A074-0B908A12FCDC}\Machine\registry.pol. GPSVC(1890.f24) 05:17:51:889 SetRegistryValue: RedirectionGuardPolicy => 1 [OK] GPSVC(1890.f24) 05:17:51:889 SetRegistryValue: DisableWebPrinting => 0 [OK] GPSVC(1890.f24) 05:17:51:889 ParseRegistryFile: Leaving. Conclusion: In this scenario, the client computer will process the group policy changes successfully even when the version number reaches its maximum value and resets. The gpsvclog confirms the successful processing of the GPO changes. description: Use the calendar in Microsoft Teams to streamline meeting and event scheduling, customize your view, and more.
title: Get started with the Microsoft Teams calendar - Microsoft Support
content: Streamline meeting and event scheduling, customize your calendar views, and much more in Microsoft Teams for desktop. In this article Open your calendar Find the right place to meet Change your calendar view Share your calendar View other calendars Print your calendar Schedule and start meetings and events Quickly access past meeting details Open your calendar To start using your Teams calendar, select Calendar ​​​​​​​ on the left side of Teams. Change your calendar view Your Teams calendar will display your work week by default. See other views, like the entire week or month, by selecting Work week at the top of your calendar and choosing one. You can also:​​​​​​​ Change the time scale to adjust space for meeting details. Save calendar views to access specific layouts later. Select Filter to customize the types of events that appear on your calendar. Select Show navigation pane to see the mini-month view, view other people’s calendars, create calendar groups, and more. Select More options > Calendar settings to change your calendar appearance, adjust event and meeting settings, and more. To learn more, see Customize your calendar in Microsoft Teams. View other calendars View multiple calendars at the same time for seamless coordination and event planning. Look at different people’s calendars, calendars that highlight birthdays or holidays, and more. In the top-left corner, select Show navigation pane . Under My calendars, create and select calendar groups to quickly bring up views of specific calendars later. Switch between split and combined views to see other calendars side-by-side or integrated into one. To learn more, see View other calendars in Microsoft Teams. Schedule and start meetings and events Easily schedule meetings and events of all types from your Teams calendar. To schedule a new meeting or event: Select Calendar in Teams. Select New or select a timeslot in your calendar. Select the dropdown arrow next to New to choose from different types of event templates. Select View all templates to see more. Select Scheduler to find a time that works best for everyone. Enter meeting or event details. Select Save . Important: When scheduling a virtual Teams meeting, turn on the Teams meeting toggle. To join a meeting or event: Select Calendar in Teams. Select a meeting or event. Select Join . To learn more about joining a Teams meeting, see Join a meeting in Microsoft Teams. Find the right place to meet When choosing a room or location for your meeting, you’ll see more details about available rooms, like capacity and technical specs. You’ll also see the option to Browse with Places Finder. To learn more, see Get started with Microsoft Places. Share your calendar Share your calendar with others to give them insight into your schedule and availability. To share your calendar with someone specific: Select Calendar in Teams. Select More options > Share . Enter the email address or contact you want to share with. Next to their name, select the dropdown menu to choose their permissions. Select Share. Depending on policies set by your IT admin, you can also manage permissions for other people in your organization in the dropdown menu below. To learn more, see Share your calendar in Microsoft Teams. Print your calendar Print out your calendar to distribute physical copies of it or keep it on hand for markups and easy access. To learn more, see Share your calendar in Microsoft Teams. Quickly access past meeting details Go right to a past meeting’s recap, chat, and other details in your Teams calendar. To access: Select Calendar in Teams. Select a past recorded meeting. Select Recap to view the meeting recap. Select Chat ​​​​​​​ to open the meeting chat. To learn more about recap in Teams, see Meeting recap in Microsoft Teams. Related topics Customize your calendar in Microsoft Teams View multiple calendars in Microsoft Teams

title: ConfigMgr: Core: ConfigMgr Setup fails with "SetCertRegistryRemote failed with error 0x80070057"
content: ConfigMgr: Core: ConfigMgr Setup fails with "SetCertRegistryRemote failed with error 0x80070057" Important: This was authored via https://aka.ms/contentidea. Follow Content Idea (CI) 198811 link for any updates. Author: Pavel Yurenev Summary/Symptom Customer tries to set up a new ConfigMgr site. After filling up all the wizard fields and passing the prerequisite checks, the Setup fails with the following error in ConfigMgrSetup.log: Configuration Manager Setup 5976 (0x1758) Make sure there is crypto key generated for the site server.Configuration Manager Setup 5976 (0x1758) crypto key is not found. Generate crypt key.Configuration Manager Setup 5976 (0x1758) ERROR: Failed to get Exchange Public key.Configuration Manager Setup 5976 (0x1758) INFO: Configuring SQL trace flags for server SQL.Server.FQDNConfiguration Manager Setup 5976 (0x1758) INFO: Setting -T8295 SQL Server Param already exists as SQLArg3.Configuration Manager Setup 5976 (0x1758) INFO: Name for SQL Server Param string value is SQLArg4.Configuration Manager Setup 5976 (0x1758) INFO: Creating SQL Server machine certificate for Server [SQL.Server.FQDN]...Configuration Manager Setup 5976 (0x1758) INFO: 'SQL.Server.FQDN' is a valid FQDN.Configuration Manager Setup 5976 (0x1758) SetCertRegistryRemote failed with error 0x80070057Configuration Manager Setup 5976 (0x1758) ERROR: Failed to write certificate configuration to registry on server SQL.Server.FQDNConfiguration Manager Setup 5976 (0x1758) ERROR: Failed to create SQL Server [SQL.Server.FQDN] certificate remotely.Configuration Manager Setup 5976 (0x1758) Not recovery mode or not top level site. Skip restoring client piloting packages.Configuration Manager Setup 5976 (0x1758) ~~===================== Completed Configuration Manager Server Setup ===================== The latter error code 0x80070057 is ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER - The parameter is incorrect. Cause SetCertRegistryRemote writes the registry entries remotely to the SQL machine, including the public key that should be created before. However, this process failed few lines above: the proper logging should look like: Configuration Manager Setup 1108 (0x454) Make sure there is crypto key generated for the site server.Configuration Manager Setup 1108 (0x454) crypto key is not found. Generate crypt key.Configuration Manager Setup 1108 (0x454) site server has crypto key. public key is 0602... Capturing the ProcMon filtered by C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Crypto\RSA\MachineKeys folder shows that SetupWPF.exe fails to access the machine key: SetupWpf.exe 10264 11152 CreateFile C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Crypto\RSA\MachineKeys\ca6f80c6495f318cbd7dddd0d9102cc2_09cea177-5c11-4006-9f8b-93d15ff882de ACCESS DENIED Desired Access: Generic Read, Disposition: Open, Options: Sequential Access, Synchronous IO Non-Alert, Non-Directory File, Attributes: n/a, ShareMode: Read, AllocationSize: n/a This means that Machine Keys have been tampered with - making the OS out of support. Article resolution Reinstall the future Site Server OS from scratch (just recreate the VM). More information If the customer accepts the risks, find the affected Key File in the Procmon trace: filter by SetupWPF.exe process and Path containing MachineKeys. Then provide the user who runs the Setup the full control over the key file.

title: Window Server 2025: Input lag when using virtualization based security (VBS) or Secure Boot
content: Window Server 2025: Input lag when using virtualization based security (VBS) or Secure Boot Important: This was authored via https://aka.ms/contentidea. Follow Content Idea (CI) 203083 link for any updates. Author: Konstantin Chernyi Summary/Symptom Customer using VMware and moving from Windows server 2016 to Windows server 2025. User reporting that they are facing lags and input delays. Issue only repro when timer interval changed to 1ms (starting teams/browser/VLC/etc) Once secure boot or VBS is disabled issue doesn't repro. Customer first involved Citrix, they build a test tool that changing timer and pushing on session lock due to pushing on win32k as Citrix calling MsgWaitForMultipleObjectsEx function (winuser.h) - Win32 apps | Microsoft Learn with QS_ALLINPUT as wakemask. In-house repro: Install windows 11/windows server 2025 Enable Hyper-v Install windows server 2025, enable nested virtualization Install windows server 2025 on nested VM <- issue can be reproduced on this VM Cause In windows server 2025 we can see from traces a lot of DPC calls - KiAbDeferredProcessingWorker This is due to code change in 2025. Article resolution Bug 57780645: JPMC Timer Interrupts - Microsoft and Broadcom Collaboration - Boards Temporary workaround for the customer - disable secure boot/VBS(virtualization based security) More information Traces that were very helpful in under understanding the issue: #xperf binary Download tss tool – aka.ms/gettss Extract it and and find in Bin folder two files – xperf.exe and perfctrl.dll on affected machine create C:\msdata folder and copy them over. Open elevated cmd and execute: C:\msdata\xperf -? C:\msdata\xperf -on proc_thread+loader+profile+interrupt+dpc+dispatcher+cswitch+timer+clockint -stackwalk Profile+CSwitch+ReadyThread -BufferSize 1024 -MinBuffers 128 -MaxBuffers 384 -MaxFile 4096 -FileMode Circular -start second -on "487d6e37-1b9d-46d3-a8fd-54ce8bdf8a53+Microsoft-Windows-Win32k+Microsoft-Windows-Winlogon+Microsoft-Windows-WMI-Activity+Microsoft-Windows-RPC" -BufferSize 1024 -MinBuffers 128 -MaxBuffers 384 -MaxFile 2048 -FileMode Circular Run Citrix tool for 20-30 seconds, repro input lag in notepad and then stop: C:\msdata\xperf -stop -stop second -d C:\msdata\%trace_name%.etl Notes: First published: Jun 10, 2025 Keywords: input lag, input slowness, KiAbDeferredProcessingWorker, autoboost

title: .NET 9.0 Update - June 10, 2025 (KB5061936) - Microsoft Support
content: NET 9.0 has been refreshed with the latest update as of June 10, 2025. This update contains both security and non-security fixes. See the release notes for details on updated packages. .NET 9.0 servicing updates are upgrades. The latest servicing update for 9.0 will remove the previous 9.0 update upon successful installation. For example, when .NET 9.0.6 is installed .NET 9.0.5 version will be removed from the computer if present. How to obtain and install the update This update is available on Microsoft Update for Windows client operating systems and available on WSUS and MU Catalog for Windows Server operating systems. Prerequisites This update will be offered if you have .NET 9.0 installed on a supported version of Windows. Restart Requirement You may need to restart the computer after you apply this update if any affected files are being used. We recommend that you exit all .NET based applications before you apply this update. Supported Windows Versions This page on .NET 9.0 Supported Windows Versions provides the most up-to-date details on the supported operating system versions. .NET Support Lifecycle This page on .NET Core and .NET 9 Support Policy provides the most up-to-date details on .NET Core Support Lifecycle Policy. How to obtain help and support for this update Microsoft Support For assisted support with .NET Core technologies, contact a Microsoft Support Professional. You need to be on a supported servicing level (the latest available servicing update) to be eligible for support. Community Support Community support is another great way to get help and even contribute to projects. See our Community page for details. More Information To get the latest .NET update, go to the Download .NET website

For more information about security vulnerabilities, please refer to the new Security Update Guide website and the May 2025 Security Updates. Windows 10 servicing stack update (KB5059504) - 19044.5911 and 19045.5911 Microsoft now combines the latest servicing stack update (SSU) for your operating system with the latest cumulative update (LCU). SSUs improve the reliability of the update process to mitigate potential issues while installing updates. This update makes quality improvements to the servicing stack, which is the component that installs Windows updates. To learn more about SSUs, see Servicing stack updates and Servicing Stack Updates (SSU): Frequently Asked Questions. Known issues in this update Noto fonts Symptoms There are reports of blurry or unclear CJK (Chinese, Japanese, Korean) text when displayed at 96 DPI (100% scaling) in Chromium-based browsers such as Microsoft Edge and Google Chrome. The March 2025 Preview Update introduced Noto fonts in collaboration with Google, for CJK languages as fallbacks to improve text rendering when websites or apps don’t specify appropriate fonts. The issue is due to limited pixel density at 96 DPI, which can reduce the clarity and alignment of CJK characters. Increasing the display scaling improves clarity by enhancing text rendering. Workaround Microsoft has shared its findings on the blurry text issue at 96 DPI, along with potential solutions with Google for further discussion. For additional support, users can report issues related to Noto CJK fonts through the official Google Noto Fonts GitHub repository. Surface Hub v1 Symptoms After installing this update for Windows 10, version 22H2, Surface Hub v1 devices might fail to start with error: “Secure Boot Violation: Invalid signature detected. Check Secure Boot Policy in Setup.” Surface Hub 2S and Surface Hub 3 are not impacted by this issue. Resolution This issue is fixed in update KB5063159. Update delay with deferral policies Symptoms Some devices in environments where IT admis use quality update (QU) deferral policies might experience delays in receiving the June 2025 Windows security update. Although the update was released on June 10, 2025, its update metadata timestamp reflects a date of June 20, 2025. This discrepancy might cause devices with configured deferral periods to receive the update later than expected. Workaround To accelerate deployment of the June 2025 updates, admins can take one of the following actions: Create an expedite policy to bypass deferral settings and deliver the update immediately if the organization is using Windows Autopatch. Adjust deployment rings or deferral configurations to reduce the delay window for affected devices. This delay issue affects only the timing of update availability for organizations using QU deferral policies and doesn't impact the quality or applicability of the update. We will not change the metadata value from the current June 20, 2025, value. This workaround is the final resolution we will provide for this issue. title: ADDS: SBSL: Slow logon delays due to drive map GPP settings on Windows Server 2022 running Citrix application
content: ADDS: SBSL: Slow logon delays due to drive map GPP settings on Windows Server 2022 running Citrix application Important: This was authored via https://aka.ms/contentidea. Follow Content Idea (CI) 201250 link for any updates. Author: Pruthviraju Dobaspet Summary/Symptom Our customer had Windows Server 2016 Terminal servers in their environment, and they are being now replaced by Windows Server 2022 Terminal servers (Citrix Servers). Our customer has observed a login delay in getting one of the GPO processing for mapping the Network Drives. The shares are hosted on NetApp Appliances and available via DFS Name spaces. Drive mapping works fine if the customer has rights to the share and network connectivity from the Remote Desktop host (Running Citrix Application) to the File share. However, the customer has noticed a considerable delay of 179328 milliseconds (2.9 minutes) to get on to the desktop. Cause After a long investigation with multiple sets of SBSL data, there were attempts made to use NetBIOS protocol on Port 443 and QUIC protocol on port 139. Initially, it was suggested to disable these protocols on Windows Server 2022, but this did not help. Further checking the new set of data, it was found that WebDAV communication is initiated on Windows Server 2022 RDS Server, which was not seen on Windows Server 2016 RDS Server. It was suggested to disable WebDAV components by disabling the “WebClient service” on the Windows Server 2022. Article resolution The delay-causing component was identified on this service request. Removing the WebDAV component on the RDS if not needed fixed the GPO processing delays on the server. The customer has seen a significant difference in the login time after disabling the “WebClient” Service on the server More information GPO operation log shows we take 160sec to apply GP Drive Maps CSE. description: Troubleshoot WordPress formatting issues on MSN, fix MSN HTML compatibility problems, and how to format custom styles correctly.
title: Troubleshoot MSN WordPress and custom formatting issues - Microsoft Support
content: If you're using WordPress on MSN or encountering formatting issues in your articles, this page outlines common problems with block compatibility, unsupported styles, and HTML rendering limitations. Why doesn’t my WordPress layout appear the same on MSN? MSN uses its own article template, which overrides WordPress styles. Layout blocks, theme widgets, and special formatting may be removed or converted during ingestion. Which WordPress blocks are supported? Common blocks like Headings, Paragraphs, Lists, Images, and Quotes are supported. Quote styles and special formatting blocks like Verse or Pullquote may lose styling. Why isn’t my audio embed working? Audio embeds from WordPress are not currently supported on MSN. You may need to convert audio into a video or include it on your original article page only. Can I use HTML to style my article? Yes, but only in the body or slide image description field. Disallowed tags will be removed, and deeply nested tags or inline styles may be stripped. Why do some of my embeds fail? MSN only supports certain embeds like Twitter, Facebook, and Instagram if they use HTTPS and follow the official embed code. Unsupported third-party widgets may be displayed as plaintext. Why do my line breaks or paragraph spacing disappear? Avoid using multiple tags or deeply nested divs. MSN may clean up extra breaks or misaligned spacing that affects readability.

description: Learn how to customize your settings and notifications for channels in Microsoft Teams to stay informed and organized, whether for all channels or specific
title: Manage channel notifications in Microsoft Teams  - Microsoft Support
content: There are two ways to adjust your settings and notifications for channels. Change Activity feed notifications for all channels Use these instructions to change Activity feed notifications for all your Posts and Threads layout channels across Teams. From the top of Teams, select Settings and more . Select Settings > Notifications and activity . From here, you can turn on or off notifications for replies to followed threads and posts or show them in the Activity feed and banner, or only the Activity feed. Change notifications for a specific channel ​​​​​​​​​​​​​​To the right of the channel name, select More options . Select Channel notifications . From here, you can turn on or off notifications for all new messages or posts (depending on layout). You can also choose to show notifications in the Activity feed and banner, or only the Activity feed. For channels in the Threads layout: Choose to Include thread replies if you want to be notified when other people reply to a post or message. Choose to Follow all new threads if you want to see new replies in Followed threads ​​​​​​​ at the top of your list of chats and channels. This setting won't notify you in the Activity feed. Related topics: Check a channel for notifications in Microsoft Teams Manage notifications in Microsoft Teams ​​​​​​​

title: Windows Server 2019: Machine shutdown with "Shutdown AD system because SS cache timer expired with no DSM connectivity"
content: Windows Server 2019: Machine shutdown with "Shutdown AD system because SS cache timer expired with no DSM connectivity" Important: This was authored via https://aka.ms/contentidea. Follow Content Idea (CI) 203438 link for any updates. Author: Ankita Singh Basu Summary/Symptom Customer has Server 2019 and when he logs in to the machine it shuts down within 2 - 3 minutes with a message "Shutdown AD system because SS cache timer expired with no DSM connectivity" However machine was booting in safe mdoe. Cause Issue was caused due to Secfsd service from "Thales Group". Article resolution We disabled Secfsd service from "Thales Group" from msconfig and issue was mitigated. More information Note: First published: Jun 26, 2025

title: June 26, 2025—KB5060829 (OS Build 26100.4484) Preview
content: <div> June 26, 2025—KB5060829 (OS Build 26100.4484) Preview For information about Windows update terminology, see types of Windows updates and the monthly quality update types. To find an overview, see the update history page for Windows 11, version 24H2. Follow @WindowsUpdate to find out when new content is published to the Windows release health dashboard. Note: Experience seamless device migration with Windows Backup for Organizations, now available for a limited public preview. This feature ensures a smooth transition to Windows 11 for new or reimaged Microsoft Entra joined devices. To learn more, see Announcing Windows Backup for Organizations. Highlights ​​​​​​​Gradual rollout A gradual rollout distributes a release update over a period of time, rather than all at once. This means that users receive the updates at different times, and it might not be immediately available to all users. To see the status of this feature, go to Windows release health dashboard.​​​​​​​​​​​​ [App defaults] New! We are rolling out some small changes in the European Economic Area (EEA) region for default browsers through the Set default button in Settings > Apps > Default apps: Additional file and link types will be set for the new default browser, if it registers them. The new default browser will be pinned to the Taskbar and Start menu unless you choose not to pin it by clearing the checkboxes. There is now a separate one-click button for browsers to change your .pdf default, if the browser registers for the .pdf file type. [Click to Do (Preview)] New! ​​​​​​​ Ask Microsoft 365 Copilot is a new action in Click to Do on Copilot+ PCs. Use it to send text or images to Microsoft 365 Copilot, which will respond to your questions. The Ask Microsoft 365 Copilot action requires a Microsoft 365 license and follows your organization’s privacy policies. [Narrator] New! The Screen Curtain feature in Narrator helps protect your privacy and improve focus by blacking out the screen while Narrator reads content aloud. This is especially helpful in public or shared spaces, where you can work with sensitive information without others seeing your screen. To turn on Narrator, press Ctrl + Windows + Enter. Then press Caps Lock + Ctrl + C to turn on Screen Curtain. While it’s on, you can use Narrator as usual with the screen hidden. Press Caps Lock + Ctrl + C again to turn it off. New! Narrator makes it easier to discover and learn about its features directly within the experience. Whether you're new or exploring advanced options, Narrator will guide you through the latest updates using a series of steps and prompts that explain each new feature and change. [PC Migration] New! ​​​​​​​ The PC-to-PC migration experience in Windows is starting to roll out. You’ll begin to see the landing and the pairing page in the Windows Backup app, giving you a first look at what’s coming. In the full experience, you’ll be able to transfer files and settings from an old PC to a new one during setup. Support for this feature during PC setup will arrive in a future update. The rollout is being introduced in phases to support a smooth experience. [Settings] ​​​​​​​New!​​​​​​​ We are starting to roll out the Settings homepage for commercial customers on PCs managed by an IT administrator. The feature will show some existing cards relevant to enterprise-managed PCs like “Recommended settings” and “Bluetooth devices” as well as two new enterprise-specific device info and accessibility preferences cards. For commercial customers who also use their Microsoft account on their managed PC, there will also be a new accounts card indicating the presence of both work and school and Microsoft account types. ​​​​​​​ New! The country or region selected during device setup now appears under Settings > Time & language > Language & region. Fixed: The storage card in Settings > System > About shows an incorrect or unreadable character instead of the proper disk size. [Taskbar & System Tray] New! ​​​​​​​ ​​​​​​​​​​​​​​The taskbar now resizes icons to fit more apps when space runs low, keeping everything visible and easy to access. You can adjust how icons appear in settings—reduce icon size only when the taskbar is full (default), keep icons at their original size at all times by selecting Never, or use smaller icons all the time by selecting Always. To change this setting, right-click an empty area on the taskbar, select Taskbar settings, expand the Taskbar behaviors section, and choose your preference under Show smaller taskbar buttons. New! In addition to the new grouping of the Accessibility menu in Quick settings, there are text descriptions for the assistive technologies like Narrator, Voice access, and more for easier identification and learning. New! Adjusted the indicator (pill) under taskbar apps to make it wider and more visible.​​​​​​​ Fixed: WIN + CTRL + Number doesn't work anymore for switching windows of an open app in the taskbar.​​​​​​​ Fixed: When using taskbar in Windows, the media controls that appear in the preview windows for apps might unexpectedly flicker. [Voice Access] New! You can now use Voice access to navigate, dictate, and interact with Windows using voice commands in Simplified Chinese and Traditional Chinese. New! You can add custom words to the dictionary in voice access. The feature will be available in all the currently supported voice access languages. [Windows Share] ​​​​​​​New! When you share links or web content using the Windows share window, you'll see a visual preview for that content. New! In the Windows share window, you can select a compression level—High, Medium, or Low Quality—when editing and sharing images, instead of selecting from a 0–100 scale. [Color] Improved: Adjusted the location of the intensity and color boost sliders under Settings > Accessibility > Color Filters, so the color previews at the top of the page remain visible while adjusting the sliders. [File Explorer] Improved: Performance has been enhanced when extracting archive files - this will particularly help in the case of copy pasting large numbers of files out of large 7z or .rar archives. [Graphics] Improved: Made underlying changes to enhance display related user experiences, including reducing screen flashing during certain display configuration transitions and eliminating unnecessary display resets that occurred in some cases​​​​​​​. Fixed: Some displays might be unexpectedly green. Fixed: If User Account Control (UAC) is set to Always Notify and the button under Settings > System > Display color calibration is selected for your display and canceled, Settings will stop responding. [Input] Fixed: Typing in Japanese with the touch keyboard might stop working after switching to typing with an English keyboard and then switching back. [MSFTEdit.dll] Fixed: Some apps like Sticky Notes and dxdiag might stop responding when the display language is set to Arabic or Hebrew display. [Quick Settings] Fixed: The top three buttons in the top row don’t respond when selecting to enable or disable them. [Printing] Fixed: Printed lines might be unexpectedly thicker than expected. Known issues in this update Noto fonts issue Applies to: All users Symptoms There are reports of blurry or unclear CJK (Chinese, Japanese, Korean) text when displayed at 96 DPI (100% scaling) in Chromium-based browsers such as Microsoft Edge and Google Chrome. The March 2025 Preview Update introduced Noto fonts in collaboration with Google, for CJK languages as fallbacks to improve text rendering when websites or apps don’t specify appropriate fonts. The issue is due to limited pixel density at 96 DPI, which can reduce the clarity and alignment of CJK characters. Increasing the display scaling improves clarity by enhancing text rendering. Workaround Microsoft has shared its findings on the blurry text issue at 96 DPI, along with potential solutions with Google for further discussion. For additional support, users can report issues related to Noto CJK fonts through the official Google Noto Fonts GitHub repository. Error events are logged for Windows Firewall Symptoms After installing this update, security event logs might include an error event related to Windows Firewall with Advanced Security, which can be safely ignored. The error is found in Event Viewer as event 2042 for Windows Firewall with Advanced Security. The event appears as "Config Read Failed" with the message "More data is available". Although this event is logged in every time the device restarts, it does not indicate a problem with Windows Firewall and can be disregarded. Windows Firewall is expected to function normally, and you don't need to take any action to prevent or resolve this error event. This event is related to a feature that is currently under development and not fully implemented. There is no impact to Windows processes associated with this event. Workaround​​​​​​​ This issue is addressed in KB5062660. title: testArticle - Microsoft Support
content: Start your article with a very short introduction (1 sentence). Put yourself in the reader's place - why are they here? What should they do? Get straight to a quick list of steps to accomplish If you need to explain a concept, or they have to do pre-requisite steps, add a quick summary below the step where they need it, and link to the concept or steps. Keep procedures short - preferably 5 or fewer steps Use Ui style for user interface elements or for text people need to enter. Use the verbs choose, select, or enter as actions, and format menus as Menu > Command. Optionally, add a screenshot for context (if UI is hard to locate, or it’s needed to complete the task). Maximum width: 520 pixels. Use a standard theme, do not show any personal information, and crop to show only what's relevant. If you want to add a video or screenshot, use a two-column grid and have the steps in the left and the video or screenshot in the right - see Steps and video grid example. Target no more than 500 words for an article. Example article Change my photo

title: Reading Coach language settings - Microsoft Support
content: Applies ToMicrosoft Teams Microsoft Teams for Education Language settings for 81 locales have been added to Reading Coach to help with the overall application experience, Paste a Passage, Create a Story, and Word Practice. With 81 different locales from around the world, the Reading Coach app is now better for learners seeking to navigate the app and better reading fluency in multiple languages. Reading Coach is a helpful tool available on the web at coach.microsoft.com and also available on the windows store. It helps you read better and say words correctly. Now, it works in more languages than just US English. This means you can navigate the application, and practice reading in other languages, not just your own. It helps people who are learning to read in a new language or trying to get better at a second language. Supported languages and locales Note: Reading Coach picks one main language for each place. For example, if you are in Mexico, it will use Spanish-Mexico. If you want to read in a different language, you need to change your browser and reading settings. This lets you use Reading Coach in the language you prefer. These languages are available now on Reading coach for Paste a Passage, Word Practice, and for the app itself. Create a story has a separate list of languages for it that are listed in the section below. (China): ug-CN Uzbek (Latin, Uzbekistan): uz-Latn-UZ Vietnamese (Vietnam): vi-VN Welsh (United Kingdom): cy-GB Multiple English dialects supported Learners can also now read in 14 different English dialects. Reading Coach will track your pronunciation all 14 of the English dialects listed below: English American (United States): en English Australian (Australia): en-au English Canadian (Canada): en-ca English Ghana (Ghana): en-gh English Great Britain (United Kingdom): en-gb English Hong Kong (Hong Kong): en-hk English India (India): en-in English Kenya (Kenya): en-ke English New Zealand (New Zealand): en-nz English Nigeria (Nigeria): en-ng English Philippine (Philippines): en-ph English Singapore (Singapore): en-sg English Tanzania (Tanzania): en-tz English South African (South Africa): en-za Paste a passage These new reading languages in 81 locales allow you to have content in one language but paste text for reading practice in another. You can also paste content in their native tongue as the application locale. For example, you can set your language settings to US English but paste a reading language in Spanish. Reading Coach's AI will recognize that this is content for Spanish and return an assessment of your performance graded accurately on your pronunciation. Now when you paste content written in a foreign language into the passage text box, Reading Coach's AI will detect the language of that content. (See the screenshot below.) Changing your reading language Choosing the button labeled with your current reading language will produce a pop-up window from which you can choose your preferred reading language from a dropdown menu. Create a story Language selection in 13 languages continues to be useful when learners are creating a story in Reading Coach. Learn more about creating a story.​​​​​​​ How to set reading language for creating a story Navigate to the Create a Story feature in reading coach. Choose the language button in the top right corner. Select a reading language from the dropdown menu. The language selection will take effect, translating the app features into content for the selected language. The screenshot above shows the selected language as "Spanish-Mexico" so all the text for the create a story feature including the names of the AI animal actors has changed to reflect that selection. The learner will be listened to in the chosen language. Supported languages for Create a Story Chinese (Taiwan): zh-tw Dutch (Netherlands): nl-nl English American (United States): en English Australian (Australia): en-au English Canadian (Canada): en-ca English Ghana (Ghana): en-gh English Great Britain (United Kingdom): en-gb English Hong Kong (Hong Kong): en-hk English India (India): en-in English Kenya (Kenya): en-ke English New Zealand (New Zealand): en-nz English Nigeria (Nigeria): en-ng English Philippine (Philippines): en-ph English Singapore (Singapore): en-sg English Tanzania (Tanzania): en-tz English South African (South Africa): en-za Filipino (Philippines): fil-ph French (France): fr-fr German (Germany): de-de Italian (Italy): it-it Japanese (Japan): ja-jp Korean (South Korea): ko-kr Portuguese (Portugal): pt-pt Spanish (Span): es-es Swedish (Sweden): sv-se Word Practice The evaluation happens while you are reading the passage aloud. The results of this evaluation are displayed on the final screen. Reading Coach will then allow learners to practice words they missed the most. Learners may choose a word they had difficulty pronouncing and practice using their device's built in microphone. The learner should press the microphone and read the word aloud. They may choose the speaker icon to hear the word said aloud by Sunny, an AI voice actor. ​​​​​​​

title: VAMT Setup with Remote SQL Connection reporting Error for Connection Closure
content: VAMT Setup with Remote SQL Connection reporting Error for Connection Closure Important: This was authored via https://aka.ms/contentidea. Follow Content Idea (CI) 164103 link for any updates. Author: Aashish Kamavisdar Summary/Symptom Issue VAMT Setup with Remote SQL Connection reporting Error for Connection Closure VAMT Proxy Activation for the ESU Endpoint with Remote SQL Configured, which is supported. Error while trying to acquire confirmation ID from VAMT Proxy Activation for the ESU Endpoint. VAMT servers will try to contact "activation.sls.microsoft.com" location to fetch the Installation ID for servers/clients in the environment which need activation. This is failing on multiple VAMT servers with an error indicating that the remote host closed the connection. The VAMT server would be talking to this destination URL over TCP port 443 - we also have a server from where this connection is successful. Network traces have been collected from both working and non-working VAMT servers. Cause We captured Network Traces & Identified that there was an Error due to TLS Version Mismatch. TCP 3-way handshake to this destination IP Address completes successfully. Without any delay, we see the VAMT server initiating closure by sending an ACK-FIN, to which the destination server responds with ACK-RST and connection is closed: Reviewing the Success Trace we Identified that after TCP Three Way Handshake, TLS Handshake is getting initiated by VAMT server and completing successfully For TLS communication, the expected behavior is that there should be a TLS Handshake between client and server, after the connection is established in TCP 3-way handshake. In the working scenario, we see the expected behavior and TLS handshake is successfully completing, post which app data is transferred. However, in the non-working scenario, we dont see the VAMT server initiating TLS Handshake -- TLS Client Hello is not being sent, instead the server is closing the connection with an ACK-FIN. We need to find why is TLS Handshake not getting initiated. One possibility could be if there is a TLS Version which is not enabled on the server - can compare the TLS versions on working and non-working VAMT servers. Engaged DS team to understand why is TLS handshake not getting initiated. Article resolution While comparing the logs and post enabling the TLS 1.0 on the affected server Issue got fixed. Additional Considerations: However, TLS 1.0 is not a secure protocol , if you want to disable TLS 1.0 please follow the best practices from the below document. https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/security/engineering/solving-tls1-problem And please enforce TLS 1.2 for the client by following this article https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/mem/configmgr/core/plan-design/security/enable-tls-1-2-client Also, ensure affected client must initiate TLS 1.2 traffic before disabling TLS 1.0. Notes: First published: May 15, 2025 Keywords: repub-2025-05-29

title: ADDS: PowerShell: Inconsistent PasswordLastSet date/time Format in AD User Export via PowerShell
content: ADDS: PowerShell: Inconsistent PasswordLastSet date/time Format in AD User Export via PowerShell Important: This was authored via https://aka.ms/contentidea. Follow Content Idea (CI) 202577 link for any updates. Author: Mukesh Agarwal Summary/Symptom When exporting Active Directory (AD) user data using PowerShell, the PasswordLastSet attribute appears in inconsistent formats across different user entries in the CSV output. This inconsistency can hinder readability and affect downstream reporting or auditing processes. Cause PowerShell’s default behavior when exporting DateTime properties like PasswordLastSet can lead to inconsistent formatting. This variation is influenced by system locale, regional settings, and how the DateTime object is serialized during export. Article resolution To ensure consistent formatting, use a refined PowerShell script that explicitly formats the PasswordLastSet field before exporting. The recommended format is yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss. More information Example of a script which can export PasswordLastSet value for users in consistent format- Import-Module ActiveDirectory $ExportPath = "C:\AD_Users_PasswordLastSet_Formatted.csv" Get-ADUser -Filter * -Properties SamAccountName, PasswordLastSet | Select-Object Name, SamAccountName, @{Name="PasswordLastSet";Expression={$_.PasswordLastSet.ToString("yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss")}} | Export-Csv -Path $ExportPath -NoTypeInformation -Encoding UTF8 Write-Host "Export complete. File saved to $ExportPath" Notes: First published: May 15, 2025 Keywords: ADUserExport, PowerShell, PasswordLastSet, Audit, DateFormat

title: ADDS: Tools: Klist.exe fails to display ticket cache; “Credentials cache C:\Users\xxx\krb5cc_xxx not found”
content: ADDS: Tools: Klist.exe fails to display ticket cache; “Credentials cache C:\Users\xxx\krb5cc_xxx not found” Important: This was authored via https://aka.ms/contentidea. Follow Content Idea (CI) 199899 link for any updates. Author: Gaurav Chavan Summary/Symptom You run “klist.exe” or “klist.exe tickets” in the user context, and expect to see the user’s Kerberos tickets, however, you get this error: “Credentials cache C:\Users\xxx\krb5cc_2280025 not found” You have validated that there are no Kerberos issues, and the client does appear to acquire and consume Kerberos tickets successfully. Additionally, other klist switches (like klist get SPN) also fail, with this message: Cause Note that these errors / messages are not from the Microsoft klist.exe (located under C:\Windows\System32\), but from a 3rd party version included in the Java Development Kit (JDK). The customer had installed Eclipse Adoptium JDK, which inserts its own path in the System variables: Since its path was placed higher than %SystemRoot%\System32, when they ran “klist.exe”, the JDK version was being launched instead of the built-in, Microsoft version. This can also be identified from a Procmon trace, filtered for “Process Create” activity: 8:11:14.1090991 AM cmd.exe 4524 Process Create C:\Program Files\Eclipse Adoptium\jdk-23.0.2.7-hotspot\bin\klist.exe SUCCESS PID: 6548, Command line: klist Article resolution Move the JDK path in the System variables below the default, Windows paths, so that when you call “klist.exe” from the command line, it launches the built-in, Microsoft version from the System32 folder. Notes: Support Topics: Windows\Windows 11\Windows 11 Enterprise and Education, version 24H2\Windows Security Technologies\Kerberos authentication First published: Mar 31, 2025 Keywords: Credentials cache C:\Users\xxx\krb5cc_xxx not found, klist, JDK

title: Windows Servicing: Understanding Windows Continuous Delivery (CD)
content: Windows Servicing: Understanding Windows Continuous Delivery (CD) Important: This was authored via https://aka.ms/contentidea. Follow Content Idea (CI) 201140 link for any updates. Author: Will Aftring Summary Short URL for this KB: https://aka.ms/howto-cd Windows Continuous Delivery (CD) is a new servicing delivery mechanism for Windows. As it is a new process, these items are subject to change. This document is to serve as an introduction to the process and OSGWiki should serve as the authoritative resource. If you have questions or concerns that are not covered in this KB, please reach out to the following folks so that they may update the KB accordingly. Email method 1 Email method 2 To: wiaftrin@microsoft.com; codoesch@microsoft.comSubject: Windows Servicing: Understanding Windows Continuous Delivery (CD) Questions Use the Mailto link HERE Growing Pains: It is important to acknowledge that CD is a very new process as a result there is lots of learning that will need to take place both within engineering and within CSS. Communicating to enterprise customers about CD fixes: The CD process will be mostly irrelevant to enterprise customers other than when a CD fixes' parent bundle is enabled by default. The internal process about requiring telemetry and internal branch testing is not relevant to customers and should not be shared. The enabled by default release date for the feature bundle that contains the fix in question is what should be communicated with enterprise customers. For example: If a bug is disabled by default in 3D, this information is not relevant to the customer as the timing may change without notice. If a bug is enabled by default in 3D, then it can be communicated that the change is likely to be available for them to leverage in the 4D / 5B Additionally, if a customer wants to enable the change early, see "How do I enable a CD fix early" Please note that the client and server SKU differences should be communicated clearly. If they have heard about the CD process already, then you can refer them to the public documentation around continuous innovation. Delivering continuous innovation in Windows 11 - Microsoft Support How do I know when my change is coming out? Work Item: In the CD work items, the release called out in the work item is the intended EnabledByDefault release date. The remaining text will use the following bug as an example: Bug 55641152: [Ge] Kerberos AP-REQ fails with STATUS_KDC_UNKNOWN_ETYPE when using RC4 due to new Kerb3961 behavior - Boards The release date is listed as "2025.03". In this case, the work item is slotted to be released EnabledByDefault in 3D. Meaning: The code change is in a feature preview state and will be broadly enabled as of 4D/5B on client SKUs or 8B on Server SKUs. From Code: When reviewing a work item in code you will need to know the specific feature AND branch you are curious about. Using Feature_Servicing_Kerb3961ApRepOfferKeys as an example. { "owner": "wiaftrin@microsoft.com", "BugId": 55641152, "Description": "Kerb3961 adds support for ApRepOffer keys to permit EType negotiation", "className": "Feature_Servicing_Kerb3961ApRepOfferKeys", "Stage": "DisabledByDefault", "DependsOn": [ { "FeatureStagingXmlName": "FeatureStaging-ContinuousDelivery", "ClassName": "Feature_Bundle_Future" } ]} This change is DisableByDefault meaning it is not yet ready to be enabled for end customers. DO NOT ATTEMPT TO ENABLE FEATURES IN THIS STATE UNLESS EXPLICITLY INFORMED BY OWNING DEV TEAM It is parented to Feature_Bundle_Future This means that as of the time of this check in, there is not a specific release date in code. The bug id is the work item that went through servicing and scheduling and can be used to determine a more authoritative time. { "owner": "wiaftrin@microsoft.com", "BugId": 55641152, "Description": "Kerb3961 adds support for ApRepOffer keys to permit EType negotiation", "className": "Feature_Servicing_Kerb3961ApRepOfferKeys", "Stage": "EnabledByDefault", "DependsOn": [ { "FeatureStagingXmlName": "FeatureStaging-ContinuousDelivery", "ClassName": "Feature_Bundle_2503" } ]} The change is in an EnabledByDefault state and will be enabled when the parent bundle is enabled. The depends on is set to Feature_Bundle_2503 meaning that in 3D it will go through a CFR rollout for non-enterprise customers. If you have a customer who would like to test this change while it is in the state, see "Enabling changes early." If the change does not have a release date in the work item, and it is bundled to Feature_Bundle_Future then there is no set release date. Follow up with the owner to clarify expectations. These release dates are subject to change at the discretion of both WSD and the owning dev. Lifecycle of a CD Work item: The largest difference between traditional servicing and CD is the mechanism in which the change will be enabled broadly. Here is the lifecycle of a change that will go through CD. This operates under the assumption that a change is needed in active branch (AB) as well. A code change is made and validated in AB The change is then placed behind containment. In code this is typically an if statement containing Feature_XXX::IsEnabled() Here is an example PR that shows this behavior: Pull request 12093571: [Kerb3961][CherryPick] Key usage for initiator listing allowed ApRep types - Repos The containment can be in a Json or an XML file depending on the team From there the change is flighted internally for at least 5 business days and needs to hit a specific usage threshold The change is flipped to EnabledByDefault and parented to a specific feature bundle When a change is in this state IT IS NOT ENABLED UNTIL THE PARENT BUNDLE IS ENABLED When referring to this state, it is useful to refer to this as "in feature preview" Here is an example PR: Pull request 12244586: [Kerb3961] Flipping Feature_Servicing_Kerb3961ApRepOfferKeys to EbD - Repos In the following D release, the feature bundle will be changed to enabled by default, broadly enabling the change. Delays in Enablement on Server SKUs: In the previous section it was discussed that the broad enablement of an EnabledByDefault change would occur in the following D release. This is true for Client SKUs but is NOT true for Server SKUs. There is a 3.5 release delay for the enablement of Server SKU CD changes. See the table below. CD Bundle Key Windows 11 24H2 (Client Edition) Windows Server 2025 (Server Edition) Release (N) D DisabledByDefault Release (N+1) B DisabledByDefault* Release (N+1) D EnabledByDefault <No Impact to Server> Release (N+4) B EnabledByDefault Example: I change is checked disabled by default in 2D It is changed to enabled by default in 3D The parent bundle is enabled in 4D On Server the change will be enabled by default in 8B This is outside of the control of the Windows component owner and is a decision that has been made by Windows Server leadership and is subject to change without any notice to CSS. Source: Delivering Windows via Continuous Delivery - OSGWiki CD Exceptions: If you believe that this timeline does not work for your customer, you can work with the dev owner to request a CD exception. This process MUST be started prior to the change being checked into a CD branch. The dev owner is responsible for filing and updating the status of the CD exception request in the work item. If you do not see this being done, please follow up with the dev owner. Ultimately, getting a CD exception is primarily under the discretion of the WSD owners of the component. If a work item is accepted for an exception thit will have the CD_Exception tag. How do I enable a CD fix early: There are two kinds of early CD fixes. Enabling the specific CD work item early This should rarely be the case. If a work item is in a DisabledByDefault state, it is not yet ready for customer usage and should be considered unsupported unless the owning dev specifies otherwise. Enabling the parent feature bundle early Regarding #2 this process is outlined here: Use Group Policy to enable a disabled by default update - Windows Client | Microsoft Learn You will need to download the appropriate feature preview enablement packages from "Preview GPs for CD Bundle Features/Bug Fixes" section of WSD Wiki-Enabling KIR preview fixes - OSGWiki: Client SKUs: Each bundle is enabled in the following month’s servicing update; in most cases, enabling the bundle with the fix will enable your feature Server SKUs: Each bundle is enabled in N+3.5 months (e.g. 2025.02D will be enabled in 2025.06B). Each bundle that hasn’t been enabled yet will need to be enabled for the feature to be enabled. For example, to enable a fix going in 2025.05D, 2025.05D, 2025.04D, and 2023.03D will need to be enabled. See Delivering Windows via Continuous Delivery - OSGWiki Frequently Asked Questions: Q: "Why does my bug need to go through CD? It's a one-line change?"A1: It doesn't matter. CD is the preferred way to send out updates. If you have an objection to this then you will need a CD exception. Q: "Why did the release date of my bug fix change?"A2: There are telemetry requirements in order to change a work items state from DisabledByDefault to EnabledByDefault. These telemetry requirements are not visible to CSS if you have questions, follow up with the owning dev or PM. These telemetry requirements must be met. If you have an objection to this then you will need a CD exception. Q: "What do I do if there is a regression?"A3: File an IcM with the owning team and they will create a KIR rollback GP. Q: "Why are we shipping these things disabled by default? We are just delaying the detection of regressions."A4: While that is possible there is internal flighting and validation that is done. Additionally, running CFRs provides the following benefits. Confirmation that rolling back the change will not introduce new issues. Any given change CAN be rolled back. Q:" Why do I need to wait on a CD change to go out if I need a fix in older OS versions?"A5: Changes cannot be backported until the owning feature team addresses the behavior. Prior to CD this was just an active branch, however, now feature teams' own CD servicing as well where it must go through the CD process before it can go out. This may lead to delays in work item fixes in non-CD OS versions. If you have an objection to this then you will need a CD exception. More information Additional Resources: Continuous Delivery - OSGWiki Delivering Windows via Continuous Delivery - OSGWiki OSGWIKI: WSD Wiki-Enabling KIR preview fixes Windows Payload Tracking EE-310 Continous Delivery for you and Me QA.COM: Introducing Continuous Delivery for Windows 11 and Windows Server 2025 (requires logon with "Microsoft" as domain logon and NOT "microsoft.com" to trigger Microsoft SSO) Microsoft-internal content created especially for customer-facing delivery partners, SEs and SEEs in the Windows Commercial part of CSS directly supporting enterprise customers needing to understand when and how continuous-delivery covered bug fixes and features will ship enabled-by-default. This content was created by Windows Commercial Readiness Engineer and Microsoft FTE Harley Henderson <harleyh@microsoft.com> on the QA.COM domain used for ALL official content created by the Microsoft Readiness team. Notes: First published: Apr 01, 2025 Keywords: wiaftrin, cd, windows

title: ConfigMgr: Client Health Check Failed due to vcredist- Error code- 1638
content: ConfigMgr: Client Health Check Failed due to vcredist- Error code- 1638 Important: This was authored via https://aka.ms/contentidea. Follow Content Idea (CI) 201085 link for any updates. Author: Rajesh Kumar Dash Summary/Symptom Client Check Failed due to Pre-requisite rule check Cause Client health check is failing on the step "client prerequisites". Which is failing to install/repair the vcredist. CCMEval.log 02-25-2025 11:50:01.519 CcmEval 4684 (0x124c) Evaluating health check rule {2F373187-6295-4CBB-BE9E-8E43C459883A} : Verify/Remediate client prerequisites. 02-25-2025 11:57:02.272 CcmEval 4684 (0x124c) Client or client prerequisite evaluation failed. 02-25-2025 12:13:40.127 CcmEval 4684 (0x124c) Client or client prerequisite installation remediation failed. 02-25-2025 12:13:40.127 CcmEval 4684 (0x124c) Please check ccmsetup-ccmeval.log for further information. 02-25-2025 12:29:29.313 CcmEval 4684 (0x124c) Client health check: FAILED 02-25-2025 12:22:45.252 ccmsetup 12840 (0x3228) Installing file 'C:\WINDOWS\ccmsetup\vcredist_x86.exe' with options '/norestart /install /quiet /log %windir%\ccmsetup\logs\VCRedist_x86_Install.log'. 02-25-2025 12:22:45.903 ccmsetup 12840 (0x3228) File 'C:\WINDOWS\ccmsetup\vcredist_x86.exe' returned failure exit code 1638. Fail the installation. 02-25-2025 12:22:46.524 ccmsetup 12840 (0x3228) InstallFromManifest failed 0x80070666 01-01-0001 00:00:00.000 [083C:83B4][2025-02-25T12:22:45]e000: Error 0x80070666: Cannot install a product when a newer version is installed. 01-01-0001 00:00:00.000 [083C:79E8][2025-02-25T12:22:45]i500: Shutting down, exit code: 0x666 If we translate this MSI error code, it means Error Code: 0x666 (1638) Error Name: ERROR_PRODUCT_VERSION Error Source: Msi.h Error Message: Another version of this product is already installed. Installation of this version cannot continue. To configure or remove the existing version of this product, use Add/Remove Programs on the Control Panel. From the above log analysis, VCRedist is coming as not detected based on installer check in registry {D7A66DA5-B103-45C1-A0A7-736C08E2F464}, which is why it's trying to install it as part of remediation. And it fails because the version ConfigMgr is using the lower version of VCRedist. However the version which is installed is somehow corrupted or not properly installed since the registry itself is missing. As a result ConfigMgr is unable to detect VCRedist is installed. HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\{D7A66DA5-B103-45C1-A0A7-736C08E2F464} HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Wow6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\{D7A66DA5-B103-45C1-A0A7-736C08E2F464} Article resolution Uninstall the existing version and let CCMEval install the VCRedist as part of Remediation.OR Uninstall and reinstall VCRedist and ensure the uninstaller registries are present after reinstallation. More information Contact RADASH for comments/feedback

title: Computer Policy: Windows Settings: Security Settings: Local Policies: Security Options: System objects: Strengthen default permissions of internal system objects (e.g., Symbolic Links)
content: Computer Policy: Windows Settings: Security Settings: Local Policies: Security Options: System objects: Strengthen default permissions of internal system objects (e.g., Symbolic Links) Important: This was authored via https://aka.ms/contentidea. Follow Content Idea (CI) 201213 link for any updates. Author: Jason Epperly Summary System objects: Strengthen default permissions of internal system objects (e.g., Symbolic Links) This security setting determines the strength of the default discretionary access control list (DACL) for objects. Active Directory maintains a global list of shared system resources, such as DOS device names, mutexes, and semaphores. In this way, objects can be located and shared among processes. Each type of object is created with a default DACL that specifies who can access the objects and what permissions are granted. If this policy is enabled, the default DACL is stronger, allowing users who are not administrators to read shared objects but not allowing these users to modify shared objects that they did not create. Default: Enabled

description: Find out supported file formats by Microsoft Copilot and how to upload files to use your AI assistant for everyday life.
title: File upload in Microsoft Copilot - Microsoft Support
content: Note: Information on this page applies to Microsoft Copilot. If you're using Microsoft 365 Copilot for work, please see File formats supported by Microsoft 365 Copilot. File upload in Microsoft Copilot allows users to upload images or certain supported file types directly into their chat sessions. Once uploaded, Copilot can analyze and extract information from these files to provide relevant insights, answer questions, or assist with specific tasks. Files you share with Copilot will be stored securely for up to 18 months and then automatically deleted. Microsoft does not use the content of the files you upload to Copilot for model training. Supported file formats Microsoft Copilot supports the following file formats, including: Documents: PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX Images: PNG, JPEG, PJP, JFIF Text & Markup: TXT, TEXT, JSON, CSV, MD You can upload up to 20 files in a single Copilot conversation. Files that can be uploaded to are limited to 50MB. How to use file upload Upload a file to Copilot using the following steps: Press the Open icon (+) and select Add images or files. Use the file picker to navigate to and select the file you want to upload on your device. Once uploaded, the file will appear as an attachment in your chat session. Type and submit a prompt that asks a question about the file, e.g. “describe this image” or “what recommendations would you give based on this document?” You can also ask follow-up questions about the file within the same conversation. Example prompts with file upload Here are some prompt ideas to get you started with File Upload: After uploading a resume: Can you help me write a cover letter I can send to the hiring manager for this entry-level marketing role? Call out my relevant experiences. After uploading a report: Give me a summary of this report and its top three recommendations. Also, provide an APA-style citation for this report I can use in an article I am writing.

title: April 8, 2025-Security and Quality Rollup for .NET Framework 4.8 for Windows Server 2008 R2 SP1 (KB5055171) - Microsoft Support
content: Applies To.NET Applies to: Microsoft .NET Framework 4.8 End of support information Windows Server 2008 R2 SP1 Extended Security Updates (ESU) third and final year ended on January 10, 2023. Additionally, Extended Security Updates on Azure only support ended on January 9, 2024. For more information, see Extended Security Updates for Windows Server overview. We recommend that you upgrade to a later version of Windows Server. For more information, see Overview of Windows Server upgrades. Summary The April 8, 2025 update for Windows Server 2008 R2 SP1 includes cumulative security and reliability improvements in .NET Framework 4.8. Note Starting in July 2020, there will no longer be optional, non-security releases (known as "C" releases) for this operating system. Operating systems in extended support have only cumulative monthly security updates (known as the "B" or Update Tuesday release). Verify that you have installed the required updates listed in the How to get this update section before installing this update. Customers who have purchased the Extended Security Update (ESU) for on-premises versions of these operating systems must follow the procedures in KB4522133 to continue receiving security updates after extended support ends on January 14, 2020. For more information on ESU and which editions are supported, see KB4497181. For more information, see the ESU blog. Security Improvements There are no new security improvements in this release. This update is cumulative and contains all previously released security improvements. Quality and Reliability Improvements WPF1 - Addresses an issue with printing large number of pages due to an OutOfMemory exception. .NET Fundamentals - Addresses an issue where System.IO APIs are used to operate on files and directories on UNC shares. 1Windows Presentation Foundation (WPF) Additional information about this update The following articles contain additional information about this update as it relates to individual product versions. 5055684 Description of the Security and Quality Rollup for .NET Framework 3.5.1, 4.6.2, 4.7, 4.7.1, 4.7.2, 4.8 for Windows Server 2008 R2 SP1 (KB5055684) Known issues in this update Microsoft is not currently aware of any issues in this update. How to get this update Before installing this update To apply this update, you must have .NET Framework 4.8 installed. You must install the updates listed below and restart your device before installing the latest Rollup. Installing these updates improves the reliability of the update process and mitigates potential issues while installing the Rollup and applying Microsoft security fixes. We strongly recommend that you install the latest servicing stack update (SSU) for your operating system before installing the latest Rollup. SSUs improve the reliability of the update process to mitigate potential issues while installing the Rollup and applying Microsoft security fixes. For general information about SSUs, see Servicing stack updates and Servicing Stack Updates (SSU): Frequently Asked Questions. If you use Windows Update, the latest SSU (KB5039339) will be offered to you automatically. To get the standalone package for the latest SSU, search for it in the Microsoft Update Catalog. Language packs If you install a language pack after you install this update, you must reinstall this update. Therefore, we recommend that you install any language packs that you need before you install this update. For more information, see Add language packs to Windows. This update will be downloaded and installed automatically from Windows Update if you are an ESU customer. title: Unable to Set Cloud Witness. Error: The Client and Server Cannot Communicate, Because They do Not Possess a Common Algorithm
content: Unable to Set Cloud Witness. Error: The Client and Server Cannot Communicate, Because They do Not Possess a Common Algorithm Important: This was authored via https://aka.ms/contentidea. Follow Content Idea (CI) 201420 link for any updates. Author: Gregory Mourougandy Summary/Symptom cx needs to have windows cluster with cloud witness. “The client and server cannot communicate, because they do not possess a common algorithm” which cx received while adding cloud witness. Cx was following below documentation: hhttps://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/failover-clustering/deploy-quorum-witness Cause The communication between storage account and cluster nodes happens on using TLS 1.0. The error appeared because TLS 1.0 was disabled on the server. To overcome this, we can use below PowerShell commands to use TLS1.2 for cloud quorum setup. Article resolution Ensure that both the client and server are configured to use TLS 1.2. You can enable TLS 1.2 on the server using the following PowerShell commands: [Net.ServicePointManager]::SecurityProtocol = [Net.SecurityProtocolType]::Tls12 Set-ClusterQuorum -Cluster ClusterName -CloudWitness -AccountName "NameOfStorageAccount" -AccessKey "AccessKeyForStorageAccount"
