description: Remove the "Read-Only" attribute from `machine.config` to fix Windows Server 2022 upgrade failure.
title: Upgrade | Windows Server 2016 to 2022 Upgrade Fails Due to Read-Only Machine.config File
content: Upgrade | Windows Server 2016 to 2022 Upgrade Fails Due to Read-Only Machine.config File AI-assisted content. This article was partially created/improved with the help of AI. An author reviewed and revised the content as needed. Learn more Important: This was authored via https://aka.ms/Rubik. Follow Rubik 5993 link for any updates. Author: Esterlin Aleman When upgrading from Windows Server 2016 to Windows Server 2022, the process may fail and revert to the previous version. This article provides details on the issue, its causes, and steps to resolve it. Symptoms During the upgrade attempt, the process fails, and the server reverts to Windows Server 2016. The following error is logged in the registry at HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\Setup\setupdiag\results: Error Found AdvancedInstaller failure. Last Phase: Pre SysPrep Last Operation: Upgrade securityExecutable: WFServicesReg.exe Exit Code: 2147500037 Phase: 38 Mode: Install (first install) Component: NetFx35CDF-CDF_GenericCommands, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=31bf3856ad364e35, ProcessorArchitecture=amd64 Additionally, the setup log located at C:\$WINDOWS.~BT\Sources\Panther\setupact.log contains the following errors: 2025-05-05 11:05:35, Error CSI 00000232 (F) Done with generic command 115; CreateProcess returned 0, CPAW returned S_OK Process exit code 2147500037 resulted in success? false Process output: [l:511 [511'DDSet_Entry: WFServicesReg.exe DDSet_Status: CFxInstaller::CopyConfigFilesToTemp is64bit=1 DDSet_Status: CFileHelper::CopyConfigFilesToTempLocation DDSet_Error: CFileHelper::CheckIsWriteable C:\WINDOWS\Microsoft.NET\Framework64\v2.0.50727\config\machine.config is read only. DDSet_Error: _fileHelper->CopyConfigFilesToTempLoca[gle=0x80004005] 2025-05-05 11:05:35, Error CSI tion failed. Error code: 0x80004005 DDSet_Error: Failed to copy config files to temp directory. Error code: 0x80004005 DDSet_CARetVal: -2147467259 DDSet_Exit: WFServicesReg.exe '][gle=0x80004005] 2025-05-05 11:05:35, Info CSI 00000233 Direct SIL provider: Number of files opened: 1. 2025-05-05 11:05:35, Error [0x018007] CSI 00000234 (F) Failed execution of queue item Installer: Generic Command ({81a34a10-4256-436a-89d6-794b97ca407c}) with HRESULT HRESULT_FROM_WIN32(14109). Failure will not be ignored: A rollback will be initiated after all the operations in the installer queue are completed; installer is reliable[gle=0x80004005] Cause The issue occurs because the file C:\WINDOWS\Microsoft.NET\Framework64\v2.0.50727\config\machine.config has the "Read-Only" attribute enabled. This prevents the upgrade process from modifying the file, causing the upgrade to fail. Resolution To resolve this issue, follow these steps: Navigate to the directory C:\WINDOWS\Microsoft.NET\Framework64\v2.0.50727\config\. Locate the file named machine.config. Right-click the file and select Properties. Under the General tab, uncheck the Read-Only attribute. Click OK to save the changes. Retry the upgrade process. After disabling the "Read-Only" attribute, the upgrade should complete successfully. More information Notes: First published: May 21, 2025 Keywords: CreatedByRubik Tags: Rubik Article Id: 5993 Support Topics: Windows Servers\Windows Server 2016\Windows Server 2016\Windows Setup, Upgrade and Deployment\Installing or upgrading Windows

title: Intune : How to retrieve Intune managed app version through PowerShell
content: Intune : How to retrieve Intune managed app version through PowerShell Important: This was authored via https://aka.ms/contentidea. Follow Content Idea (CI) 202800 link for any updates. Author: Aanand Jha Summary/Symptom To fetch the version of a managed app using PowerShell in an Intune-managed environment, you generally use the Microsoft Graph API. Cause Reviewed all available output properties, including AdditionalProperties, but couldn’t locate any field corresponding to the app version. Article resolution I recommend trying the following query: Module --> Microsoft.Graph.Beta.Devices.CorporateManagement (Get-MgBetaDeviceAppManagementMobileApp -MobileAppId "MOBILEAPPID").AdditionalProperties Reference: In the base command, version details are not provided by default. You need to add an additional parameter function to retrieve the version information. Expand property capability is not supported because additional property values or attributes are dictionary types, attributes, or objects, not string objects. Since expand property only works with string-type objects, using it alongside additional properties in the same command line will not work. Instead, a second command line is required, where you specify the base command followed by brackets and '.additionalProperties' to get the output.

content: Windows Search Not Working in "OneDriveSynced" Folders on Windows 11 23H2 machines Important: This was authored via https://aka.ms/contentidea. Follow Content Idea (CI) 200368 link for any updates. Author: Saisrinivas Chikoti Summary/Symptom Reported on: Windows 11 23h2 Machines Reported Symptoms: When an end user searches within File Explorer for a file or folder in a OneDrive-synced folder, no results are displayed. Other information: Windows Search and File Explorer search function normally without any issues. We rebuilt the index, and under Indexing Options, OneDrive appears to be indexed under the Users directory. Additionally, Cloud Content Search is enabled. Problem snippet : OneDrive Sync folder problem snippet: Cause We gathered Search ETL traces and Process Monitor logs during the reproduction of the issue by creating a test folder. A test folder was created, and three different file types were moved into it. These files were then hydrated by selecting "Always keep on this device" before stopping the logs. Log Analysis: Converted and merged the ETL traces. It shows successful indexing for all 3 different files in "Test folder" [Microsoft-Windows-Search-Core/Diagnostic] ITrans=0x272B0ABCB20, ResID=0x5DF1, Status=0x2, Type=0x1, Flags=0x8100017D, InternalFlags=0x4, CrawlNumber=0xFFFFFFFF, CrawlType=0x0, Extra1=0xF5B, Extra2=0x0, Extra3=0x0, Path=file:C:/Users/XXXX/OneDrive - AXA_OLD/Documents/Quiz - Windows Edition - XXXXXX.docx [Microsoft-Windows-Search-Core/Diagnostic] DocID=53127, URL=C:\[a0bb3b87-872f-47aa-ab86-2dadb40c39ea]\Users\XXXX\OneDrive - AXA\TEST\XXXX.xlsx, Info=ProcessDataChange - EXTERNAL Notification on existing URL received (MODIFY) scope:1962 [Microsoft-Windows-Search-Core/Diagnostic] ITrans=0x272AC302F60, ResID=0xCF87, Status=0x4, Type=0x2, Flags=0xA1100175, InternalFlags=0x0, CrawlNumber=0xFFFFFFFF, CrawlType=0x0, Extra1=0x0, Extra2=0x0, Extra3=0x0, Path=file:C:/Users/XXXX/OneDrive - AXA/TEST/XXXXXX.xlsx [Microsoft-Windows-Search-Core/Diagnostic] ITrans=0x272B270DD60, ResID=0xAD78, Status=0x2, Type=0x1, Flags=0x8110817D, InternalFlags=0x4, CrawlNumber=0xFFFFFFFF, CrawlType=0x0, Extra1=0x2, Extra2=0x494E4458, Extra3=0x0, Path=file:C:/Users/XXXX/OneDrive - AXA/TEST FOLDER/XXX.txt Procmon : Search indexer querying the Test folder and it show success too: SearchIndexer.exe 16228 CreateFile C:\Users\XXXX\OneDrive - AXA\TEST SUCCESS Desired Access: Read Attributes, Disposition: Open, Options: Open Reparse Point, Attributes: n/a, ShareMode: Read, Write, Delete, AllocationSize: n/a, OpenResult: Opened SearchIndexer.exe 16228 QueryBasicInformationFile C:\Users\XXXX\OneDrive - AXA\TEST SUCCESS CreationTime: 2/28/2025 3:46:07 PM, LastAccessTime: 2/28/2025 4:16:33 PM, LastWriteTime: 2/28/2025 3:46:49 PM, ChangeTime: 2/28/2025 4:16:33 PM, FileAttributes: RDARP 0x80000 S earchIndexer.exe 16228 CloseFile C:\Users\XXXX\OneDrive - AXA\TEST SUCCESS We see an error in the ETL logs: 0x80070057 QueryText=SELECT WorkId, System.ParsingName, System.ItemNameDisplay, System.SFGAOFlags, System.ItemType, System.ThumbnailCacheId, System.Kind, System.Search.Rank, System.ItemTypeText, System.ItemFolderPathDisplayNarrow, Path, System.FileAttributes, System.DateModified, System.DateCreated, System.DateAccessed, System.Size FROM SystemIndex WHERE NOT System.Shell.SFGAOFlagsStrings = SOME ARRAY['superhidden'] AND System.Shell.OmitFromView != 'true' AND (Scope = 'file:C:/Users/XXX/OneDrive - AXA') ORDER BY System.Search.Rank DESC, System.DateModified DESC, System.ItemNameDisplay ASC, ErrorCode=0x80070057 0x80070057 -2147024809 E_INVALIDARG However, the procmon does not show any errors interestingly. Article resolution Later, we collected TTD traces for the explorer.exe and SearchIndexer.exe processes. These traces revealed that the Local ID data was incorrect. 0:005> dv Locale = 0x7d0 0:005> ?0x7d0 Evaluate expression: 2000 = 00000000`000007d0 This locale ID is not valid, the valid one is 0x2000 (8192) TransientLangId is set to wrong value: which is 2000: which shows in process monitor too: We went to the path: - HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Control Panel\International\User Profile\en-BE Wrong Value: 0x7d0( 2000) The correct value for en-BE is 0x2000 (8192 in decimal) And changed the value to 0x2000 (8192 in decimal) shown in below snippet: Then later, rebooted the machine. The Search works as expected in the OneDrive Sync folder. A heartfelt thank you to EE, Pablo (pgavela@microsoft.com) for his invaluable assistance in analyzing the logs and guiding in the right direction to resolve the issue. More information Search ETL Commands: To start the Trace: logman create trace "enduser_MSSearch2" -ow -o c:\enduser_MSSearch2.etl -p "Microsoft-Windows-Search" 0xffffffffffffffff 0xff -nb 16 16 -bs 1024 -mode Circular -f bincirc -max 4096 -ets logman update trace "enduser_MSSearch2" -p "Microsoft-Windows-Search-ProfileNotify" 0xffffffffffffffff 0xff -ets logman update trace "enduser_MSSearch2" -p {2955E23C-4E0B-45CA-A181-6EE442CA1FC0} 0xffffffffffffffff 0xff -ets logman update trace "enduser_MSSearch2" -p "Microsoft-Windows-Search-ProtocolHandlers" 0xffffffffffffffff 0xff -ets logman update trace "enduser_MSSearch2" -p "Microsoft-Windows-Search-Core" 0xffffffffffffffff 0xff -ets To stop the Trace: logman stop "enduser_MSSearch2" -ets TTD Tracing: tttracer -attach <explorer.exe PID> tttracer -attach <SearchIndexer.exe PID> Windows: Windows Search overview Windows: Search: Guidance and initial troubleshooting for Windows Search https://dev.azure.com/Supportability/SharePointOnline/_wiki/wikis/SharePointOnline/1285065/Windows-desktop-search-not-returning-OneDrive-contents-(VDI) Notes: Support Topics: Windows\Windows 11 SR Number: 2502201420001312 First published: Mar 13, 2025 Keywords: Onedrivesearch, Onedrivesync

title: Make Exceptions for certain fonts when using GPO to BLOCK UNTRUSTED FONTS
content: Make Exceptions for certain fonts when using GPO to BLOCK UNTRUSTED FONTS Important: This was authored via https://aka.ms/contentidea. Follow Content Idea (CI) 200515 link for any updates. Author: Harshal Pardeshi Summary/Symptom Customer was using GPO Untrusted Font Blocking but Adobe uses Creative Cloud which does not download font files locally to known locations.Customer wanted help to exclude Adobe Creative Cloud so that he could use any fonts downloaded from the Adobe CC. Article resolution Microsoft Suggests having fonts placed in the %windir%\fonts folder rather than the exclusions. However, customer could not do this to multiple systems given he wouldn't which fonts would be downloaded by the user So, we suggested the customer to use exclusions for the given software for their fonts to be not blocked We found out using process explorer that Adobe CC uses the binary Coresync.exe when the font download process is initiated and the Adobe CC fonts are downloaded to the below folder C:\Users\<your user name>\AppData\Roaming\Adobe\CoreSync\plugins\livetype\r Adobe suggests removing the policy to block untrusted fonts completely which wasn't acceptable to the customer. With Further testing we suggested the customer to use the below exclusion steps We enrolled into a Adobe CC trial and added below active fonts in creative cloud Solitas Serif Tuna GPO to block untrusted fonts was enabled no newer events could be seen about the fonts being blocked as we already made the below exclusions in registry The blocking untrusted fonts feature - Windows Client | Microsoft Learn HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Image File Execution Options\Coresync.exe Add QWORD (64-bit) Value, naming it as MitigationOptions. Add the value for the setting desired for that process: To turn on this feature, type 1000000000000. To turn off this feature, type 2000000000000 <= I used this option to allow the blocked fonts for this process To audit with this feature, type 3000000000000. This helped customer achieve the desired result and he could deploy the same exclusions registry to multiple devices using GPP. More information The blocking untrusted fonts feature - Windows Client | Microsoft Learn Block untrusted fonts in an enterprise | Microsoft Learn Notes: Support Topics: Windows First published: Mar 16, 2025 Tags: Explorer, EXPLORER.EXE, font, fonts, GPO

title: ADDS: Security: LSASS crash (0xc0000409) when Kerberos accesses a file share due to corrupt list on Windows 11 24H2 / Windows Server 2025
content: ADDS: Security: LSASS crash (0xc0000409) when Kerberos accesses a file share due to corrupt list on Windows 11 24H2 / Windows Server 2025 Important: This was authored via https://aka.ms/contentidea. Follow Content Idea (CI) 200092 link for any updates. Author: Ryan Ries Summary/Symptom A Windows 11 24H2 client or Windows Server 2025 machine attempts to access a file share, and lsass crashes. Subsequently the machine reboots. The user may not realize what the trigger is and it may appear as though the machine is crashing randomly. This occurs on machines that are fully up to date (as of the time of this writing) with the February 2025 hotfix. A crash has been observed when accessing a cloud (AAD) file share, and also crashing while accessing an onprem file share. Both scenarios appear to be affected. Exception details c0000409 STATUS_FAIL_FAST_EXCEPTION Subcode: 0x3 FAST_FAIL_CORRUPT_LIST_ENTRY A crash dump of lsass reveals the following: DbgID ThreadID User Kernel Create Time (UTC)10 3450 (0n13392) 3s.296 3s.234 02/27/2025 06:14:03.616 AM # Call Site Info 0 kerberos!RtlFailFast+0x5 1 kerberos!FatalListEntryError+0x5 2 kerberos!InsertHeadList+0xe 3 kerberos!KerbCacheKdcProxyCacheEntry+0x72 4 kerberos!KerbInitializeCloudKerbFromAsRepCredential+0x5e5 5 kerberos!KerbConsumeAsRepCallbackAndInitializeCloudKerb+0x7a 6 kerberos!KerbQuerySpnOracle+0x92 7 kerberos!KerbGetServiceTicketInternal+0xa01 8 kerberos!KerbGetServiceTicketEx+0xce Ticket: cifs/pii_removed.file.core.windows.net@ 9 kerberos!KerbGetServiceTicket+0x7b a kerberos!SpInitLsaModeContext_Old+0x2f2c b lsasrv!WLsaProcessContext+0x73d c lsasrv!WLsaInitContext+0x97 d lsasrv!NegBuildRequestToken+0xa9f e lsasrv!NegGenerateInitialToken+0x56 f lsasrv!NegInitLsaModeContext+0x8c910 lsasrv!NegInitLsaModeContextEx+0xea11 lsasrv!WLsaProcessContext+0x73d12 lsasrv!WLsaInitContext+0xcc13 lsasrv!SspiExProcessSecurityContext+0x60414 sspisrv!SspirProcessSecurityContext+0x25215 rpcrt4!Invoke+0x7316 rpcrt4!Ndr64StubWorker+0x6ee17 rpcrt4!NdrServerCallAll+0x3c18 rpcrt4!DispatchToStubInCNoAvrf+0x1719 rpcrt4!RPC_INTERFACE::DispatchToStubWorker+0x1941a rpcrt4!RPC_INTERFACE::DispatchToStub+0x8b91b rpcrt4!LRPC_SBINDING::DispatchToStub+0x8b91c rpcrt4!LRPC_SCALL::DispatchRequest+0xaa81d rpcrt4!LRPC_SCALL::QueueOrDispatchCall+0xe41e rpcrt4!LRPC_SCALL::HandleRequest+0x2ba Client: PID: 0x4 TID: 0x44301f rpcrt4!LRPC_SASSOCIATION::HandleRequest+0x24620 rpcrt4!LRPC_ADDRESS::HandleRequest+0x3ac21 rpcrt4!LRPC_ADDRESS::ProcessIO+0x2f322 rpcrt4!LrpcIoComplete+0xc823 ntdll!TppAlpcpExecuteCallback+0x3b424 ntdll!TppWorkerThread+0x56325 kernel32!BaseThreadInitThunk+0x1726 ntdll!RtlUserThreadStart+0x2c 0:007> ?? LogonSession->PrimaryCredentials.KdcProxyCache.Initializedunsigned char 0x00 '' TTD is impossible due to the virtual machines having RunAsPPL enabled with UEFI lock, and RunAsPPL cannot be disabled because it would require running the UEFI opt-out tool and it would require physical access to the machine at a very early phase during boot, which is not possible in an AVD environment. lsass crashes while attempting to acquire a Kerberos service ticket for cifs/pii_removed.file.core.windows.net. When lsass attempts to acquire this Kerberos service ticket, it first looks in the local SPN cache. It did not find the cache entry there, so it goes on to query the SPN Oracle. This of course is an Azure endpoint that requires Cloud Kerb and so the KDC proxy is a login.microsoftonline.com/tenant-id/kerberos URL. So now we have a cache entry for the KDC Proxy cache so we try to add that cache entry to the KDC Proxy cache. Problem is, that cache is uninitialized. In the simplest terms we attempt to add an object to an uninitialized linked list, and this makes lsass explode. KerbInitKdcProxyCache must be called prior to adding anything to this cache. KerbCleanupKdcProxyCache unitializes the cache. Probably every time the cache is emptied out. But it seems we have a race condition where someone has called the uninitialize function first, then we try to add something new to the list without re-initializing the list first. Cause I have proposed the following to fix to the crash from VOIDKerbCacheKdcProxyCacheEntry( __in PKDC_PROXY_CACHE KdcProxyCache, __inout PKDC_PROXY_CACHE_ENTRY CacheEntry ){ D_DebugLog((DEB_TRACE_KDC, "cache proxy cache entry %p for domain %wZ\n", CacheEntry, &CacheEntry->DomainName)); KerbLockKdcProxyCache(); InsertHeadList( &KdcProxyCache->CacheEntries.List, &CacheEntry->ListEntry.Next ); KerbUnlockKdcProxyCache();} To this: VOIDKerbCacheKdcProxyCacheEntry( __in PKDC_PROXY_CACHE KdcProxyCache, __inout PKDC_PROXY_CACHE_ENTRY CacheEntry ){ D_DebugLog((DEB_TRACE_KDC, "cache proxy cache entry %p for domain %wZ\n", CacheEntry, &CacheEntry->DomainName)); NT_ASSERTMSG("KdcProxyCache->Initialized == TRUE", KdcProxyCache->Initialized); KerbLockKdcProxyCache();if (KdcProxyCache.Initialized) { InsertHeadList( &KdcProxyCache->CacheEntries.List, &CacheEntry->ListEntry.Next ); } KerbUnlockKdcProxyCache();} This safeguard is already in place in several other functions through the same source code file. Article resolution Track related bugs. Install corrective or preventative OS versions or OS updates as they become available OS Bug # Resolving KB Release Date Comments VNEXT \ Active Branch 57576500 RTM RTM Windows 11 24H2 56488103 (DBD)56488103 (EBD)56488103 (EBD) KB5064081 <TBD><TBD> 2025 8D 2025 9D on client SKU2026 1B on Server SKUs 2025 8D KB5064081 released to WUC on August 29, 2026 disabled by default. That fix will be flighted from 0 to 100% enablement on WIn11 24H2 clients over the next 30 days with full enblement triggered by the installation of 9D.25. Current thinking is that this fix will not be enabled by default on WS 2025 Server SKUs until 1B.26. This fix shipped disabled by default in Windows Updates released on and after 8D.25 KB5064081 but via an MSI needs documented in: WSD Wiki-Enabling KIR preview fixes - OSGWiki For questions NOT resolved by this KB including whether this issue was mitigated by 8D.25 KB5064081, please notify To: Herbert Mauerer <Herbert.Mauerer@microsoft.com>; Ryan Ries <Ryan.Ries@microsoft.com>; Telmo Terencio <Telmo.Terencio@microsoft.com>; Arren Conner <arrenc@microsoft.com> Subject: MSS Case <case #> is a match for KB5055152 ADDS: Windows 11 24H2: LSASS crash in Kerberos when attempting to access a file share due to corrupt list Include: Repro Steps Business impact details More information Related bugs OS Bug 57576500: [AB] Crash in Kerberos when attempting to access a cloud file share due to corrupt list OS Bug 56488103: [Ge] Crash in Kerberos when attempting to access a cloud file share due to corrupt list Related Cases 2503070040009352 2502200050004829 2501300040013852 2503050030003350 2503260050003356 2504110040007715 2503260050003356 2508040050002118 Notes: SR Number: 2501300040013852 First published: Feb 28, 2025 Keywords: repub-2025-05-29 Tags: underinvestigation

title: ConfigMgr: Client registration issue on servers.
content: ConfigMgr: Client registration issue on servers. Important: This was authored via https://aka.ms/contentidea. Follow Content Idea (CI) 200029 link for any updates. Author: Vivekanandan Lingan Summary/Symptom 01-28-2025 14:04:18.969 ClientIDManagerStartup 2732 (0xaac) RegTask: Failed to send registration request message. Error: 0x87d0023101-28-2025 14:04:18.969 CcmMessaging 2732 (0xaac) Failed in WinHttpReceiveResponse API, ErrorCode = 0x2f8f01-28-2025 14:04:18.969 CcmMessaging 2732 (0xaac) [CCMHTTP] ERROR: URL=https://abc.com/ccm_system_windowsauth/request, Port=443, Options=448, Code=12175, Text=ERROR_WINHTTP_SECURE_FAILURE01-28-2025 14:04:18.969 CcmMessaging 2732 (0xaac) [CCMHTTP] ERROR INFO: StatusCode=<unknown> StatusText=01-28-2025 14:04:18.969 CcmMessaging 2732 (0xaac) Successfully queued event on HTTP/HTTPS failure for server 'abc.com'.01-28-2025 14:04:18.969 CcmMessaging 2732 (0xaac) Post to https://abc.com/ccm_system_windowsauth/request failed with 0x87d00231. Cause ERROR_WINHTTP_SECURE_FAILURE: 12175 One or more errors were found in the Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) certificate sent by the server. Article resolution Open Registry --> Computer\HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\SCHANNEL\Protocols\TLS 1.2\Client Enabled to set to 0 Changed to 1. Initiated the client registration and the registration was successful. More information Enable TLS 1.2 on servers - Configuration Manager | Microsoft Learn Notes: Support Topics: Management Tools\Configuration Manager\Microsoft Configuration Manager (current branch - version 2309) (Preview), Management Tools\Configuration Manager\Microsoft Configuration Manager (current branch - version 2403) (Retired) First published: Mar 01, 2025 Keywords: "12175", "0x2f8f"

title: ConfigMgr: Machines are failing to scan using WSUS.
content: ConfigMgr: Machines are failing to scan using WSUS. Important: This was authored via https://aka.ms/contentidea. Follow Content Idea (CI) 200167 link for any updates. Author: Vivekanandan Lingan Summary/Symptom Machines are failing to scan using WSUS. Cause These settings are found in IIS Manager > Application Pools > choose WsusPool and then click the Advanced Settings link in the right-side pane of IIS manager. Queue Length was set to 25000. Error Code: 0x80244022 (2149859362) Error Name: WU_E_PT_HTTP_STATUS_SERVICE_UNAVAIL Error Source: Windows Update Agent Error Message: Same as HTTP status 503 - the service is temporarily overloaded. Article resolution These settings are found in IIS Manager > Application Pools > choose WsusPool and then click the Advanced Settings link in the right-side pane of IIS manager. Queue Length was set to 25000. Modified the Queue Length to 2000. Did IISreset. Notes: First published: Mar 05, 2025 Keywords: "0x80244022", "temporarily overloaded", "503"

title: Windows: OpenSSH: SYSLOG support for SIEM integration including CVE, JSON or XML formats in OpenSSH
content: Windows: OpenSSH: SYSLOG support for SIEM integration including CVE, JSON or XML formats in OpenSSH Important: This was authored via https://aka.ms/contentidea. Follow Content Idea (CI) 200223 link for any updates. Author: Arren Conner Summary Abstract Q. Is it possible for the OpenSSH syslog to support SIEM integration (Security information and event management) solutions by exporting the CFE , JSON or XML file formats?. Per https://github.com/PowerShell/Win32-OpenSSH/wiki/Logging-Facilities current as of March 7, 2025, logging to event viewer or a text file is currently supported.
